Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney could steal the Nobel Peace Prize from Donald Trump after the president spent the year complaining about not receiving the award.

Trump has repeatedly aired his grievance about the Norwegian Nobel Committee not offering the medal to him, claiming to have helped resolve several world conflicts. Now, with this year’s prize announcement less than two weeks away, one of the president’s political foes may receive the coveted award.

Carney had a 14 percent chance to take the Nobel Peace Prize on October 9, leading humanitarian organizations Doctors Without Borders and Sudan’s Emergency Response Rooms, sports betting information site Covers reported Monday morning, citing data from prediction market Kalshi.

The Canadian leader has pushed back against Trump amid an escalating trade war. Carney said the U.S. tried to restrict his country’s ability to make trade deals with other nations during talks last month, which he found to be “unacceptable” and “a question of sovereignty,” the Associated Press reported.

Carney got a standing ovation for a speech he gave in January at the World Economic Forum in Davos, Switzerland, in which he rebuked Trump’s threats to slap tariffs on imports from European allies until the U.S. reached a deal to acquire Greenland.

open image in gallery Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney could steal the Nobel Peace Prize from Donald Trump after the president spent the year complaining about not receiving the award ( Getty Images )

“Canada strongly opposes tariffs over Greenland and calls for focused talks to achieve our shared objectives of security and prosperity in the Arctic,” Carney said.

He also talked about the “rupture in the world order…where the large, main power, geopolitics, is submitted to no limits, no constraints.

“On the other hand, I would like to tell you that the other countries, especially intermediate powers like Canada, are not powerless. They have the capacity to build a new order that encompasses our values, such as respect for human rights, sustainable development, solidarity, sovereignty and territorial integrity of the various states,” Carney said.

open image in gallery Carney had a 14 percent chance of taking the award, leading humanitarian organizations Doctors Without Borders and Sudan’s Emergency Response Rooms, according to a Monday morning report, citing data from prediction market Kalshi ( AFP via Getty Images )

Carney’s chances of winning the Nobel Peace Prize dropped to 5 percent on Kalshi by Monday evening, falling behind Sudan’s Emergency Response Rooms and Doctors Without Borders. But he still led Trump, who had a 2 percent chance of winning the award on Kalshi.

Trump has exaggerated his accomplishments in world peace while starting a war with Iran, saying the Middle Eastern country posed an “imminent” threat to Americans because of its “nuclear ambitions.”

“I ended eight wars. Did I get the Nobel Prize? No,” Trump said from the Oval Office earlier this month. “Although the person that got it was nice enough that she gave it to me. She said, nobody in the history of the Nobel Prize deserves it more than you. But in Norway, they don't like me because I think they think I'm a little conservative."

Trump was referring to Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado, the 2025 Nobel Peace Prize winner who presented her medal to Trump in January after U.S. forces captured Venezuela’s then-President Nicolás Maduro.

Publicly viewable Pentagon data reveals that at least 19 American troops have died in the Iran war, and thousands more Iranians have been killed, according to reports.

open image in gallery Trump has exaggerated his accomplishments in world peace while starting a war with Iran, saying the Middle Eastern country posed an 'imminent' threat to Americans because of its 'nuclear ambitions' ( Getty Images )

During his speech at the United Nations General Assembly in New York last week, Trump threatened to annihilate Iran.

“I have a big decision to make — will a deal be made with Iran that lets them rebuild and create a far greater country than it ever was before…or do I annihilate the Islamic Republic and do it quickly, never giving them a chance to kill and destroy people and countries again?” Trump asked.

While Trump wages war with a Middle East adversary, he is also picking a fight with America’s northern ally. The president has pushed for Canada to become the 51st state and called Carney the “future governor of Canada.” He also signed an executive order last month to change the name of Lake Ontario to “Lake America.”

After trade talks failed, Trump imposed a 50 percent tariff on about $20 billion of Canadian imports last month, according to the AP. Canadian officials then announced “dollar-for-dollar” tariffs on American goods, including steel, electronics and dairy, that began earlier this month. Trump’s administration then banned some Canadian dairy products, motorcycles, and most alcoholic beverages, which Carney said were “relatively modest measures” compared to other U.S. actions, according to another AP report.

Carney has signaled that he will continue to work with Trump on other international issues, saying, “We continue to have to work with the United States. We can compartmentalize across this.”

News.title: UK borrowing costs hit highest level since 2007
News.content:
Britain’s borrowing costs hit their highest level since 2007 after Middle East tensions pushed oil prices above $108.

Yields on 10-year gilts, which determine the price the treasury pays to borrow money, rose above 5.43pc on Monday, before edging back to 5.42pc.

These are levels not seen in almost two decades, underlining the challenge facing John Healey as he prepares for next month’s Budget.

The Chancellor is coming under pressure to slash spending or raise taxes to bring Britain’s borrowing costs under control, against a backdrop of growing debt and rising inflation.

The surge in 10-year gilt yields pushes them above the 19-year high of 5.41pc recorded earlier this month, threatening to put a dent in Mr Healey’s fiscal headroom – a self-imposed guardrail to guide public spending.

Economists said high costs reflect the scale of Britain’s near-£3tn national debt and the rise in inflation facing the country.

“The uncomfortable truth for the PM and his Chancellor, John Healey ... is that the wide spread of gilt yields over peers is fair, in our view, given the UK’s dire fiscal position and the inflationary pressures stemming from high energy prices,” said Elliott Jordan-Doak, at Pantheon Macroeconomics.

“Gilt yields will fall if energy prices drop, but investors will continue to be driven by the economics and the Government’s willingness to take tough fiscal decisions, both of which point to yields staying high.”

UK borrowing costs are growing amid a wider bond market sell-off after Donald Trump rejected a peace deal with Iran over the weekend, pushing oil prices higher.

Brent crude, the international benchmark, rose by 3pc to just over $108 a barrel on Monday, adding to global inflation pressures. Bond traders reacted by demanding higher yields from governments to lend them money.

The yield on 10-year US Treasury bonds rose to above 5.24pc, the highest level since 2007.

Read the latest updates below.

News.title: Taylor Swift becomes most-awarded artist in MTV history
News.content:
Taylor Swift broke records at the 2026 MTV Video Music Awards (VMAs) on Sunday, becoming the most-awarded artist in VMA history.

The pop star, 36, was previously tied with Beyoncé for the title, with 30 VMAs each. However, Swift took home three awards at the ceremony, bringing her career total to an unmatched 33.

The Fate of Ophelia, ⁠Swift’s first single from her record-breaking The Life of a Showgirl album, claimed the top trophy – Video of the Year – and she dedicated the honour to the late country music legend Dolly Parton.

During her speech, Swift praised Parton as “the ultimate showgirl” who told stories that were “so vivid and so rich”.

“I think that we were all very lucky to share this planet with Dolly Parton for a time,” she said.

Parton, an award-winning country singer, died in August at the age of 80.

Swift also received the inaugural Artist Director Honors, a new award meant to recognise artists “whose work behind the camera has expanded the possibilities of music video and advanced the art of visual storytelling”.

The 36-year-old has written and directed 18 videos of her roughly 60 videos during her career. The ‌most recent, for ‌her new single Patient Zero, debuted during ⁠the ceremony.

News.title: Five reasons why Australia’s win over Boks was an all-time classic
News.content:
If the Wallabies play like this in their own backyard at their own World Cup next year, boy we are in for a treat. After years in the doldrums, this five-try victory over South Africa was the latest reminder of their transformation under the stewardship of Les Kiss.

Their gritty performance in Perth – the city where Australia will open rugby’s showpiece in 12 months’ time – was caveated by the fact they were facing a second-string Boks side. But there can be no denying they are on an upward trajectory, even if their discipline dramatically deserted them late on.

In a helter-skelter denouement, Australia played the majority of the final 10 minutes of the match with 11 men on the pitch as South Africa threatened to mount a late comeback. Tom Wright’s eye-catching intercept try looked to have secured a match-winning moment, but it was scratched off after Hunter Paisami joined Harry Wilson, Ryan Lonergan and Joseph Sua’ali’i in the bin.

Ox Nche’s 80th-minute score made it a four-point game with time left for the restart, but Australia had enough fight to secure a dramatic victory largely built on execution and patience.

Five tries by the hour mark, including a Len Ikitau first-half double, ultimately gave South Africa a mountain to climb. The Wallabies’ field coverage and industriousness in defence was far superior to that of the four-time world champions, while Max Jorgensen and Sua’ali’i were pillars of excellence out wide.

After clinching a 3-1 win over New Zealand in their historic “Greatest Rivalry” series, Rassie Erasmus had the luxury of resting several of his A-listers for this one-off Test in Western Australia. The changes ultimately had an adverse effect, with the visitors faulty at the set-piece and lacking their usual snarl and bite. They found themselves playing catch-up in a chaotic game that Australia, despite their discipline creaking in the dying moments, deserved to win.

Here, Telegraph Sport explores five reasons why this was one of the craziest Test matches in recent memory.

Wallabies outmuscle Boks over 60 emphatic minutes

The Wallabies front up impressively to earn a seven-point lead at the break after a quickfire Len Ikitau double cancels out tries from Johan Grobbelaar and Edwill van der Merwe, before Ben Donaldson finishes a sublime attacking set from the hosts.

News.title: England show ODI depth in thrashing of Sri Lanka
News.content:
England’s international summer comes to an end at the Oval with a series decider against Sri Lanka. After England won the first game in Durham, Sri Lanka bounced back to take a 16-run win at Headingley on Thursday to set up this winner-takes-all match today. Sri Lanka put up a much better fight in the second one-day international than they have throughout the rest of their white-ball tour. The tourists posted 321 for six, with their captain Kusal Mendis leading the way with 121 off 100 balls, his seventh ODI century.

England’s reply got off to the best possible start, with both openers Tom Banton and Ben Duckett hitting fifties. It appeared to be going well for England, with Jos Buttler and Will Jacks also registering half centuries, but Buttler’s hamstring injury in addition to the regular loss of wickets meant Sri Lanka were able to claim victory to take us to a series decider in London today.

“I am so happy winning and getting the hundred,” Mendis said. “The overall performance was very good. We started really well and the middle order batted really well. Nothing special, basic cricket and I was very happy with 320, we wanted more than 300 on this pitch. [Dunith] Wellalage bowled really well, the whole team, after the powerplay. The guys gave 100 per cent. Today [Thursday] is finished and now we have to focus on the next game and do the basics right.”

When Buttler retired hurt in the 38th over of England’s run chase, the hosts were 254 for four and were in a great position to chase the total down and claim a series victory. From the 37th over onwards, England were only able to score one four and one six.

“It was an outstanding game,” England captain Harry Brook said. “You can look back and dwell on some many different areas but that is not what this team does, we go back to the drawing board and get ready for the Oval. We put up a really good fight with the ball. To restrict them to 320 and have the chance to chase that down was a hell of an effort.

“The lads got the chase off to a flyer. You could not really ask for much more. We probably stalled in that middle period and lost a few too many wickets, but the fight we showed was great. We have got a great opportunity now to try and win this series, and a great opportunity for 12 months’ time. In pressure situations, like the one that awaits us at the Oval, it will be great to see where we are as a team.”

Buttler has been ruled out of this match due to a hamstring injury and has been replaced in the squad by Dan Lawrence, who had been playing for Surrey in the final round of the County Championship.

Play from the Oval will get under way at 10.30am.

News.title: Saracens storm Leicester to launch new Venter era in style
News.content:
Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of this mouthwatering Gallagher Prem meeting as Leicester Tigers host Saracens at Welford Road.

Last season, Leicester reached the play-off semi-finals in Geoff Parling’s first full season at the club, before losing to arch-rivals Northampton Saints, who went on to win their third title in the competition.

In a new era for Leicester as they plot a route back to the very top, Aaron Wainwright and Mako Vunipola make their Prem debuts.

Leicester head coach Geoff Parling is brimming with excitement ahead of this tasty match and has talked about his side’s preparation for the new season.

“Firstly we are looking to evolve our game, we’re not looking to rip it up and completely restart,” he said. This team is built on being competitive and winning, we’ve got to be in the mix every year. For me it’s all about being consistently near the top and then getting in those big games and having the ability to perform in them.”

“I’m well aware that there’s lots of elements from the season and different circumstances but the main thing is that the league is designed to have a top four that go into the play-offs so the top four is the aim.”

Saracens finished one place below Leicester in the previous campaign and missed out on the play-offs after a 32-12 final round loss to Exeter Chiefs.

Boss Joe Shaw has handed debuts to Tomos Williams and Alfie Barbeary, and he’s raring to go ahead of this fixture.

“We’ve had a great pre-season, but we’re itching to get stuck into the league campaign now,” he said. “We have a really competitive squad who are driving standards and good habits across the pitch. We are confident in the squad we have put together and are excited to see what they can achieve this campaign.”

Kick-off is at 15:00.

News.title: England throw it away with defending unworthy of a top nation
News.content:
Tuchel does not plan to address the issue with his players ahead of the remaining Nations League games against Czech Republic and Croatia.

Asked if the City verdict had been a cause of discussion ahead of the Spain game, Tuchel replied: “Not for me, but I can imagine maybe for the Man City players. I won’t comment on it as it’s an ongoing case.

“I didn’t make it a topic. It was not a topic for me. I’m just thinking about Spain and the team and meetings. The players have more time than me. So I can imagine they talk about it. It’s good they do. I don’t think it was a distraction for them.”

Kane added: “There was a discussion, but when we’re with England, we kind of put club football to one side and it was no different this week.”

Tuchel also refused to point the finger of blame at Guéhi, O’Reilly or Kane, who missed a penalty, for England’s defeat despite admitting his team got off to the worst possible start by conceding a goal after two minutes.

“We will focus on the positives, but also highlight the stuff we can do better,” Tuchel said. “Not even speaking about individual mistakes because this is normal. It just happens. It should not happen, and for sure not in this amount. But there is no sense in showing the individual mistakes or telling them ‘please don’t make mistakes’. That is normal, but we can do things better. We can defend the third goal better. But we will focus on the positives. There is a lot to take away from the game.

“We wanted to be the team desperately to beat them [Spain] and we think we had them. We still think we had them at half-time. That was the way the team showed up after half-time. So we will focus on that, but the reality is we lost and the reality is we need to prove it again.”

News.title: Red Roses triumph over New Zealand in chaotic late scenes – how it unfolded
News.content:
Just when it looked like the Red Roses’ lustre was beginning to fade, up stepped Zoe Harrison.

In one of the most dramatic finishes to an England match in recent memory, the fly-half gobbled up Amy Du Plessis’s pass to glide over the whitewash and secure a pulsating win over New Zealand.

Ever the epitome of calmness, Harrison was undeterred by the fact she had just missed what would have been a match-winning penalty from 42 metres out with the score locked at 19-19.

But after their arm-wrestle with Canada last weekend in Exeter, which finished 26-26, there was simply no way the Red Roses were going to settle for a draw for a second week running.

A year to the day since they were crowned world champions in their own back yard, England’s status as the most dominant side in the women’s game was all but confirmed by this never-say-die victory over the Black Ferns.

News.title: Russell holds his nerve to see off Verstappen and win Azerbaijan GP
News.content:
The Azerbaijan Grand Prix weekend went the way many believed the 2026 season would play out. George Russell strolled to victory from pole, though with a little late jeopardy, whilst Kimi Antonelli’s crash in qualifying meant he had to fight his way through the field to finish fifth. That, after all, was the order of things last season.

Yet the past few days in Baku are an inversion of the season’s storyline. It is Antonelli who has been the faster driver, heading for a maiden world title at the second time of asking. Russell has been the troubled one. This was only the Briton’s third victory of the season and his first since Austria in late June. Antonelli has racked up eight wins and, before this weekend in Baku, a well-deserved 81-point lead over Russell.

Russell’s dominant and impressive run from pole to the chequered flag on Saturday is both a reminder of what he is capable of and also what might have been, had he been able to find this type of form earlier and more often. The reality, though, is that he needs to replicate this for the rest of the season to even be in with a sniff, barring a catastrophic meltdown from Antonelli. Still, Russell looked elated to have ended his barren run.

The finish was a little more tense than Russell deserved, having established a healthy lead in the first half of the race. Two late safety cars eradicated his advantage and helped put Max Verstappen’s Red Bull on his gearbox. In the end, he triumphed by just under 0.2sec and, as Antonelli finished fifth – with some help from two safety-car inducing crashes – he made up 15 points on his Mercedes team-mate. Isack Hadjar completed the podium for Red Bull after missing the past three races with a wrist injury.

Sports.title: Man City in huge trouble after guilty verdict but spare thought for innocent fans & signings who face uncertain future
Sports.content:
Next

WE now know that there was a giant elephant in the Manchester City dressing room.

A gigantic pile of the stuff all the way up to the ceiling.



Leaving behind a stench that may never dissipate and certainly not for long after the shovels have been put to use.

If the findings of the independent commission — who spent two years weighing up evidence from both the Premier League and City — are as damning as expected, the guilty will pay a heavy price.



Not just in terms of City’s status because wholesale breaches of financial regulations — if confirmed — will surely bring a punishment that adds up to relegation.

Pending compensation claims adding up to hundreds of millions will further damage even City’s UAE owners, who will be viewed by many as complicit, if not the orchestrators of the entire approach.

But so, too, will the innocent suffer.

The fans, most of whom took the club’s protestations of outrage over the allegations levelled against them at face value.

While there are still some who want to believe this is all a plot by the dastardly “Red Cartel”, most recognise a different scenario now.

Yet none of those supporters sent the emails, wrote the contracts, signed off the accounts.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

And nor did the players — left stunned and shocked by the news that had international dressing rooms across Europe and beyond chuntering over the weekend.

You have to assume they, or their agents, would have asked about the progress of the Prem’s case.

But nobody could possibly have known it was proceeding, even at a seemingly glacial pace.

Equally, players were surely also given assurances from the highest echelons of the club that there was nothing to worry about.

No need for relegation clauses.



Would Marc Guehi, Antoine Semenyo, Elliot Anderson — to name just three — have joined City if they were given even the tiniest of hints they might be playing in the Championship by August 2027?

Whatever happens now, however long it takes, everything about City has changed.

Those titles, those managers, those players.

What were Man City charged with? MAN CITY have been found guilty of all but one of the 115 charges they were initially hit with. Those charges were upped to 130 and fit into the following six categories… Failing to give accurate financial information over sponsorship revenue, related parties and operating costs between 2009-10 and 2017/18. Total charges: 50

Failing to provide full details of managerial remuneration between 2009/10 and 2012/13. Total charges 8

Failing to provide full details of player remuneration between 2010/11 and 2015/16. Total charges 12

Failing to comply with Uefa Licencing and Financial Fair Play regulations between 2013/14 and 2017/18. Total charges 5

Breaching Premier League Profitability and Sustainability rules between 2015/16 and 2017/18. Total charges 25

Failing to co-operate with the Premier League investigation between 2018/19 and 2022/23. Total charges 30

Total charges: 130

All compromised, undercut and permanently questioned.



Half a century ago, Brian Clough turned his first meeting with his new Leeds players into a warzone.

Old Big ’Ead stared Norman Hunter, Johnny Giles, Billy Bremner and Co in the face.

And Clough said: “You lot may all be internationals and have won all the domestic honours there are to win under Don Revie.

“But, as far as I’m concerned, the first thing you can do for me is chuck all your medals and all your caps and all your pots and all your pans into the biggest f***ing dustbin you can find.

“Because you’ve never won any of them fairly. You’ve done it all by cheating.”



Enzo Maresca has joined the Etihad giants three times since the Prem probe began.

And he will clearly not say anything of the sort to his squad when they return — presumably still in a state of shock — following this international break.

He does not have to.

Every rival fanbase, starting at Anfield on Sunday week, will do it for him.

A ceaseless, unrelenting barrage of abuse, placards, jeers and chants.



Sympathy, too, will be in short supply.

City may have won trophies with a swagger and delivered some remarkable, unforgettable teams and moments.

Yet long-standing suspicions over the mechanisms that led to that dominance have now, seemingly, been justified.

It also becomes clear just why City were so, so desperate to bring down Richard Masters and the Prem executive team, going out of their way to block and hinder the investigation.

The Wizard of Oz was all powerful until someone finally peeked behind the curtain.



Masters and Co wanted to pull it back with a mighty yank — exposing the whole shebang to the disinfectant of sunlight.

All we have seen, so far, is the shadows behind the scenes.

Not the evidence, the findings, the scale of the reported deceit that the probe appears to have found over many years.

For the good of football, the rest of it must be put in the full public spotlight quickly.

Everybody has waited far too long.



When it started, that elephant was a calf. Now it’s a fully-grown adult.

UTD LOOK RAT-TLED

SIR JIM RATCLIFFE has never been scared of hacking people off.

Even if it means his own sporting hero, Manchester United icon Eric Cantona, thinks he is a villain.

Like the proverbial scorpion, stinging the frog carrying him across the river, it’s in his nature.

The kid from Failsworth who turned himself into Britain’s richest man at one point, the head of a global conglomerate.



Billionaire Sir Jim, 73, has always adopted a ‘take no prisoners’ stance when it comes to business.

So it shouldn’t have been a shock that Ratcliffe and Ineos brought that attitude to their stewardship of United after buying a stake in February 2024.

Now, the reality is beginning to strike.



Fans have been on the verge of mutiny since the Glazers’ takeover in 2005.

If the white knight proves no better than the American dragons, their fury will be incandescent.

LEVY WITH LAST LAUGH

AN hour into the Premier League shareholders meeting — and a familiar face walked through the doors of the same central London hotel last week.

Whether Daniel Levy, former executive chairman of Tottenham, initially realised he was 20 yards from the room where it happens was unclear.

Although he gave a slightly nervous smile towards the small gaggle of journalists in the lobby.



But as one of the men who pushed Prem chiefs hardest to investigate Manchester City – and who lodged Spurs’ claim to push for compensation and damages if the chance arose – that smile might have been wider 24 hours later.

BEER WE GO

ANDY BURNHAM’S plan to lift the booze ban for people watching football matches brought plenty of reaction from both sides of the argument.

My Sun colleague Pete Nuttall argued he really didn’t want to be showered with beer from joyful Seagulls fans every time his Brighton side score.



Fair enough.

But every Spurs fan will tell you the Prime Minister’s proposal is not an issue if you’re going to stay bone dry all season.

FINAL THOUGHTS

AT LEAST one part of the World Cup “what if” has now been settled.

Fans had pondered how events might have played out in July’s Metlife final had England not lost to Argentina.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The answer now seems clear: a football match, not a Fight Club.



Fun to watch. And Spain winning… comfortably.

ENGLAND manager Thomas Tuchel warned the Three Lions’ leaky defence they are a “danger” to themselves.

Sports.title: Football’s biggest scandals including Juventus match-fixing and £113m Fifa corruption case after Man City bombshell
Sports.content:
Next

MANCHESTER CITY are just the latest big-name club to join football’s roll of shame.

Scandals, financial and otherwise, have been part of the game since it became an organised sport and have driven other sides to the brink – or even to extinction.



Etihad chiefs are probably unaware of what happened to Leeds City just after WWI.

But they should be all too familiar with the humiliation of Juventus and the demise of Glasgow Rangers in the modern era.



All three clubs were punished severely after investigations or whistleblowers lifted the lid on systematic rule-breaking.

Yet in each case, there was a comeback and a return to glory which could offer some hope to shattered City fans.



LEEDS CITY 1919

As if to prove there is nothing new under the sun, the Leeds City scandal of 107 years ago is in many ways the most similar to Manchester City’s.

Secret payments, leaked documents, a refusal to cooperate with the authorities – it was all there.

So was manager Herbert Chapman, who went on to become the Pep Guardiola of his era of English football.

But only after a lifetime ban for his part in the scandal was lifted.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Leeds City, formed in 1904, were showing signs of emerging from on and off-field problems when boss Chapman left in 1914 to take over a local munitions factory to help the war effort.

By the time he returned in 1918, the club was being torn apart by rows between his unpopular right-hand man George Cripps and chairman Joseph Connor.

Cripps, annoyed at being demoted back to assistant, threatened to tell the football authorities about illegal payments made to guest players during the war years – including England internationals Charlie Buchan and Fanny Walden.

His solicitor James Bromley did a deal with the club early in 1919 for Cripps to accept a pay-off in return for a promise to keep quiet.

But the truth was not hidden for long.



When journeyman full-back Charlie Copeland rowed with the club over the terms of the new contract he was offered for the 1919/20 season, he was literally sent to Coventry.

But Copeland, with Bromley as his solicitor, told the authorities about the illegal payments – prompting claims from Connor the lawyer had leaked information from the Cripps settlement to the player.

The Football League demanded Leeds submit the relevant documents by October 6.

When the club failed to do so, it was expelled from Division Two. Leeds’ place – and its playing record for the season so far – was given to Burslem Port Vale.



Five City officials, including Connor and Chapman, were banned from the game for life.

The Leeds squad was auctioned off at the Metropole Hotel for a total of £10,000 and the Elland Road ground sold to Yorkshire Amateurs.

But then a ray of light. Elland Road was bought by a new club, Leeds United, and Huddersfield Town chairman Hilton Crowther loaned it £35,000 in early 1920, with United soon elected into Division Two.

Meanwhile, Chapman’s ban was lifted and he joined Huddersfield, whom he led to two titles and an FA Cup, before joining Arsenal.



Chapman was caught up in controversy again when it emerged the Gunners had made secret payments to Buchan – previously part of the Leeds scandal – to persuade him to join the club.

But Chapman escaped punishment and the tactical innovator turned Arsenal into the leading side of the early 1930s.

JUVENTUS

The story of the humbling of one of world football’s great names reads like a Mafia novel.

Calciopoli – literally “Footballville”, in an echo of the name given to political corruption scandals of the early 1990s – brought down not only Juventus, but also AC Milan and a number of other clubs in the latest episode in the Italian game’s chequered history.



The authorities were already investigating Juve over allegations of systematic doping.

But their tapping of conversations between the club’s general manager, Luciano Moggi, CEO Antonio Giraudo, executives at other Serie A teams and other football officials, uncovered something which was arguably more shocking.

Moggi, with the help of his counterparts, had allegedly conspired to try to influence referees across the 2004/05 and 2005/06 seasons – both of which had ended with Juventus as champions.

It was alleged officials favourable to Juve were appointed to their matches, and they and others were pressurised to make decisions that benefited the club during games.



That included giving out yellow or red cards to influential players from other teams which would rule them out of future matches against Juve.

Magistrates in Naples investigated 41 individuals, including nine referees, and 19 matches from 2004/05, plus 14 more from the following campaign.

The scandal broke in May 2006 and was seismic even by the standards of Italian football.

Senior federation official Franco Carraro was the first to resign, followed by the entire Juve board, Moggi, Giraudo and head coach Fabio Capello.

Juve were stripped of their 2004/05 and 2005/06 titles – the latter awarded to Inter Milan – and relegated to Serie B, with an additional penalty of a nine-point deduction.



Star players including Zlatan Ibrahimovic, Patrick Vieira, Emerson and Fabio Cannavaro all left the club.

AC Milan, Fiorentina, Lazio and Reggina escaped relegation but were deducted eight, 15, three and one point respectively for the 2006/07 Serie A season.

Meanwhile a process was beginning that would lead to NINE years of sporting, civil and criminal proceedings against individuals involved.

Yet Italian football had a triumphant summer, as Marcello Lippi guided the nation to its fourth World Cup triumph.

And members of Moggi’s squad then set about helping Juve return to the top, too.



Gianluigi Buffon, Alessandro del Piero and Mauro Camoranesi did not leave the Old Lady despite relegation.

Capello’s replacement, former Juve star Didier Deschamps, guided the club to the Serie B title as they defied the points deduction to finish six clear of second-placed Napoli.

Back in the top flight, from 2011/12 Juve won an unprecedented NINE Serie A titles in a row under Antonio Conte and Massimiliano Allegri and Calciopoli became just a blip in their history.

GLASGOW RANGERS

The collapse of Rangers is arguably the biggest, most damaging scandal to hit any famous club before Manchester City.

And it is not just Celtic fans who believe the institution founded in 1872, and so one of the oldest football teams in the world, actually ceased to exist in 2012 when it went bust owing millions to the taxman.



At the turn of the millennium, as Scottish football began to fall further behind England and much of Europe in terms of income, it was becoming harder for clubs like Rangers to compete.

So in order to attract star players like Ronald de Boer and Tore Andre Flo to Glasgow, they had to find creative ways of matching the money on offer elsewhere.

The scheme Rangers came up with involved the club, and the parent company controlled by then chairman Sir David Murray, paying cash into Employee Benefit Trusts (EBTs) on top of regular salaries.

Current Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta was also among the 67 players, 24 club staff and 24 other Murray Group employees to receive a total of more than £47m from EBTs between 2001 and 2010.

Rangers said the payments, kept secret from the football authorities, were loans.



But HMRC regarded them as earnings, and therefore subject to income tax and national insurance contributions.

With penalties and interest, it left the club facing a £49m bill.

Murray sold cash-strapped Rangers to Craig Whyte in May 2011 for £1. Only for it to emerge Whyte had once been banned from being a company director for seven years and should not have been allowed to purchase the club.



By February 2012 Rangers were forced to call in the administrators, incurring an immediate 10–point penalty.

Then HMRC played hardball, refusing to allow the club to exit administration through Company Voluntary Arrangement, which would have involved them and other creditors receiving only a fraction of what they were owed.

So Rangers Football Club was forced into liquidation.

After most of the players tore up their contracts in accordance with football regulations, the remaining assets were eventually sold to a company named Sevco Scotland Ltd.

To this day, Celtic fans and others call the team from the blue half of Glasgow “Sevco”.



A long legal process began which ended in 2017 with the Supreme Court backing HMRC’s position that the EBT payments should be treated as earnings.

Meanwhile Rangers were in meltdown on the pitch, too.

The “new” club was sent all the way down to the Third Division but controversially allowed to retain the three titles and eight domestic cups won between 2001 and 2010.

Rangers worked their way back to the top flight in time for the 2016/17 season and under Steven Gerrard won the 2020/21 title, preventing Celtic from establishing a new record of 10 in a row.

But Rangers still bear the scars and Scottish football is still stained by the bad blood from the embarrassing saga.



2015 FIFA CORRUPTION SCANDAL

In May 2015 the US Department of Justice disclosed a 47-count, 164-page criminal indictment charging seven FIFA executives with having received $150million (£113m) in bribes over more than two decades.

Those execs were arrested by Swiss police in Zurich, where FIFA is based.

Seven more officials and sports marketing individuals were later included in the DOJ indictment for offenses dating back to 1991.



It was alleged that they had received bribes from marketing groups in exchange for television contracts.

The charges included racketeering, wire fraud, and money laundering

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Swiss proceedings also opened probes into the awarding of the 2018 and 2022 World Cups to Russia and Qatar.

Ex-FIFA president Sepp Blatter was later forced to resign.

Sports.title: Rio Ferdinand takes firm stance over Man Utd and JJ Gabriel - 'Can't be bullied by a young kid!'
Sports.content:
Rio Ferdinand takes firm stance over Man Utd and JJ Gabriel - 'Can't be bullied by a young kid!'

JJ Gabriel has informed Manchester United that he wants to leave, with several European giants keen to sign him, and Rio Ferdinand has given his old club some advice

View 2 Images Rio Ferdinand has a clear message for his old club (Image: Rio Ferdinand Presents)

Rio Ferdinand has told Manchester United not to be "bullied" by JJ Gabriel after he asked to be released by the club.

‌



The 15-year-old star's future at United has been the subject of intense speculation recently after it emerged that he was unhappy. Gabriel is yet to make his first-team debut for United and has grown frustrated by the lack of opportunities, despite his age.

‌



He is not happy to just be starring for United's under-21s and his family believe Gabriel's development would be better served elsewhere. Gabriel has been courted by Barcelona, Real Madrid, Bayern Munich and Paris Saint-Germain, while United's Premier League rivals are also interested, if his exit can be arranged.

‌



Ferdinand visited United's squad during their pre-season in Ireland and was hugely impressed by Gabriel's ability. But the former United defender has urged his old club not to bend over backwards because it would set a dangerous precedent.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



"I just feel that Man United can't be seen to be bullied by a young kid who is 15 years old, no matter how good he is," Ferdinand said on his YouTube channel.

"So whatever the outcome is, Man United have to remain strong in this until the end because whatever the decision or whatever way this plays out, there will be kids coming after this who will be using it as a reference point and you can't be seen to be weak in this situation as a football club.

"But I'm not going to sit here and hammer on the kid or pick apart what's going on because I don't have the facts around how they've got to this situation, this end point, that JJ Gabriel and his family are demanding to leave."

‌



View 2 Images JJ Gabriel wants out of Manchester United (Image: Manchester United/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Two of Ferdinand's children, Lorenz and Tate, are pursuing professional careers in the Brighton academy and he was asked if he sympathised with Gabriel's family.

"As a parent I'm the same," he admitted. "I want to know what you think of my son and how you see him and how long it will take. But I know that nothing is guaranteed in this game because there are too many things that can alter your path, be it injuries, form, timing and confidence etc."

Article continues below

Gabriel turns 16 on October 6 and can then be legally represented by an agent. But currently, he would only be allowed to find a new club at the end of the season, unless United agree to deregister him.

It's a messy situation, but one thing isn't in doubt for Ferdinand. "What a talent this kid is," he said. "It’s crazy. I don’t know where this kid’s ceiling is. I’ve seen him play, I’ve seen him train, I’ve listened to people who have coached him for a number of years and there’s no doubt this kid is going to the top."

Sports.title: Joe Hart opens up on Man City guilty verdict with clear message - 'I know what we did'
Sports.content:
Joe Hart opens up on Man City guilty verdict with clear message - 'I know what we did'

Manchester City players have rarely spoken about the Manchester City charges verdict since reports emerged on Friday, with Joe Hart now becoming one of the first

View 2 Images Joe Hart has spoken out about Manchester City's guilty verdict (Image: BBC)

Joe Hart does not think that Manchester City will be found guilty of their Premier League charges because of how much their former goalkeeper trusts chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak. In response to Friday's reporting, the Abu Dhabi Executive Council member insisted: "Our confidence and intent in proving the club's innocence is just as strong as when this began."

‌



Hart, 39, played a part in City's first two Premier League-winning teams. He played 348 times in 12 years at the club.

‌



Barely any former City players have reacted publicly to the reports. Hart became one of the first, but spoke very carefully.

‌



Erling Haaland gives manager what he wants after Man City 115 charges verdict made public READ MORE :

Why Premier League have not made a statement on Man City 114 charges bombshell READ MORE :

Speaking on BBC Radio 5 Live during The Monday Night Club, he said: "I've heard everyone else go down every single rabbit hole, every single wormhole, every single discussion. My honest opinion is I've got no reason not to trust Khaldoon [Al Mubarak]. What he said is enough for me.

"I loved how he spoke. I loved the letter because that was from someone who cared about the club."

Al Mubarak said in part: "The Premier League process still has a long way to run, and our confidence and intent in proving the Club's innocence is just as strong as when this began."

‌



"There are so many things that I would like to be able to share with you to help you understand why we feel so confident in our position.

View 2 Images Khaldoon Al Mubarak wrote an open letter to Manchester City supporters over the weekend (Image: Getty)

FOLLOW OUR MAN CITY FB PAGE! Follow our Manchester City Mirror Football Facebook page

‌



"But the strict confidentiality of the legal process and our determination to respect it mean I cannot do that at the moment. Even this letter underwent several legal checks to make sure it complies."

Hart continued on the radio programme: "If Man City are found guilty, which I don't think they are because of what Khaldoon said, then there are conversations to be had, but right now I'm very confident and very, very calm.

"I'm very proud of what I've achieved and what I did with Manchester City and what we achieved as a team. And that doesn't change, that doesn't change until you tell me."

‌



The player-turned-pundit later concluded by saying matter-of-factly: "I did what I did. I lined up 11 v 11 and had it out on the pitch. I won some games, lost some games, drew some games, and I shook hands, and I walked off.

"I know what I did, I know what we did, and I know how it happened. It didn't feel like we were scheming or plotting."

Sports.title: Thomas Tuchel backs England to overcome defensive frailties as he drops selection hint
Sports.content:
Thomas Tuchel backs England to overcome defensive frailties as he drops selection hint

Thomas Tuchel's side face Czech Republic in Prague on Tuesday night looking to re-establish their rock solid defence following a night of mishaps in the defeat by Spain

View 4 Images Thomas Tuchel has backed his error-prone defence to turn it around (Image: Justin Setterfield/Getty Images)

Thomas Tuchel admits England have become a “danger to themselves” when it comes to defending.

‌



Tuchel oversaw a perfect World Cup qualifying campaign as they were water tight at the back and did not concede a single goal. But the three goals conceded against Spain at Wembley means they have now shipped 13 goals in their last six games.

‌



They have kept just four clean sheets in 13 games in 2026 and, tellingly, in each of the last five times they have conceded three or more goals Jordan Pickford has not been in goal.

‌



That run dates back to Aaron Ramsdale, Dean Henderson (twice), Nick Pope and now James Trafford, who obviously shipped three goals against Spain at Wembley on Saturday. Leeds keeper Trafford will be between the posts again in Prague against the Czech Republic as he continues his job share with Pickford.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



But Tuchel made it crystal clear that England’s defending is actually trying to cut out individual errors as on Saturday it was Marc Guehi and Nico O’Reilly who were guilty of uncharacteristic mistakes. England boss Tuchel said: “We suffered clearly from individual mistakes when we had the ball, especially in the deep build-up.

“Of course, that is something we cannot repeat, especially not at this kind of level. We have to take care about this. We have to be technically absolutely clinical also under pressure.

“We need to improve these things but strangely enough, when we had the ball we were the biggest danger to ourselves around the box because we just had too many individual mistakes. Purely in defending, I have no concerns and trust that we can do it.

‌



“I don't see a pattern. It was individual mistakes. I didn't see a pattern in defending. I think we defended very well in a block when we were organised, but we had just big individual mistakes. But I could not see any defensive pattern that would concern me.”

View 4 Images James Trafford will keep his place in goal (Image: Carl Recine/Getty Images)

Maybe it is not the time to make too many changes - and Tuchel made it clear he will back his defenders - and bringing in Trent Alexander-Arnold would seem like something of a risk because of his attacking instincts.

‌



Tuchel was not giving anything away on that front, but says he is relishing to see the keeper job share and also said that Alexander-Arnold is proving his desire to play for England.

Tuchel said: “We use the Nations League to see where we are with the other goalkeepers. It is in this camp it’s Traff and Pickers and we absolutely know what he gives us and how he performs under pressure. He did nothing wrong.

“There was no reason from performances to open up this position for competition. I think it's necessary with every other player that we are aware of ‘what if’.

‌



View 4 Images Marc Guehi's mistake allowed Lamine Yamal to make it 1-0 to Spain (Image: Carl Recine/Getty Images)

“If a player that starts a season well, like Traff at Leeds, has the chance to prove it and to play in our style and to do the build-up and patterns and defensive patterns in the way we want to do it. We just need to see it at some point.

“I will not tell you about other changes. We wait and then we see. But I will not change now because someone made an individual mistake, and they've been good for us through all the other matches.

‌



“Trent has been good, he had a very good training week and the excellent training in Wembley after the match, where he showed that he absolutely wants to play and wants to be with us. We're good. Today was a good training session. Everything is fine. He's ready to go.”

View 4 Images Czech Republic beat England 2-1 in October 2019 (Image: Denis Doyle/UEFA via Getty Images)

Back in 2019, England lost to the Czech Republic in Prague and that ended their 43-game unbeaten run in qualifying. That must serve as a warning to this England team as they try to finish in the top two to qualify to progress in the Nations League.

‌



Even Jurgen Klopp is finding international management tougher than it looked after Germany lost to Greece and that is a feeling that Tuchel is familiar with.

Tuchel added: “Everyone told me. Everyone told me that it is tough to form a team and everyone comes with different ideas and the focus was to bring them together, play properly as a team and implement patterns of play and we are a step further.

“We had a tournament together, we had this experience together. We digested it. We had a result that some think was not enough, some think it was a good result, whatever we had a result and we continue and this helps us. It is a process. So, it is another proof that to do it in international football you do it in four or five days what you do in four or five weeks at a club.”

Sports.title: Lewis Hall using World Cup snub as fuel to win England boss Thomas Tuchel over
Sports.content:
Lewis Hall using World Cup snub as fuel to win England boss Thomas Tuchel over

Lewis Hall is out to leave a lasting impression on England boss Thomas Tuchel during the international break after failing to make the cut for the World Cup in the summer

View 2 Images Lewis Hall (Image: Justin Setterfield)

Lewis Hall says he is using the pain of World Cup rejection as fuel this season.

‌



The Newcastle left-back has started the campaign in great form for his club and that earned him an instant recall from Thomas Tuchel after he missed out in the summer.

‌



Hall has signed a new deal at Newcastle, looks in great shape and wants to make the England left-back slot his own. When asked whether the World Cup heartbreak as fuel, Hall said: “Yeah, I think it's important to use that. Obviously, you don't want to get too worked up on it and too down about it, because that can also come across quite negative.

‌



“So, I'm using that frustration and I think anyone who was not in the squad is going to be disappointed. I think everyone will be doing the same to try and get themselves back on the squad.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



“Whenever you're in the squad, ultimately you've got the shirt, you've got to do what you can to keep it. When you're not in the squad, you've got to do what you can to try and take it off other people.

“I think that's what everyone describes as healthy competition, and that's important to pushing the team forward and the nation forward. I think that gets the best out of players. I think I'm in the squad now, and it's my job to make sure I stay in the squad.

“I think that's what football is about. It's all about your chances. I think in order to get where you want to be, you're going to get chances to impress, and as long as you take these chances, I think you can create whatever you want to create, really. So, yeah, I'm in the squad now, which I'm really grateful for. When I do get an opportunity, I'm hoping that I can take it.”

‌



Hall looks set to get it against Czech Republic as Nico O’Reilly is an injury doubt and he is determined to impress Tuchel, who gave him his debut at Chelsea.

Remarkably, Hall even said he had sympathy for Tuchel when he called him to say he was not in the squad. He did not want to even discuss that phone call. But despite missing out, Hall said he watched all the games at the World Cup.

View 2 Images Hall has enjoyed a fine start to the season with Newcastle (Image: Newcastle United via Getty Images)

‌



He added: “I think for me, it's important that we keep that relationship just between me and him with what he said and what we discussed. But he knew that I was going be disappointed, and it wasn't only me, he would have spoken to a lot of people in the summer who would have been disappointed.

“And as much as it's not a nice phone call for me to receive, I know it's obviously tough for him, because he knows that it's a dream for everyone to play in a World Cup. So I'm not going to discuss what we said.”

Hall was born on September 8, 2004, which was the day of an England game when they won in Poland. Maybe that is a good omen.

Article continues below

He added: “I did not know that. I was born in the afternoon, I think, four o'clock in the afternoon. Just before kick-off. Maybe I was a lucky charm.”

Sports.title: Man City chief declares Premier League charges battle far from over in bombshell statement
Sports.content:
Man City chief declares Premier League charges battle far from over in bombshell statement

Manchester City's CEO has addressed the recent reports claiming that the former Premier League champions have been found guilty of almost all the 115 charges brought against them

View 2 Images Ferran Soriano (R) and Manchester City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak (Image: Getty Images)

Ferran Soriano, the Manchester City chief executive officer, is said to have stressed that the club's fight with the Premier League over the 115 charges brought against them is far from over during a European Football Clubs board meeting.

‌



Football was rocked last week by reports that City had been found guilty of all but one of the charges against them, though the former Premier League champions are expected to appeal the verdict. Formal confirmation has yet to arrive but City's chairman, Khaldoon Al Mubarak, released a statement over the weekend reiterating that the club were confident of clearing their name.

‌



And Soriano, speaking at a meeting which was also attended by senior figures from other Premier League clubs, adopted a similar stance of defiance during an impromptu address on Monday.

‌



Per The Athletic, Soriano wanted to address the reports and made it clear that the club would continue to fight against the charges.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



“It has taken eight years to reach this point and it will still take much more time,” he is understood to have said.

Soriano declined to comment further when he was asked to do so by reporters in Copenhagen after the meeting.

His comments echo similar sentiments to that of Al Mubarak, who released a statement over the weekend in the wake of the reports which claimed City have “irrefutable evidence” to help fight their case.

‌



“I have been part of this Club for 18 years. I have had the privilege to stand with you in the Etihad, at Wembley, and in Istanbul,” City's chairman wrote in a message which also referenced previous statements made by the club.

View 2 Images Manchester City could be handed a significant point deduction

“This Club matters to me, and you have shown and told me – time and time again - how much Manchester City matters to you. This is why I am writing to you today. Following Friday’s media reporting, many of you will have spent your evening answering questions and responding to messages from friends, family and colleagues. So have I.

‌



“Here’s what I said to my family: The Premier League process still has a long way to run, and our confidence and intent in proving the Club’s innocence is just as strong as when this began. There are so many things that I would like to be able to share with you to help you understand why we feel so confident in our position.

“But the strict confidentiality of the legal process and our determination to respect it means I cannot do that at the moment. Even this letter underwent several legal checks to make sure it complies. Every word matters and holds true.”

Sports.title: Delia Smith's husband Michael Wynn Jones dies aged 85 as Norwich pay tribute
Sports.content:
Delia Smith's husband Michael Wynn Jones dies aged 85 as Norwich pay tribute

Michael Wynn Jones, the husband of TV chef Delia Smith, has died aged 85, with Norwich City paying tribute to their former majority shareholder in a statement

View 3 Images Delia Smith with Michael Wynn Jones at a Norwich game in 2023 (Image: Stephen Pond/Getty Images)

Norwich City have announced the death of their former majority shareholder, Michael Wynn Jones, at the age of 85.

‌



Jones is the husband of celebrity TV chef and cookery writer Delia Smith, 85, and was often seen alongside her at Norwich matches. The couple, who lived near Stowmarket in Suffolk, have been married since 1971.

‌



They were the majority shareholders of the Canaries from 1997 to October 2024. After selling their stakes, they became honoury life presidents of the Championship side.

‌



Norwich said in a statement: "Everyone at Norwich City is deeply saddened by the passing of our honorary life president, Michael Wynn Jones. Michael died peacefully at home on Monday morning, aged 85.

"He will be greatly missed. His family are grateful for the wonderful care provided by the community nursing team at St Elizabeth Hospice.

"Our deepest condolences are with Delia and Tom, and with all of Michael’s family, friends and loved ones. At the family’s request, we ask that their privacy be respected at this difficult time."

‌



View 3 Images Delia Smith and Michael Wynn Jones were regulars at Norwich games (Image: Alex Morton/Getty Images)

Norwich's rivals, Ipswich Town, added: "We send our condolences to Delia and Tom, all of Michael’s family and friends, and everyone at Norwich City at this time. Rest in peace, Michael."

Former Norwich winger Darren Huckerby said: "Such sad news, he stayed out of the limelight but all at [the club] owe him so much." Fellow ex-player Darren Eadie described Wynn Jones as "a kind and caring gentleman".

‌



Wynn Jones and Smith were majority shareholders of Norwich for 28 years, investing millions of pounds in the club. They reduced their stakes in the club to 10 per cent in 2025, selling the rest to FB Norfolk Holdings Group, the company of American millionaire Mark Attanasio, who now holds 85 per cent.

View 3 Images The couple were heavily involved at Norwich for 28 years (Image: Stephen Pond/Getty Images)

"The club’s existing board would like to place on record its sincere thanks and gratitude to Delia and Michael for their contributions to the club during their time as directors," the club said at the time.

Article continues below

“Delia and Michael have always been clear that they would act in the best interests of the club when passing on stewardship of it. By structuring the agreement in this way the parties have secured the long-term financial security of the club.”

As well as his involvement in Norwich City, Wynn Jones was known as a writer, editor and publisher. The Welshman established New Crane Publishing, which published some of Smith's cookbooks, while he also worked for Mirror Magazine when it hired her as a cookery writer in 1969.

Sports.title: Czech Republic chasing historic England win repeat with manager out to avenge grudge
Sports.content:
Czech Republic chasing historic England win repeat with manager out to avenge grudge

Czech Republic's new manager, Santi Denia, has previously tasted defeat twice against England while leading Spain's youth teams - but he has a blueprint to follow this time

View 2 Images Santi Denia is the new Czech Republic boss (Image: Marco Steinbrenner/Getty Images)

Czech Republic captain Ladislav Krejčí has promised to try and repeat one of his nation’s greatest-ever victories.

‌



England lost in the same stadium, the Fortuna Arena in Prague, in 2019 which ended a sequence of 43 games unbeaten in qualifiers. Wolves defender Krejčí, 27, is dreaming of another famous night and upset against England on Tuesday night.

‌



Krejčí said: “I remember I watched it on TV. I didn't play back then but it was really a great victory for the whole nation because defeating one of the best European and world teams in football is great. It's the kind of thing that shows us that even a little nation like us can do a feat like this, so that's why we go into this game with this motivation.

‌



"Really, that's the greatest thing when you represent your country. When you play against these kind of players and teams, and when you manage to defeat them. It would really mean a lot if we could replicate that."

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Krejčí will come back into the Czech starting XI after missing their Nations League opener against Croatia on Saturday. The former Girona defender says that he will be ready and also playing in England will give him extra insight and motivation.

Krejčí said: “I’m feeling good. I’m back in the team. I’m back in training and I feel ready. The decision is up to the coach but I feel good.

“I have special motivation for every match, especially these strong teams. When you play against teams like this. It’s not something you experience every week. This is a great opportunity to show we can play against teams like this so I’m very motivated.”

‌



The Czech Republic finished bottom of their Group at the World Cup and they have a new manager in former Spain youth coach Santi Denia. Denia was in charge for both games when Spain lost to England in the under-17s World Cup in 2017 and again in the under-21s European Championships in 2023.

View 2 Images Czech Republic beat England 2-1 in October 2019 (Image: Denis Doyle/UEFA via Getty Images)

The Czech boss was glowing about England’s improvements, their style and also insisted they are on the right path despite all the talk about England’s weaknesses in style and DNA.

‌



Denia said: “The development of the FA is unbelievable. They have invested a lot of money in their young players. The facilities. This is the way to grow. Invest a lot of money in young players.

“The association give a lot of opportunities for performances with friendly games. I think it is one of the best federations in the world.

“I think it’s very, very close. The level of Spain and England, also the clubs. The national teams are the same. You showed in the previous match, it’s very close. It’s details. I don’t want to compare both teams. It’s a different style. They are big teams, big coaches, big players.”

Article continues below

Denia hinted he might change the keepers from Newcastle’s Lukáš Horníček - who played well despite the defeat to Croatia - and may start with Tottenham’s No1 Antonín Kinský.

Sports.title: Littler in shock first-round exit at World Grand Prix as Van Gerwen also beaten
Sports.content:
Defending champion Luke Littler suffered a shock first-round exit at the World Grand Prix as he lost out 2-1 to Luke Woodhouse in Leicester, on the same night that six-time winner Michael van Gerwen was also eliminated.

Littler won the first set, but was far from his best as Woodhouse spurned several chances at double to have taken the opener into a deciding leg.

Woodhouse made no mistake in sets two and three, however, to see him pull off one of the biggest upsets in the hostory of the double-in, double-out tournament.

Image: Luke Littler's World Grand Prix defence was ended at the first hurdle by Luke Woodhouse

He'll face former finalist Nathan Aspinall in the second round after he overcame Kevin Doets in a final-leg decider earlier on the opening night.

Following his stunning early exit, Little posted on his Instagram: "Well played @lukewoodly180 was a good game, good one to be apart of aswell.

"Both hit, both missed but Luke took his chance and nice week off now, all the best to Luke for rest of tournament."

Littler followed that up by signalling his intent to now attend the Super League Grand Final on Saturday, which features his beloved Warrington Wolves - and would have clashed with the Grand Prix semi-finals.

"May aswell get myself to OT (Old Trafford) now I'm out. LETS GO THE WIRE @warringtonrlfc," Littler added.

Following his seismic victory over Littler, Woodhouse said afterwards: "Luke's not a robot. He's going to have days and weeks and whatever where he's not right on it.

"But look I think people have echoed it and I'm going to say it again, he's one of a kind Luke.

"I hope people will take the time to appreciate how good he is and not give him a hard time. You might not see another Luke Littler ever again."

Van Gerwen dumped out but Price, Clayton win

Elsewhere, not only were Van Gerwen's hopes of a seventh Grand Prix crown dashed but he suffered a third-straight first-round loss in the tournament as Ryan Joyce came back from a set down to defeat the Dutchman.

Welsh duo Gerwyn Price and Jonny Clayton, winners of the Grand Prix in 2020 and 2021 respectively, also progressed, with Price putting in the performance of the night as he averaged 101.61 and dropped only one leg in beating Sebastian Bialecki.

Clayton was made to work much harder by Krzysztof Ratajski, one of six matches (out of eight) to go the distance on the opening night.

Cameron Menzies and Kevin Doets both missed match darts when losing out to Ross Smith and Aspinall, respectively.

Each had chances to wrap up two-set victories, but Menzies missed two looks at tops before Smith swept him aside 3-0 in the deciding set, while Doets spurned three match darts - including a wild miss at bullseye - and Aspinall would ultimately take it in a last-leg decider in the third set.

Danny Noppert came flying out of the blocks to open the night, claiming five consecutive legs before Niko Springer, out of nowhere, claimed the next three to take the second set, before normal service resumed in the third.

Wessel Nijman, meanwhile, rounded off the evening with a routine 2-0 victory over Rob Cross.

He'll face Clayton next, while Noppert takes on MVG conqueror Joyce and Price goes up against Smith, who revealed he almost pulled out of the World Grand Prix after being hospitalised in the week leading up to the tournament.

"I've had a week from hell," Smith said after his first-round victory. "I've come home and picked up some sort of virus and I've had a few issues with my heart as well.

"I was in hospital on Friday. I thought I was pulling out of this event on Saturday, so to be here is an achievement in itself. Let alone play and win like that, I'm very happy."

Sports.title: 'The 12-day Masters 1000 is too much tennis' - Henman calls for changes to calendar
Sports.content:
Former British No 1 Tim Henman has called for changes to the calendar saying the 12-day Masters 1000 is "too much" tennis.

World No 1 Jannik Sinner announced he will not be able to return from a knee injury as planned at the China Open next week, having not played since Wimbledon.

Carlos Alcaraz missed the French Open and Wimbledon with a wrist problem while Britain's Emma Raducanu and Jack Draper are among a number of other players who have been out for lengthy spells in 2026.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Alcaraz spoke about the intensity of the schedule and how important it is to have a break to prevent injury

Eight of the nine Masters 1000 tournaments across the season are mandatory for most top players along with four ATP 500 events, and the growth of most Masters events to 12 days has been a bone of contention among players.

Former world No 4 Henman, who won the Masters 1000 title at the Paris Masters in 2003, would like to see changes.

"I think it's been pretty well documented that the 12-day Masters 1000s is just too much tennis," said Henman.

"That's too much time on the road and unfortunately we're seeing that with the number of players that are injured. I would definitely bring that to eight or nine days, which would free up the calendar.

"That's sort of more of a product change. I think if I had to make a practical, rule chance, then I would just get rid of the let serve.

"Every other shot can hit the top of the net, go over and in, so I would get rid of it and play it as it comes."

'ATP must do something if they want us to play important tournaments'

Image: Alcaraz inspired Team Europe to victory over Team World in the Laver Cup at the weekend

Alcaraz's run to the US Open quarter-finals was his first tournament since the Barcelona Open back in April after suffering a wrist injury.

Speaking in New York, the Spaniard stated: "Honestly, my break was longer than expected.

"Given the packed schedule, I obviously didn't want to stop because of an injury. However, in the future, I will take breaks, longer breaks. Maybe not four months, but one or two months, skipping certain tournaments, because it's impossible to play them all."

At the Laver Cup, which was won by Team Europe, Alcaraz said: "I think tennis has changed a lot. They have changed the balls, the courts, the speed of how we play, the movement is now more aggressive and you have to be prepared.

"We need weeks to practice and to make the physical training. There are more important tournaments making us play more and more, so I really want to takes breaks.

"Who knows what will happen in the future, but if the ATP and [chairman] Andrea Gaudenzi has to do something if they want us to play a lot of important tournaments."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the US Open mixed doubles with Serena Williams and Carlos Alcaraz taking centre stage

Italian Flavio Cobolli is also having second thoughts about the number of tournaments he plays in.

"If you look at the number of tournaments and the number of matches we play during the year, it's not that high," he said. "We're used to playing that much. The only thing we're not used to is staying at a tournament for so many days.

"The tournament format has changed, and maybe we still need to get used to it. I've now been away from home for almost a month and a half, and even if I had gone all the way here, I would have played fewer than 10 matches."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Martina Navratilova answers questions at the US Open about American success, British woes at Grand Slams, and why tennis is harder than football!!!

Murray: I understand it from the players' perspective

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Naomi Broady, Ryan Harrison and Jamie Murray discuss Alcaraz's future schedule

Speaking to Sky Sports Tennis, Jamie Murray said: "I can totally understand it from the players' perspective. The Tour is longer than it's ever been in terms of commitment and days away from home.

"These younger guys have seen how Roger [Federer] and Rafael [Nadal] have elongated their careers - how they finished their careers as well. If they want to play until they're 34, 35, 36, they will probably have to skip tournaments and that's something the Tour needs to consider.

"The Tour is catering for over a hundred players and they want to be out there competing."

Sports.title: 'I didn't leave my family to lose' - LeBron ready for Philly success
Sports.content:
NBA legend LeBron James has quashed retirement talk as he gets set for record-extending 24th season having signed with the Philadelphia 76ers this summer.

James will begin his expected final chapter at his inaugural camp with the 76ers.

He made the NBA world wait a few weeks before announcing his decision over the summer to join to Philadelphia on a two-year $8m (£6m) contract with a player option for next season.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player LeBron James has stunned the basketball world once again by announcing he's signed for the Philadelphia 76ers, a franchise that hasn't won an NBA title in 43 years

If James wins a title in Philadelphia, the 76ers would be the fourth franchise to become champions with him on the roster.

James won two championships in Miami, one in Cleveland and one with the Los Angeles Lakers.

"I'm not going to speak to the future right now; I'd be doing myself a disservice," James said at the Sixers' media day.

"I'm just living in the moment, especially knowing where I am in my career.

"Me trying to focus on what my future looks like, I wouldn't be giving myself grace. I'm more in the present now, understanding that I'm in year 24... I just like being in the moment, and we'll see what happens."

And if that Philly title happens, it would give Joel Embiid his first ring - which is part of James' motivation.

"I didn't leave my family (in Los Angeles) to lose in the second round," said James, who will turn 42 in December. "I know that for sure. Work needs to be done and I'm ready to get to work."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Here's a look back at the 22-time All-Star's best career plays...

Much as James did for Cleveland when he ended a 56-year championship drought for the city by leading the Cavaliers to the title in 2016, he's in Philadelphia largely to help snap a championship drought for the Sixers that stretches to 1983.

The Sixers went 45-37 last season and were swept in the second round by the eventual champion New York Knicks.

"Understand that the noise is going to be the noise," James said. "What happens outside of this building is going to consistently happen, and it's going to be doubled and triple and quadrupled down on you. It just comes with the territory. I understand it.

"I think the luxury of my game is, I can do everything. Literally, I can do everything."

Sports.title: Tuchel: On the ball, we were a danger to ourselves
Sports.content:
Thomas Tuchel believes England were a danger to themselves on the ball during their 3-2 defeat to Spain.

The Three Lions made several crucial mistakes in their loss to the reigning world and European champions on Saturday and were made to pay with goals from Lamine Yamal, Alex Baena and Mikel Oyarzabal.

Having gone the whole of the World Cup qualifying campaign without conceding, Tuchel's side have now let in nine from their last three internationals against Argentina, France and Spain.

Despite showing frailties against elite opposition, Tuchel does not think England's issue lies with their defensive set-up and instead insists that their mistakes have come from causing their own issues in possession.

"It's not a concern yet," Tuchel said ahead of England's second Nations League game against Czech Republic on Tuesday.

"I felt that in terms of organised defending, block defending and active defending, we were at a higher level than in many other matches.

Follow Czech Republic vs England with Sky Sports Follow Czech Republic vs England with our live match blog on the Sky Sports website and App on Tuesday; kick-off 7.45pm.

"If you want to look at it in isolation on how we did within the structure and in the units of the sides, I was quite happy and I think it was a step ahead.

"We suffered clearly from individual mistakes when we had the ball, especially in the deep build-up, so that is of course something we cannot repeat. Not at this level.

"Strangely enough, when we had the ball, we were the biggest danger to ourselves around the box because we just had too many individual mistakes. Purely in defending, I have no concerns and I trust that we can do it."

Your England questions answered! We'll be running a Q&A with Sky Sports News England reporter Rob Dorsett on Tuesday morning. Head to the Sky Sports website or App and get your Three Lions question in and Rob will answer the best of them!

Tuchel's comments come off the back of widespread criticism of his tactics during England's World Cup semi-final defeat to Argentina, where he opted to defend a one-goal lead rather than looking to extend their advantage.

The German responded by hitting out at the 'DNA' of English players. "I think ball possession plays a crucial role; it's maybe not in our DNA like it is in Spanish DNA or in Argentinian-Brazilian DNA, to take the ball and control the game with the ball," he said following their exit.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sam Blitz analyses whether Thomas Tuchel's comments on England's 'DNA' are correct or an excuse after defeat to Argentina in the World Cup semi-final

It raised scrutiny over England's footballing identity, but Tuchel believed his players showcased exactly that in the defeat to Luis de la Fuente's side at Wembley.

"I think there was a lot of discussion about this before [the Spain game]," Tuchel stated.

"I think we showed our style and we showed our courage. The players showed an identity and they showed it throughout the 90 minutes.

"We gave them a lot of problems. We caused ourselves some problems with individual mistakes. Mistakes can sometimes happen. They shouldn't, but they did happen.

"We had the world and European champions on the edge of a defeat. In the decisive moments we played our best football. We kept attacking when we were a goal ahead. We were even more dominant and more of a threat.

"We were a little bit self-responsible for the break in momentum towards the end of the match. But overall we have a lot of positives to take away."
