World.title: Thembisa murder: Estranged husband found dead hours later
World.content:
Boitumelo Gift Mashita, 23, was shot while on her way to work in Temong, Thembisa, on Monday morning. Police later found her estranged husband dead in a vehicle in Midrand. Images: X

Boitumelo Gift Mashita’s family suspected someone close to her had killed her. By Monday evening, police had linked her estranged husband to the murder — and found him dead inside his vehicle in Midrand.

Mashita, 23, was shot while on her way to work in Mapungubwe Street, Temong, at about 05:45 on 28 September. She worked as a chef in Centurion and leaves behind a five-year-old son.

Family feared someone close to Mashita was involved

A man linked to the murder of 23-year-old Boitumelo Gift Mashita in Tembisa this morning has been found dead in his vehicle in Midrand. Police say he was her estranged husband and a person of interest.



Photo: Top left of the picture – the red Kia in Midrand where he was found.… pic.twitter.com/1Os2CYfbTY  September 28, 2026

Before the police update, Mashita’s sister, Yeolanda Sithole,said that the person the family suspected had allegedly threatened to kill her. Her uncle, Motlatsi Khoza, said the family believed someone close to Mashita was responsible.

In an interview, the family remembered Mashita as someone who brought life to their gatherings. They said her phone was missing after the shooting and that she kept her identity document behind it.

Her aunt, Jeanette Khoza, struggled with the thought of telling Mashita’s young son that his mother had died. “I don’t know what we are going to tell the boy,” she told said.



BREAKING NEWS | Police have confirmed that a man suspected of murdering 23-year-old Boitumelo Mashita in Thembisa has been found dead inside a vehicle in Midrand. For more news, visit https://t.co/N9V5BF50jx pic.twitter.com/vhhmPZQI5M — SABC News (@SABCNews) September 28, 2026

Estranged husband found dead in Midrand

Police initially opened a murder and robbery case after reporting that Mashita’s belongings had been taken. Investigators later linked her estranged husband to the killing and identified him as a person of interest.

Gauteng police spokesperson Brigadier Brenda Muridili said the SAPS Tembisa Tracking Team was tracing him when Midrand police found his vehicle with his body inside.



Muridili said he may have ingested an unknown substance.

“No foul play is suspected at this stage,” she said. “A post-mortem examination will be conducted to determine the exact cause of death.”

Midrand police will open an inquest. Police have not explained how Mashita’s missing phone and the reported theft of her belongings fit into the murder investigation.



Muridili said preliminary investigations had found no link between Mashita’s killing and the recent cases involving women’s bodies found across Ekurhuleni.

World.title: Sundowns defender Grant Kekana (34) not ruling out his Bafana Bafana return
World.content:
Mamelodi Sundowns defender Grant Kekana has not shut down the door on his Bafana Bafana return.

The 34-year-old centre-back played a huge role in helping Bafana finish third at the 2023 Africa Cup of Nations. Injuries and poor form saw him lose his place in the national team.He missed out of the 2025 AFCON as well as the 2026 FIFA World Cup.

With the likes of Mbekezeli Mbokazi, Olwethu Makhanya and Ime Okon secured their place in the Bafana squad, Kekana’s return looks unlikely.



The veteran defender though feels he can still add to the national team under Pitso Mosimane.

“I’m feeling good and better than I’ve been in the long time,” said Kekana on SNAWA.

“It’s just for me to continue working, I think there’s still a chance for me but all the players that have been selected are fully deserving of their places.



“I think it’s going to be a nice time to watch them. Coach Pitso has got something to build.

Kekana eyeing Bafana return

Kekana’s return to the national team looks more like a dream given the quality of defenders Mosimane has. All centre-backs are 23 years and below and almost all of them play their football overseas.

One player who is also looking to return to the Bafana squad is 29-year-old Siyabonga Ngezana. He is ahead of Kekana in terms of the pecking order meaning the Downs defender will most likely not get another chance to play for Bafana.



Should Kekana be granted another opportunity?

World.title: United States wins 11th successive Presidents Cup title
World.content:
UNITED STATES - The US has clinched victory in an 11th successive Presidents Cup after seeing off the Internationals in Illinois.

However, it was no easy win for Team USA, as they needed to stage a fightback on the final day.

They headed into Sunday’s fourth round trailing by three points and looked to avoid a second defeat since the biennial competition began 32 years ago.

They dominated the singles, winning nine of the 12 matches, to seal a 17-13 win.

Cameron Young, Justin Thomas, Scottie Scheffler, Chris Gotterup, and Collin Morikawa also won.

US President Donald Trump attended as honorary chairman, greeting players and speaking before the matches began.

World.title: Norris and Calapinto smoke peace pipe
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Lando Norris has issued an apology to Franco Colapinto.

The Brit had criticised the Argentine for causing a crash that took both drivers out of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix.

The incident took place during a Safety Car restart in Baku.

Colapinto locked his brakes in the first corner and hit the side of his Alpine team-mate Pierre Gasly, who was sent straight into Norris.

Despite earlier saying Colapinto should not be in Formula 1, Norris has since retracted his utterances.

World.title: WATCH | Is your boss paying your pension ?
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Regulators have again urged workers to ensure their retirement contributions are being paid over by their employers.

The Financial Sector Conduct Authority says employees often receive the shock of finding their pension funds have gone AWOL when they apply for a two-pot retirement fund withdrawal.

READ | Joburg pensioner wins R2.6m billing battle

More than half a million South Africans have discovered that funds that are being deducted from their salaries are not being paid over to retirement funds.

More than 16 000 employers have now been flagged for not paying.

The regulator has calculated that R8.3-billion in pension funds is owed, which includes penalties for interest that has not been earned

World.title: 'Stop pointing fingers, deal with criminality' - Liquor Traders Association
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The Gauteng Liquor Traders Association insists tavern owners are being used as scapegoats for violence and turf wars.

Association spokesperson Jongikhaya Kraai said the blame can not always be pointed to liquor outlets when such shootings happen, especially when they are legally licensed.

"The outlets that we are talking about, yes, it is at a residential area. It is a licensed outlet, meaning it went through all the hoops that it was supposed to jump to be licensed at that particular area.

"Unfortunately, liquor traders in this province or in townships cannot afford rentals at affluent areas or at business zoned or business sites. We can only operate where we reside and the unfortunate part is that some of these killings, we cannot unfortunately run away from,"

Kraai noted the elements of criminality behind these incidents and urged for more police visibility.

"I hope we stop pointing fingers at each other and start dealing with the criminality we face every day," he said.

But the Southern African Alcohol Policy Alliance argues otherwise.

According to its campaign director, Nomcebo Dlamini, liquor outlets cannot deflect blame onto already overburdened police.

"Ten to 12 percent of our GDP goes to these issues that are around alcohol. And not that we're saying that businesses should not exist, but we are basically saying public health really should be uppermost in every decision that we make," she said.

Recent mass shootings in Gauteng and the Western Cape have reignited concerns over safety at taverns.

A total of 32 people were killed in three separate mass shootings this weekend.

World.title: Chapter 9 institutions team up for national inquiry into the state's response to GBVF
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Three Chapter 9 institutions have joined forces for a national inquiry into how the criminal justice system responds to gender-based violence and femicide in South Africa.

The Commission for Gender Equality, the South African Human Rights Commission, and the Cultural, Religious and Linguistic Communities Rights Commission are leading the inquiry.

The national inquiry is expected to run from 29 September to 2 October in Johannesburg in different phases.

READ | Twist in Thembisa murder case as estranged husband found dead

The first phase is expected to focus specifically on survivor testimony and lived experiences, while the second stage will focus on pre-trial functioning and accountability within the criminal justice system.

“The National Joint Inquiry seeks to hold duty bearers accountable for issues, challenges and improvements that may be necessary to the justice system,” the Commissions said.

World.title: A total of 32 gunned down in two days: Where are the AK-47s coming from?
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The last weekend of September 2026 has been marred by bloodshed, with 32 people killed in three separate shootings.

This has once again renewed concerns over the growing gun violence in South Africa and access to illegal firearms, which are used in these incidents.

Julian Rademeyer from the Global Initiative Against Transnational Organised Crime (GITOC) said the ongoing trend in mass killings observed in the country is closely linked to organised crime.

READ |'Send a thief to catch a thief' - Mkhwanazi on crushing gangs and organised crime

This, he said, includes illegal gold mining, extortion, gangs, drug trade, as well as taxi violence.

Adding to that, Rademeyer said, are killers who walk around knowing there are no consequences for their heinous crimes.

“They're operating with almost complete impunity walking into a tavern in the morning with AK-47s and opening fire on a crowd without any care of who is caught up in that gunfire.”

Rademeyer painted a grim picture of the country's murder landscape.

While police statistics show a decline in the murder rate, he said there appears to be an increase in the ferocity and number of the types of incidents in recent months.

According to Rademeyer, a total of 44 people were killed in September in four attacks.

In August, at least 32 were killed in eight attacks, while in July about 27 people were killed in seven attacks.

“A major concern is the violence that comes with these attacks,” he said.

That violence was on full display in Wedela, west of Johannesburg, where a total of 18 people were gunned down after suspects armed with AK-47s opened fire at a tavern on Saturday night.

The same day, but in Mthuma Street, Site C, Khayelitsha, Western Cape, four people were shot and killed.

Another 10 people were killed in a separate shooting in Lwandle, Western Cape, in the early hours of Sunday morning.

READ |Carletonville tavern shooting: Death toll rises to 18

Rademeyer said South Africa is awash with illegal firearms, with illegal firearms entering through various channels.

“There are leakages and thefts from state stockpiles, from the police, from SAPS-13 evidence stores, from the SANDF. We've got leakages from the security industry. That's excluding weapons that are in circulation.”

Adding to that is the influx of AK-style weapons, with Rademeyer alleging that some originate from outside the country and are being smuggled into gangs in the Western Cape.

Rademeyer fighting crime will need more boots on the ground backed by stronger crime intelligence.

But this becomes hard when the systems in place are already weak.

World.title: Twist in Thembisa murder case as estranged husband found dead
World.content:
Please note that the following story may contain graphic visuals and content.

JOHANNESBURG - A man suspected to be responsible for the murder of Boitumelo Mashita in Thembisa on Monday morning has been found dead inside his vehicle in Midrand.

This has led the police to register an inquest case for investigation.

According to Gauteng police spokesperson Brenda Muridili, the man is believed to be Mashita’s estranged husband.

READ | 23-year-old woman killed in Thembisa

Muridili said authorities who had been tracing him as a person of interest were informed by the Midrand Police Station that his car had been found within the policing precinct with his body inside.

Police are now working to establish the cause of his death.

“It is believed that he may have ingested an unknown substance, as no foul play is suspected at this stage. A post-mortem examination will be conducted to determine the exact cause of death,” she said.

On Monday morning, residents of Temong in Thembisa woke up to gunshots and the body of a 23-year-old woman lying on Mapungubwe Street.

At the time of the incident, Mashita was on her way to work but never made it there.

World.title: IEBC, DCI Deny cross-border vote smuggling allegations as The Standard defends investigation
World.content:
Chairperson of the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC) Erastus Edung Ethekon during the launch of Roadmap to peaceful 2027 General elections.[David Gichuru, Standard]

The Standard’s cross-border vote smuggling investigation continued to draw strong reactions on Monday, with both the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC) and the Directorate of Criminal Investigations (DCI) issuing formal statements denying the allegations and questioning the timing of the report.

IEBC Chairperson Erastus Edung Ethekon said in a statement released on Sunday evening that allegations of illegal voter registration, unlawful voter transfers, and the registration of foreigners remained "unsubstantiated and untrue."

World.title: Police reveal Cohen, Wairimu's repeated disputes before murder
World.content:
Dutch tycoon Tob Cohen and his wife Sarah Wairimu Kamotho.[File, Standard]

Two police officers have told the High Court how repeated domestic disputes between slain Dutch businessman Tob Cohen and his wife Sarah Wairimu had brought them to the attention of police months before his death.

The officers testified on Monday before Justice Diana Kavedza at the Kibera High Court, describing separate incidents handled at Parklands, Spring Valley and Gigiri police stations.

World.title: Kalonzo signals at working with Ruto if 2027 poll is free and fair
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Wiper Patriotic Front leader Kalonzo Musyoka at St Michael and All Angels ACK Cathedral in Bondo, Siaya County on September 27, 2026. [Clinton Ambujo, Standard]

Wiper Patriotic Front leader Kalonzo Musyoka has signalled that the Opposition could accept the outcome of the 2027 General Election and consider working with President William Ruto if he wins through a free and fair contest.

Speaking at St Michael and All Angels ACK Cathedral in Bondo, Siaya County, Kalonzo said the political class must commit itself to democratic competition and be prepared to accept the verdict of voters.

“If you beat us, we will have to consider if you have behaved yourself, and if we beat you, we have to look at all these things,” he said.

The Wiper leader also called for stronger democratic institutions, warning against political confrontation that could deepen divisions in the country.

“We have a nation here. We have to make this country truly democratic. I do not think we have a shortcut,” he said.

Kalonzo used the church service to make a broader appeal for a united and effective Opposition, saying political leaders had a responsibility to work together in the national interest.

“Kenya needs a functional official opposition; one that is united and does not thrive on disunity. As leaders, we have a responsibility to work together and play our part in fixing this nation,” he said.

He said he had remained in the Opposition even when some political allies moved into government.

“I have stood in the opposition all these years. Even when others joined government, my brother Eugene Wamalwa and I remained steadfast, and we will continue to stand firm,” he said.

Kalonzo also turned his attention to Parliament, claiming that the National Assembly had been “captured” and challenging lawmakers in both Houses to exercise their constitutional responsibilities.

“The National Assembly has been captured. Let this message reach every leader in the National Assembly and the Senate: you have the power to change things, not just to complain later,” he said.

He urged legislators to defend the interests of the people who elected them and to put the country ahead of political considerations.

The former Vice President also defended retired President Uhuru Kenyatta against claims that he is financing the Opposition ahead of the 2027 contest.

Kalonzo argued that presidential campaigns have historically relied on networks of political allies and supporters rather than family resources alone.

“But here we are saying, please let Uhuru rest; he is a retired President. Stop saying he is our financier,” he said.

Kalonzo cited previous presidential campaigns involving Uhuru, former President Mwai Kibaki and Raila Odinga, arguing that major political campaigns require support from friends and associates.

“Even when Uhuru was running for President, or Kibaki and even Raila, no family has enough resources to support a presidential campaign. It is friends who support you,” he said.

He warned that Kenya was at a delicate political moment and urged leaders to avoid actions that could deepen instability.

“We should not allow the country to get to a worse situation than where it is. We are on the edge of a cliff; the country is at a crossroads,” he said.

World.title: ODM delegates reject Sakaja using the party for gubernatorial bid
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Nairobi ODM chairman George Aladwa addressing the media over the upcoming ODM nominations in Nairobi. [Collins Oduor, Standard]

Nairobi ODM delegates have resolved to reject and lobby against attempts by some people in President William Ruto's broad-based government to give Nairobi Governor Johnson Sakaja the ODM ticket in the 2027 gubernatorial race.

Party members, delegates and branch chairpersons met in Makadara, where they agreed that ODM be allowed to field their own candidates instead of the party allowing UDA leaders to vie on the party ticket.

They also resolved to back Makadara MP George Aladwa. With Tutam songs renting the air during the meeting, they also agreed to back President Ruto's re-election.

"Aladwa should be the party's candidate for Nairobi governor, and every candidate should seek the seat through their own political party," said an agitated delegate from Kasarani.

They insisted ODM should not allow an outsider to join the party and use its ticket to contest for the gubernatorial seat, arguing that the ODM ticket should be reserved for a candidate who enjoys the support of its members.

"We will not allow someone from another party to come and vie using ODM while we have our own members. As a party our only candidate is Aladwa," said delegate chairs.

They added that their position follows a series of meetings held across all 17 constituencies in Nairobi, with Makadara being the final constituency to hold its meeting.

They further argued that the Nairobi gubernatorial seat requires a leader with experience and leadership skills, warning ODM members against supporting candidates they believe lack the necessary political and leadership experience.

They also sustained their criticism towards former president Uhuru, alleging that he is undermining the party and dividing it, and they will not allow it.

George Aladwa backed the ODM members' position, saying every politician seeking elective office should do so through their own political party.

The delegates maintained that ODM should protect its identity and ticket, insisting that candidates from outside the party should not be allowed to use the ODM ticket to pursue elective positions when active and loyal members are sidelined.

The delegates are calling on ODM to ensure that the nomination process is free, fair and transparent, giving party members an opportunity to choose the candidate they want to represent them.

World.title: Oil rig arrives in Mombasa ahead of Kenya's first commercial drilling
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Oil rig arrives in Mombasa ahead of Kenya’s first commercial drilling. [Courtes]

Kenya has moved closer to commercial oil production after a 1,500 horsepower drilling rig arrived at the Port of Mombasa ahead of its deployment to the South Lokichar Basin in Turkana County.

The GW70 rig, leased by Gulf Energy E&P BV from Great Wall Drilling Company, docked at Kilindini Port on Friday aboard MV Transit Sedanka after sailing from Duqm Port in Oman.

It is expected to be transported to Turkana, where drilling is scheduled to begin on November 1.

“All workstreams at Gulf Energy E&P BV SEZ are running to a tight project management schedule, and the project remains on course for First Oil production in December 2026,” Gulf Energy Chief Executive Officer Paul Limoh said.

The arrival marks a step in the commercial development of the South Lokichar Basin, more than a decade after oil was first discovered in Turkana in 2012.

The first phase of the project is expected to produce about 20,000 barrels of crude oil per day, with output projected to rise to 50,000 barrels per day in the second phase.

The Energy and Petroleum Regulatory Authority (EPRA) says Kenya is targeting first oil in December 2026, while the first crude exports through the Port of Mombasa are expected in the first quarter of 2027.

The GW70 will undergo commissioning and acceptance checks before drilling begins. Gulf Energy has contracted Baker Hughes for integrated well services and SLB to provide an early production facility for the first phase.

World.title: Two more suspects arrested over lawyer Kyalo Mbobu murder
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

The two suspects are currently in custody undergoing processing as detectives pursue additional leads.

Detectives have arrested two more suspects in connection with the fatal shooting of lawyer Kyalo Mbobu, as an intelligence-led operation targeting people linked to the September 9, 2025 murder intensifies.

The two boda boda riders Nicholas Lemiso Naula and Noah Kipkirui Langat were arrested in Nairobi’s Central Business District, following sustained efforts by detectives to trace individuals suspected to have been involved in the killing.

According to the Directorate of Criminal Investigations (DCI), Lemiso is a boda boda rider who allegedly ferried the main suspect, Police Constable Julius Cheruiyot, to and from the scene of the murder, while Langat was arrested over alleged surveillance on Mbobu before his killing.

"With three suspects now in custody, detectives are intensifying the hunt for other persons suspected to have played a role in the meticulously planned killing," DCI stated.

His arrest comes shortly after detectives arrested Cheruiyot in connection with the killing.

“The dragnet over the fatal shooting of lawyer Kyalo Mbobu has widened, with detectives arresting a second suspect as an intelligence-led operation targeting persons linked to the murder intensifies,” DCI said.

The two suspects are currently in custody undergoing processing as detectives pursue additional leads and seek to identify and arrest other people who may have been involved. The DCI said the operation remains active as investigators work to establish the circumstances surrounding Mbobu’s murder.

“The DCI is leaving no stone unturned in its efforts to unravel the full circumstances surrounding Lawyer Mbobu’s murder and bring all those responsible to justice,” the agency said.

World.title: KRA seizes 53,000 under-declared smartphones at Eldoret Airport
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

The consignment was intercepted by KRA enforcement teams following an intelligence report.

Kenya Revenue Authority (KRA) has seized a consignment containing 53,000 under-declared smartphones at Eldoret International Airport, averting a potential tax loss of Sh21.5 million.

KRA enforcement teams intercepted the consignment after an intelligence report indicated it contained undeclared mobile phones and other high-end electronic goods.

The cargo, which had been declared under five Customs entries, was part of consolidated shipments that also included shoes, clothing, automotive spare parts, household goods, electronic accessories and other assorted items.

KRA said an initial declaration listed only 3,000 smartphones. However, verification established 55,607 ordinary smartphones, alongside 309 undeclared high-end smartphones.

The high-end devices included Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra, Samsung Galaxy Z Fold and Apple iPhone 17 Pro Max models.

“The consignment therefore reflects both under-declaration and non-declaration of dutiable goods,” KRA said in a statement issued on Wednesday.

The tax authority said the verification exercise was conducted to establish whether all mobile phones contained in the consignment had been properly declared.

KRA said the alleged tax evasion contravenes Section 203 of the East African Community Customs Management Act (EACCMA), 2004.

The law provides that a person who makes a false or incorrect Customs entry, or knowingly participates in the fraudulent evasion of duty, commits an offence.

“A person who, in any matter relating to Customs, makes any entry which is false or incorrect in any particular, or in any way is knowingly concerned in any fraudulent evasion of the payment of any duty, commits an offence,” KRA said, citing the law.

According to the authority, a person convicted under the provision is liable to imprisonment for a term not exceeding three years or a fine of up to US$10,000.

KRA said it was intensifying efforts to uncover tax evasion schemes to improve revenue compliance and ensure adherence to tax laws and procedures.

“KRA is actively engaged in unearthing tax evasion schemes to boost tax revenue compliance as well as adherence to tax laws and procedures, hence ensuring fair trade is maintained within the market,” the authority said.

The authority also appealed to members of the public, taxpayers and businesses with information on individuals, companies or networks involved in the generation, sale, purchase or use of fictitious VAT invoices to report them.

KRA said information provided would be treated confidentially and the identity of informants kept anonymous.

World.title: 'We know what happened': Uhuru claims Raila won 2022 polls
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Former President Uhuru Kenyatta. [File, Standard]

Former President Uhuru Kenyatta says he remains convinced that Raila Odinga won the 2022 presidential election.

Speaking during a Jubilee Party meeting in Nairobi on Tuesday, September 22, Uhuru questioned how the Azimio coalition could have lost the presidency despite performing strongly in other elective races.

“We did everything to help Baba become President of the Republic of Kenya. He got the votes, and to this day I know that he is the one who won those votes. We know how things happened, and we do not want it to happen that way again,” Uhuru said.

The late Odinga contested the August 9, 2022 election under the Azimio la Umoja-One Kenya Coalition Party, with Martha Karua as his running mate. Ruto ran under the United Democratic Alliance (UDA) as the presidential candidate of the Kenya Kwanza Alliance.

Ruto was declared president-elect after garnering 7,176,141 votes, 50.49 per cent, against Odinga's 6,942,930 votes, 48.85 per cent. Ruto's margin was 233,211 votes.

The Supreme Court later unanimously upheld his election after dismissing petitions challenging the results.

But Uhuru pointed to the coalition's performance in the parliamentary and county races to question how Azimio could have lost the presidency.

“How can you say we were defeated when we had most of the MPs, governors and senators? How were we defeated in the presidency?” he asked.

In the National Assembly, figures published after the election initially put Azimio ahead of Kenya Kwanza, with 165 seats against 160, while 12 seats were held by independent MPs.

Azimio also won 23 of the 47 governorships, while Kenya Kwanza secured 22. The remaining two were won by Taita Taveta Governor Andrew Mwadime and former Meru Governor Kawira Mwangaza, who ran as independent candidates.

In the Senate, Kenya Kwanza had an advantage, winning 24 of the 47 directly elected seats against Azimio's 23.

The parliamentary balance later shifted in favour of Kenya Kwanza after several MPs changed their political allegiance.

In October 2022, National Assembly Speaker Moses Wetang'ula declared Kenya Kwanza the majority coalition with 179 MPs against Azimio's 157, after several MPs from parties including UDM, MDG, Maendeleo Chap Chap and PAA moved towards the Kenya Kwanza side.

Uhuru also rejected claims that he was responsible for Odinga's loss, saying he was not a candidate in the election.

“I am surprised when people say that we did not help Baba and that they defeated me. I was not on the ballot, and they are lying. I was only Raila's handyman,” he said.

He warned against what he described as divisive and dirty politics, saying Kenya should not repeat the events surrounding the 2022 election.

“Dirty politics and politics aimed at dividing Kenyans will take us nowhere. Let us not divide each other. What does it help us? Sell your manifesto,” Uhuru said.

He said he accepted the Supreme Court's decision after the 2022 presidential petitions and handed over power to Ruto without disputing the outcome, accusing Ruto of dragging his name in his failed leadership.

“When we finished and the court ruled, we did not dispute it. We went and handed over the presidency to them. And now, after four years, they are still talking about Uhuru. But when things are not working, people tend to look for excuses,” he said.

This is the clearest public assertion by the former president since the 2022 elections that Odinga won the presidential vote.

World.title: Proposal to harvest organs from Egypt’s death-row inmates sparks controversy
World.content:
A proposal by professor of critical care medicine at Kasr Al-Ainy Faculty of Medicine, Hossam Mowafy, regarding harvesting organs from individuals sentenced to death has sparked controversy and raised medical, legal, and religious questions.

Mowafy called for a definitive ruling on the legal and religious status of the idea—specifically whether organs could be harvested before or after the execution of the sentence.

He addressed inquiries to the Public Prosecutor and the Al-Azhar Grand Sheikh, seeking clarification on the compatibility of such a measure with Low and Sharia provisions, particularly given the critical need for life-saving organ transplants among some patients.

The Fatwa Secretary at Dar al-Ifta, Hisham Rabie, explained that transplanting organs from the deceased to the living is allowed in principle, according to established fatwas in Egypt and rulings by various Islamic jurisprudence councils; however, he emphasized that this practice is subject to specific religious guidelines.

A question of free will

He noted that a key requirement is that the consent to donate must stem from free will and a person of full legal capacity, free from coercion or any form of physical or psychological pressure.

The circumstances of a death-row inmate, along with the associated constraints and psychological pressures, Rabie said, raise questions about full consent, thereby posing an obstacle to authorizing the proposal in its current form.

A lawyer before the Court of Cassation and the Supreme Constitutional Court, Amr Abdel-Salam, said that the proposal conflicts with the regulations governing organ transplantation.

He explained that donation requires free and informed consent, and that the consent or testamentary directive must be formally documented in accordance with legal procedures.

Abdel-Salam added that the status of a person sentenced to death raises issues regarding the existence of free will—whether before or after the sentence is carried out—noting that the restrictions imposed on such individuals mean that utilizing their organs for donation requires an explicit legal basis.

He pointed out that the Egyptian Constitution enshrines the inviolability of the human body and stipulates that organ donation after death requires consent or a documented will; he emphasized that the state does not gain the right to dispose of a person’s body simply because a death sentence has been issued.

Abdel-Salam explained that Article #60 of the Constitution establishes the inviolability of the human body, while Article 61 defines the donation of tissues and organs as a “gift of life,” permitted either during one’s lifetime or after death through consent or a documented will.

Resolving the proposal requires considering these constitutional and legal parameters, alongside the religious and ethical aspects associated with organ donation, he said.

Formal declaration

The founder of the Liver Oncology Unit at the National Liver Institute, Mohamed Ezz al-Arab, said that Law #5 of 2010 on organ transplantation allows for post-mortem organ donation – provided there is a formal declaration of intent to donate.

He emphasized that the use of a deceased person’s organs cannot be separated from the wishes they expressed prior to death.

Ezz al-Arab stressed that the crucial factor is not merely the medical viability of the organ, but the existence of a legal declaration—documented in official records—that reflects the donor’s free will.

He explained that post-mortem donation must be based on a declaration made by the individual before death; the absence of such a legal declaration could raise concerns regarding potential coercion or pressure exerted on the individual prior to the procedure.

Edited translation from Al-Masry Al-Youm

World.title: Questions loom over alleged UK terror plot near air base used by US bombers
World.content:
Fairford, England —

The five men arrested on suspicion of a terrorist plot to attack an airbase in England used by long-range US bombers are all UK nationals, according to British police.

The five are residents of London, and are aged between 23 and 25, according to a statement from counter-terrorism police, which spoke of “multiple new lines of enquiry.”

The men, who have not been identified, were arrested early Sunday close to the base at Fairford in western England, from where US B-1 bombers have been flying missions against Iran.

“This is a hugely complex and large-scale operation,” Vicki Evans, a senior counter-terrorism officer, said on Monday.

UK authorities have not disclosed where the men are being held, nor what was found in three white vans the men appear to have used.

Aerial footage on Sunday showed a bomb disposal robot roaming between the vans in woods near the base. The rear doors of two of the vans were open and large black items could be seen scattered on the ground nearby.

CNN teams nearby later heard what sounded like two controlled detonations from the direction of the village where the vans were found.

Iranian threat

Asked if a hostile foreign state could have been behind the incident, British Defense Minister Wes Streeting said on Monday he did not “want to speculate at this stage of the investigation.”

In July, Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps specifically noted Fairford’s use by US bombers, warning the UK that “any base used for aggression against Iranian territory constitutes a legitimate target for our forces.”

The Iranian embassy in London issued a statement Monday saying it “categorically rejects and strongly condemns the recent unfounded and malicious speculations published by some British individuals and media outlets attempting to link Iran to arrest of five suspects in the vicinity of RAF Fairford base.”

US President Donald Trump called the arrests “fantastic,” saying the US and the UK had the men under investigation for “a long time.”

A US Air Force B-1 Lancer bomber is pictured on the tarmac at RAF Fairford on Sunday. Justin Tallis/AFP/Getty Images

“Working with Britain, it was an amazing job,” Trump told reporters in Chicago. “They were looking to do big damage to our fort and working with the British worked out great.”

“We had them under view for a long time, and we got them,” he said.

UK authorities have not commented on the US president’s assertion. It’s unclear whether the five men were under surveillance before their arrival in the Fairford area in the early hours of Sunday.

“Hooded and masked”

Photographs of the men – shirtless with their hands tied behind their backs – appeared in UK media Sunday.

They were initially detained under laws on possession of explosives and were later additionally arrested “on suspicion of preparation of a terrorist act,” according to a statement by counter-terrorism police.

A local resident said she came across the men when returning home on Saturday night.

“Both the driveway and the road were blocked by three white vans,” she said.

The resident, who wishes to remain anonymous, told CNN that the vans were parked in a “strange formation” about 100 meters from the base fence.

She believed there were more than five men in the group and most had their faces covered. Authorities have not indicated that they are looking for other individuals.

Some ran into the field and some towards the neighboring village, she said.

A photo geolocated by CNN shows suspects arrested and on the ground in Fairford on Sunday. Social Media

She called the emergency services at 1:40 a.m., according to phone records she showed CNN. Within ten or 15 minutes, armed police arrived.

“I think it was pure luck that I arrived in the village at a similar time to the vans,” the resident, a farmer, added.

Multiple UK media outlets – including the BBC, the Guardian and the Telegraph – reported, citing sources, that the operation was not intelligence-led, suggesting the vigilance of local residents may have played a key role in alerting authorities.

Counter-terrorism police said they first received a call “relating to three suspicious vehicles which appeared to be travelling towards the airbase” about an hour before the resident called.

Streeting said the resident had “a partial picture” of the situation, adding that the work of the police and the security services “takes place often unsung, unreported, for good reason,” he said.

A cordon around the area where the men were detained remains, with a number of people evacuated from their homes.

Tightened security

Armed police maintain road blocks and security checks around RAF Fairford on Monday. Leon Neal/Getty Images

Local people told CNN that security around the base had been tightened in recent days, with roadblocks at the entrance. But roads and lanes in the immediate area were still open.

The woman who called the police and one other local resident said that during previous conflicts, such as that against Iraq in 2003, there had been heavy security around the base.

But security since the Iran conflict began has been less evident, they said.

In March, the UK government gave the US Air Force permission to use Fairford to carry ⁠out strikes on Iranian missile sites used to attack ships in the Strait of Hormuz.

Days after the IRGC issued its threat against Fairford in July, Iranian media published a video of a group describing themselves as Iranian patriots at the perimeter fence of the base.

“This is RAF Fairford on British soil — the place where US military aircraft take off from these very runways to attack our people and our homeland,” one man says, with an Iranian flag hanging on the fence.

“We came to stand just a few meters from the nest of hostile aircraft and raise the proud flag of Iran,” the unidentified man says on the video.

A US Air Force spokesperson at Fairford – where the 501st ​Combat Support Wing is based – told CNN on Sunday: “For operational security reasons we will not discuss specific force protection measures.”

The unit “remains vigilant and will take appropriate actions to ensure the safety and security of our US service ⁠members, civilians, contractors, and their families,” the spokesperson said.

CNN’s James Frater contributed to this report.

World.title: Egypt launches public operations for 2nd phase of BRT project
World.content:
The Egyptian Transport Ministry announced the launch of public operations for the second phase of the Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) project, effective Saturday, September 26, covering the route from the Ain Sokhna Road station to the Sun Capital station.

This extends the BRT network from the intersection of the Ring Road and the Alexandria Agricultural Road to the Sun Capital station, establishing it as a key component of the modern mass transit system serving Greater Cairo.

Professor of road and port engineering, Abdullah Abu-Khadra, said during a phone interview with the Sada el Balad channel, that ticket prices have been set competitively: five Egyptian pounds for trips spanning between one and four stations, rising to LE35 for journeys covering 27-30 stations.

He added that the full journey across both phases spans approximately 75 kilometers, offering citizens an air-conditioned transport service with regular trips and fixed schedules, running from the Ring Road–Alexandria Agricultural Road intersection to the Sun Capital station.

Phase II Comprises 16 Stations

The second phase of BRT project spans approximately 40 kilometers and includes 16 stations; the total length of the system, once both phases are operational, will reach around 75 kilometers.

This new phase serves several vital areas and corridors across Greater Cairo—including Ain Sokhna Road, Maadi, Mokattam, al-Jazair, al-Imamain, al-Zahraa, al-Bahr al-A’zam, Omraniya, Talbiya, and Maryoutiya, extending to the Sun Capital area—with stations entering service successively in the coming period.

Abdullah Abu-Khadra, professor of road and port engineering, emphasized that the project represents a significant advancement in Greater Cairo’s mass transit system.

As a modern, organized, electric-powered mode of transport, the BRT system contributes to alleviating traffic congestion and reducing haphazard traffic movements on the Ring Road, Abu-Khadra said.

Integrated Transport System

The Sun Capital station is a key component of the integrated transport system.

Situated at the intersection of the Ring Road and Fayoum Road and spanning an area of ​​80,000 square meters, it facilitates the provision of comprehensive transport services for commuters traveling along the Fayoum Desert Road and the surrounding areas.

Abu-Khadra noted that the BRT system relies on interchange points that connect it with other modes of transport, enabling passengers to switch between different transport options during a single journey.

Prominent example of this integration is the Adly Mansour Station, which connects to Metro Line III and the Light Rail Transit (LRT), alongside other interchange points linking the BRT to various other modes of transportation.

Bridges, Tunnels, and Elevators

Passengers access and exit BRT stations via pedestrian bridges, tunnels, and elevators, ensuring safe and secure movement between the stations.

These measures are part of a plan to regulate traffic flow on the Ring Road, which includes prohibiting direct pedestrian crossings and eliminating informal microbus stops along the route, replacing them with a more organized transport system.

Edited translation from Al-Masry Al-Youm

World.title: Netanyahu made a secret visit to the UAE on Sunday, source says
World.content:
Jerusalem —

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu secretly visited the United Arab Emirates on Sunday and met with the country’s president, Sheikh Mohammed bin Zayed, an Israeli source familiar with the visit told CNN.

The source said Iran dominated the agenda, an arena where the two countries have deepened their cooperation, including during the current Iran war.

The Israeli Prime Minister’s Office did not confirm the visit. CNN reached out to the UAE foreign ministry for comment.

The rare trip, if confirmed, comes exactly one month before Israel’s October 27 election and against the backdrop of heightened political controversy in Israel over reporting by Haaretz and The New York Times alleging that Bin Zayed had warned Netanyahu of a major Hamas operation days before the October 7, 2023, attack.

The Atlantic separately reported that Egypt’s intelligence chief Abbas Kamel flew to Israel on September 26, 2023, to warn that Gaza would “blow up.” And on Sunday, The Wall Street Journal reported that there were at least three Egyptian warnings conveyed to Israel about Gaza, the last one in a phone call to Netanyahu, just days before the attack.

Netanyahu’s office has repeatedly denied receiving any warning and has dismissed the reports as fabricated lies aimed at damaging him electorally. But his rivals have used the allegations to make accountability for the failure to prevent the October 7, 2023, attack a central campaign issue.

People walk past a television channel  featuring Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, right, and his main rival, opposition candidate Gadi Eisenkot, ahead of Israel’s general election, in Ramat Gan, Israel, on Wednesday. Oded Balilty/AP

After initial reports of a warning from Bin Zayed, the UAE’s Foreign Ministry said earlier this month that it “does not comment on media stories or speculation regarding conversations between government leaders,” but it did not deny the call. “When necessary, all relevant intelligence has been and continues to be communicated between the relevant entities,” the statement said.

At the time, an Israeli source familiar with the matter said Netanyahu’s office tried to get the UAE to deny the report, but the UAE only agreed to issue a statement about intelligence sharing.

Netanyahu’s Likud party subsequently issued a statement, posted on the prime minister’s X account, alleging “blatant foreign interference” in Israel’s elections by UAE-based Palestinian politician Mohammed Dahlan. The party provided no evidence for the claim.

Netanyahu’s rivals, meanwhile, have seized on the reported warning to renew their attacks on his handling of the events preceding October 7.

Gadi Eizenkot, currently polling as the prime minister’s main challenger in Israel’s upcoming elections, said Saturday that the revelation about the warning “leaves no room for doubt: Netanyahu led, with blindness, arrogance and irresponsibility, the State of Israel to the greatest disaster in its history.”

In May, Netanyahu’s office said the prime minister had secretly visited the UAE in March, during the early days of the Iran war, calling it a “historic breakthrough.” The UAE foreign ministry, however, denied his claim at the time as “completely unfounded.”

During the war, Israel is also said to have deployed an Iron Dome missile defense system to the UAE and Israeli officials have said security cooperation between the two countries reached unprecedented levels.

Netanyahu has never made a publicly acknowledged official visit to the UAE.

World.title: AI agents promise to do everything for you. There may be a big wrinkle in that plan
World.content:
Meta wants its new Muse AI agent to be the gateway to users’ digital lives. But that all depends on whether popular apps and services are willing to give it the keys.

Agents go a step beyond how most people have used AI up to this point. Instead of simply answering questions, organizing emails and creating images, they can take multistep actions on the internet. They can compare prices, shop, book reservations and fill out forms, if the companies that sell things and take reservations allow them.

That change may spark a new battle over the future of internet services. Amazon recently blocked Muse’s AI agent from accessing its store, and some experts say the move could foreshadow a dilemma for online businesses.

If more people use AI agents for daily tasks, businesses may need to make a critical choice: Partner with companies like Meta and risk their own platforms possibly becoming irrelevant. Or potentially miss out on reaching billions of customers through what may be the future of how people get things done.

Shares of Airbnb, Expedia, and Trip Advisor fell around 5% last week after Meta announced new updates for its Muse agent.

Meta’s Muse makes waves

The idea of AI agents isn’t new; OpenAI, Google, Apple and Amazon, along with Meta, have been working towards this future for years and have gradually rolled out new agent-like features.

But Muse caught on almost immediately, shooting to the top of the free app chart on Apple’s App Store 10 days after its September 8 debut. Meta owns Instagram, Facebook and WhatsApp, and its pervasive internet presence — along with the app’s relatively easy interface — largely drove the AI agent’s success.

Meta launched an app for its AI agent, Muse, on September 8. The app rose to the top of the free app chart on Apple’s App Store 10 days after its debut. Samuel Boivin/NURPHO/AP

Compared to other tech giants, Meta has done a better job at showing Muse’s capabilities to consumers, according to Francisco Jeronimo, an analyst with technology market research firm International Data Corporation.

“Others have not been so vocal about using the agents to be able to shop as Meta has been with Muse, and I think that’s the main difference,” he said.

Meta has partnered with Walmart, GameStop, Sephora, Expedia, OpenTable and Shopify to incorporate their services into the Muse app. But e-commerce juggernaut Amazon refused to play ball with Meta. Amazon blocked the agent, saying it was not given notice or a choice about whether its store should be available through Muse.

The company also cited concerns around how Amazon account data and credentials would be handled, and said agents don’t offer Amazon’s personalized recommendations.

“We think it’s fairly straightforward that third-party applications that offer to make purchases on behalf of customers from other businesses should operate openly and respect service provider decisions about whether or not to participate,” Amazon said in a statement to CNN.

Online restaurant reservations platform Resy also told CNN that it “does not currently permit unapproved third-party bots or agents” to access its service. The platform locked a user’s account following attempts by his AI agent, a separate assistant called Instinct, to book hundreds of tables per hour earlier this month.

“Unapproved automated activity can introduce risks to the platform and compromise a fair reservation experience for diners,” the company said.

CNN was able to book a reservation through Muse after providing login information, like a phone number and confirmation code. Resy integrates with ChatGPT and Claude and said it will “continue to evaluate opportunities” as AI agents progress.

Risks and rewards of agents

Amazon may be an outlier. But some experts say AI agents pose real risks that could give many online service providers some pause before allowing agents to use their platforms.

For one, there’s the potential decrease in web traffic if tasks are primarily handled on the AI agent apps. Brands could also lose the ability to learn about customer shopping habits or further entice users into additional purchases with in-app promotions or product recommendations.

“You browse Amazon for that thing that you’re looking for, but then you also see other things that you know you may end up buying,” said Mandeep Singh, a senior industry analyst for Bloomberg Intelligence.

Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg speaks during the Meta Connect event September 23. Jeff Chiu/AP

Additionally, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg said Wednesday that the company eventually plans to charge a commission for transactions made through Muse. This means other companies may lose a cut of their sales.

And it’s not just shopping and reservation apps that may be impacted. AI agents are generally good at tasks that require research, like comparing insurance policies or mobile carrier plans. This could potentially make it easier for users to switch plans to land a better deal.

But the upside could also be huge. Muse has already been downloaded more than 2.5 million times, according to market intelligence firm Sensor Tower, giving businesses visibility to millions of people around the world. That could make Muse especially appealing to smaller and mid-sized brands, like those who work with Shopify.

That was part of the appeal for travel platform Expedia, which chose to allow AI agents because it wants “to show up wherever travelers are searching,” Kathryn Heinz, Expedia’s vice president of enterprise alliances and AI, said in a comment to CNN. She added that about two-thirds of Expedia’s traffic comes through its own platforms.

And some might see it as a move to future-proof their business.

“I think long term, that’s exactly what we will see: the AI platforms to become the layer and the main interface for most of us when we are when we are shopping,” International Data Corporation’s Jeronimo said.

World.title: Inside the Trump campaign strategy to reverse Republicans’ dwindling hopes of winning the midterms
World.content:
The midterms mood among Donald Trump’s inner circle has soured as GOP candidates openly break with the president and his approval ratings hit an all-time low, prompting a largely unspoken but age-old question: How does an unpopular president best help his party keep control of Congress?

Trump advisers have privately acknowledged that there’s little expectation he can win over large numbers of independents and swing voters, which was part of his path to victory in critical states in 2024. And while they’re more concerned about losing control of the House, Republicans’ previous confidence that they can hold onto the Senate is dwindling by the day.

“It’s obviously going to be f***ing rough,” one Trump adviser told CNN, adding that they believe the best-case scenario is achieving what Democrats did in 2022, when under former President Joe Biden they narrowly lost control of the House but kept the Senate.

Still, Trump’s team is planning an aggressive campaign schedule for Trump and Vice President JD Vance in October in both battleground and deep-red states alike, multiple officials told CNN — as advisers believe their only hope at holding ground is increasing turnout, and the president can help with that.

“The system is built around what areas we need to goose turnout 2-3 points,” one operative told CNN.

In recent weeks, Trump’s senior advisers, including chief of staff Susie Wiles, put together a calendar that has Trump on the campaign trail for most days in October, though two administration officials said that not all stops had been confirmed. He is planning trips to Alabama and Oklahoma next week, but a GOP official said those were “outliers” in the travel strategy, which would focus more on battleground districts.

“He’ll be playing hard in Florida, Texas, Michigan and Ohio — he’ll be on the road just about every day in October campaigning. We’re leaving it all on the table,” the official added. However, even in more purple states, the plan is for Trump to go to more conservative areas, according to another official.

Advisers also hope the Trump-Vance campaigning will help raise money as Republican groups — including Trump’s MAGA Inc. PAC — have begun hemorrhaging cash across the country. This week, the Senate Leadership Fund increased its spending in Texas to $100 million to support GOP Senate candidate Ken Paxton in a state they haven’t lost in decades, exposing the party’s fresh worries about the Senate.

And while one Republican operative said that the enormous sum was moving the needle in their direction “some,” it wasn’t clear it would be enough to reverse the strong political headwinds largely created by the president himself.

Asked if there was anything Republicans could do to change the tide, the operative replied: “Go back in time and never start the war with Iran.”

Running away from Trump

Republicans in both purple territories and even some red districts have broken from Trump on issues ranging from the Iran War to the economy to immigration. Republican Mike Rogers, the Michigan Senate candidate in one of the most closely watched races this cycle, lamented in a recent ad that “Groceries cost too much. We have to bring prices down.”

“The war with Iran needs to end and end quickly,” Rogers said. “When it does, energy costs will plummet, but Michigan families can’t afford to wait for that to happen.”

That sentiment was echoed by the GOP’s Senate candidates in Iowa and Ohio. Other Republican lawmakers have voted to limit Trump’s war powers. House lawmakers in Florida and Texas have also criticized the administration on immigration. Several others have removed Trump references from campaign websites.

The GOP official involved in strategy brushed off concerns about candidates distancing from the president, saying “they need to run the races they need to run, and we’re obviously encouraging them to do what they need to do.”

In a sign of how potentially polarizing the president and his MAGA brand are right now, much of the money being spent by Trump’s PAC is coming through two newly formed groups with far less politically aligned names: No Going Back PAC Inc. and Safety & Affordability PAC Inc.

However, Trump’s political team still believes that his ability to drive turnout is one of Republicans’ greatest assets come November. While some Republicans have quietly expressed concerns about candidates in sensitive races appearing alongside Trump, one official brushed off the notion.

“The cake is already baked. There’s no getting away from Trump for these guys. So we have to lean into it,” the official said. “The left is going to attack [Republican candidates] as being close to Trump no matter what, so why not get the benefit out of it, which is max turnout.”

Trump’s midterms catch-22

Multiple sources working on midterm strategy told CNN that Trump’s political operation was working off that central belief — that they could still win with enough turnout. In order to minimize the percent of “persuadable” voters that are needed, their thinking goes, it’s critical to get as many base voters to the polls as possible.

“It’s all a turnout game,” a GOP campaign official said. “From day one, the campaign committees and the president’s political operation have been sharing data to make sure we’re hammering the exact people we need to turn out.”

A voter cast a ballot on the first day of early voting in Minnesota on September 18 in Minneapolis. Ellen Schmidt/AP

Sources noted that while this was not the traditional way to look at a midterm when a president’s approval ratings are so low, Trump has always been a different political animal who defies typical expectations.

But his advisers also privately acknowledge a major problem with that strategy: Trump isn’t just an incredible driver of enthusiasm for his own supporters; he’s also a strong driver of Democratic turnout.

“The issue with putting his name on the ballot is it could ultimately serve as a bigger driving force for Democratic voters who hate him,” the campaign official said.

White House spokesperson Davis Ingle said in a statement that Trump has “built one of the most robust coalitions in political history” and “the President understands how to communicate with them.”

“President Trump is the unequivocal leader, best messenger, and unmatched motivator for the Republican Party, and he is committed to maintaining Republican majorities in Congress,” Ingle added.

Deploying Vance

The White House and the president’s political apparatus view Vance as a crucial surrogate, and one that tends to stay far more on message compared to the president. But the campaign doesn’t exactly view him as an ace card to deploy in truly competitive territories — he’s still viewed as an extension of Trump. Both men are seen as potentially doing more damage than good in certain swing districts, sources familiar with the discussions tell CNN.

The decision of where and when to send both men is driven directly by the massive data operation that the president’s political team has amassed, one that was fortified during Trump’s 2024 campaign and is now also being used by the Republican National Committee and the GOP’s House and Senate campaign arms. James Blair, who left the White House to take charge of the political operation ahead of the midterms, has been weighing in on the calendars.

Vance, who has met directly with GOP lawmakers and candidates on the ballot in November to help them workshop messaging, has also been tasked with raising so-called “hard money” for the Republican National Committee.

“JD’s primary responsibility has been fundraising,” one source told CNN, nodding to Vance’s role as the RNC’s finance chair. The source described that as an urgent necessity, particularly given the Supreme Court’s ruling earlier this month allowing political party committees, like the RNC, to get discounted television ad rates ahead of the midterm elections.

Vance isn’t the only surrogate the White House has deployed — senior staffers have also worked directly with Wiles to pick campaign stops and priorities for members of Trump’s Cabinet. In fact, Trump’s political team has tracked and ranked Cabinet officials’ campaign involvement, with higher points for traveling to swing districts and subtractions for overseas trips.

The rankings have been shared with officials in group settings in hopes it would incentivize more campaign involvement, according to multiple sources familiar with the matter. During a summer meeting at the Waldorf Astoria in Washington, Blair credited Small Business Administrator Kelly Loeffler as leading the pack, with Acting Secretary of Labor Keith Sonderling in second, sources present at the meeting said.

World.title: Huthi missiles threaten civil aviation over Red Sea, warns Yemen’s Information Minister
World.content:
Yemeni Information Minister Moammar al-Eryani warned civil aviation authorities and international airlines of the Huthi group’s use of Iranian air defense weapons that have been converted into cruise missiles.

This threat could extend to international flight paths in southern Red Sea, he stressed, coinciding with escalating confrontations on the ground and the Yemeni leadership’s declaration of “general mobilization and national call to arms” against the group.

He said that the gravity of the alarming development revealed by the Yemeni army lies not only in the nature of the weapons used but also in their launch sites, particularly as they are being directed from Huthi-controlled areas toward international air corridors.

The minister recalled the 2020 downing of Ukrainian flight PS752 in Tehran—which claimed 176 lives—and called upon the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO), aviation safety authorities, and airlines to incorporate this new development into their risk assessments for regional flight paths and to take action before an “aviation disaster” occurs.

The Yemeni Armed Forces had previously announced the detection of Huthi use of Iranian air defense weapons—reportedly converted into cruise missiles—launched from al-Hudaydah Governorate toward international flight paths in the southern Red Sea.

The Yemeni Armed Forces spokesperson Majed al-Nuzaili said that the Huthis employed these weapons using “innovative techniques and tactics,” noting that the missile is capable of loitering for up to 25 minutes and utilizes heat-seeking technology to target heat sources.

He added that these weapons, according to Yemeni army intelligence, lack the ability to distinguish between military and civilian targets; consequently, launching them along international flight paths poses a threat to civilian aircraft and passengers, as well as to planes operated by the United Nations and humanitarian and relief organizations.

Nuzaili called on the ICAO and the International Air Transport Association IATA to take the necessary measures to address potential risks.

These warnings come amidst escalating military tensions, following the announcement by the Coalition to Support Legitimacy that it had intercepted and destroyed two drones launched by the Houthis toward the Riyadh area, as well as a ballistic missile aimed at Khamis Mushait, in Saudi Arabia, according to Coalition spokesman Brigadier General Turki Al-Maliki.

The Huthis announced that a bridge in al-Makhadir district of Ibb Governorate had been struck by Saudi airstrikes.

The Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) states called on the international community to adopt a firm stance to put an end to the repeated terrorist attacks by the Huthis against Saudi Arabia.

General mobilization

In a speech marking the 64th anniversary of the September 26, 1962 Revolution, Rashad al-Alimi, Chairman of the Presidential Leadership Council, called for “general mobilization and a national call to arms.”

He urged Yemenis to rally behind the armed forces and security services and to join their ranks through official channels, with the aim of “restoring state institutions and extending sovereignty over all Yemeni territory, all the way to Sana’a.”

Alimi announced an opening for a safe return to the fold of the Republic and constitutional legitimacy, pledging a comprehensive amnesty—in accordance with constitutional and legal procedures—for anyone who abandons the Huthis and ceases fighting or working on their behalf.

He also promised to regularize the status of military and security personnel and preserve their legally acquired employment rights.

World.title: Sisi moves to delegate certain Presidential powers to Defense Minister – here’s what that means
World.content:
The former Director of the National Defense College, Mohamed al-Ghabbary explained President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi’s decision to delegate certain Presidential powers —as stipulated in the General Mobilization Law—to the Minister of Defense and Military Production.

During a phone-in to the program “Ala Massoulity” (On My Responsibility) on the Sada al-Balad channel, Ghabbary said that the decision is a routine legal and administrative measure that recurs whenever a new Minister of Defense assumes office.

The Official Gazette published the presidential decree, issued on September 22, delegating the Minister of Defense and Military Production to exercise the powers stipulated in Articles 9, 12, and 24 of Law #87 of 1960 for a period of one year, with the decision to take effect on November.

Routine Procedure

Ghabbary noted that the delegation is not a new decision linked to an emergency situation, but rather a routine procedure that repeats with the change of the Minister of Defense.

He explained that the President, in his capacity as head of the National Defense Council, delegates specific powers to the Minister of Defense in accordance with legal provisions.

Ghabbary added that the Minister of Defense undertakes this task alongside his primary duties, given that the administrative aspect of implementing mobilization measures is linked to the entity he heads.

He stressed that the decision does not signal a change in the state of general mobilization, explaining that a mobilization plan is already in place, and that the call-up of reservists or the reinforcement of units is linked to training exercises and operations conducted by the armed forces.

What is general mobilization?

Ghabbary explained that military organization relies on both active-duty and reserve forces, and that mobilization is the mechanism used to bring the armed forces up to the required strength.

He noted that an army’s peacetime force typically ranges between 50-70 percent, depending on the specific country and its arrangements, whereas mobilization serves to bring that force up to the required level—a process applicable to both peacetime and wartime scenarios.

Peacetime mobilization is linked to continuous training, he said, as certain units require their personnel force to be fully staffed while conducting exercises and training maneuvers.

Not a Declaration of War

Linking the authorization decision to regional conditions has raised concerns, he said, noting that he had received inquiries from people both inside and outside Egypt asking if the decision meant the country was heading toward war.

A state of war is preceded by other measures, including the declaration of a state of emergency and the implementation of a strategic state initiative, he explained.

Ghabbary affirmed that the current decision constitutes neither a declaration of war nor a declaration of a state of emergency, explaining that it is a routine legal procedure.

Citizens have the right to ask such questions and that it is the role of specialists to clarify the nature and rationale of the decision, he affirmed.

Civilian Resources

The former head of the Central Agency for Public Mobilization and Statistics (CAPMAS), Abu Bakr al-Gendy, explained that the general mobilization system is not limited to the armed forces and their personnel.

It also encompasses an inventory of the state’s civilian resources, allowing them to be utilized in accordance with specific needs and governing regulations, he said.

Gendy said that the events of 2011—accompanied by unrest, chaos, and the disruption of certain transport services—demonstrated the practical importance of this system. At the time, the state was able to leverage available resources to respond rapidly, he said.

Gendy cited the transport of wheat supplies to various governorates—following disruptions to transport networks—as a prime example; the armed forces intervened using their own transport assets, successfully moving and distributing the wheat within a short timeframe.

He added that a decision was issued at the time to deploy transport vehicles to move quantities of wheat from areas such as Alexandria and Suez to other governorates, thereby facilitating the delivery of supplies to citizens within a short timeframe.

Wheat and food supplies were transported across governorates and heavily secured following the events of 2011. he noted.

Gendy emphasized that the successful handling of those circumstances was linked to the existence of a database and a prior inventory of civilian capabilities; this enabled the state to act swiftly without having to start from scratch to assess resources during the crisis.

Edited translation from Al-Masry Al-Youm

World.title: Liberia: Lawyers for the former Vice President Say Arrest, Detention, Prison and Search Breached Constitution as Bail Fight Heads to Appeal
World.content:
MONROVIA – When the Monrovia City Court issued a writ on August 25, 2026, commanding police to “arrest the living bodies” of Jewel Howard-Taylor, it set in motion one of the most consequential criminal cases against a former senior official in Liberia’s recent history.

By Rodney D. Sieh

A month later, the former Vice President sits under house arrest, her bail application denied, her phones and computers seized, and her lawyers argue that nearly every step the State has taken against her has run afoul of the Constitution.



In a formal statement, her legal team lists what it calls a “cumulative constitutional injury”: ten separate points at which, they contend, Mrs. Howard-Taylor’s liberty was taken or restricted without full regard to the safeguards in Article 21 of the 1986 Constitution.

The allegations against her remain unproven, and so do her lawyers’ claims. Both will ultimately be tested in court.

WHAT THE STATE ALLEGES

The writ of arrest, obtained by FrontPageAfrica, lays out the government’s case in stark terms.

According to the writ, businessman Sheik Bashiru Kante brought two foreign nationals, Taras Zadereiko, alias “Tony,” and Mihovil Vrovac, alias “Michael,” to Liberia in 2021, where they allegedly conspired to import and export cocaine through Liberia to Europe.

The State claims the group set out to recruit top government officials to protect the scheme, and that in 2022 Kante introduced the two men to Mrs. Howard-Taylor, then Vice President.

The writ alleges that in early 2022 she met the men at her Sophie residence in Congo Town, and that they invited her to Dubai to meet Croatian national Nikola Ivancic, whom the government describes as a drug kingpin and ringleader of the cartel. There, prosecutors claim, a meeting was held about using Liberia as a transit point for cocaine, and she agreed.

The State further alleges she received US$45,000 from Ivancic in Dubai “for shopping,” later requested and received US$75,000 from the cartel through Kante, and subsequently received a further US$15,000.

She is charged under the Controlled Drugs and Substances Act of 2023, the New Penal Law and the AML-CFT Act of 2021, with offenses including importation and exportation of controlled drugs, illicit trafficking, criminal conspiracy, criminal facilitation and criminal solicitation.

THE DEFENSE’S TEN COUNTS

Her lawyers do not address the merits of those allegations in their statement. Instead, they focus on process, and they list ten grievances:

1. Arrest without presentation of a writ of arrest

2. No demonstrated completed investigation to justify the initial deprivation of liberty

3. Incarceration beyond 48 hours

4. Failure to formally charge and present her before a court within 48 hours

5. Absence of an indictment at the relevant stage

6. Incarceration at the Monrovia Central Prison while unconvicted

7. Treatment inconsistent with the distinction between an accused and a convicted prisoner

8. House arrest and substantial restrictions on movement

9. Continued pretrial deprivation of liberty

10. Denial of bail despite the passage of several years since the alleged conduct

“An accusation is not a conviction,” the statement declares.

THE 48-HOUR RULE

At the center of the defense argument is Article 21 of the Constitution, which requires that anyone arrested be formally charged and presented before a court of competent jurisdiction within 48 hours.

The legal team contends the records show Mrs. Howard-Taylor was held beyond that window before the required judicial process was completed. If that chronology holds up, it would be among the most straightforward constitutional questions in the case: the 48-hour rule is not discretionary.

The lawyers are careful to concede the State’s right to investigate. “The issue is not whether the State has authority to investigate alleged criminal conduct. It does,” the statement says. “The issue is whether that authority was exercised within the constitutional limits.”

‘WHILE UNDERGOING INVESTIGATION’

The defense’s second count, that no completed investigation justified her detention, finds an unexpected echo in the government’s own paperwork.

A court interim order dated September 22, 2026, signed on the directive of Judge Ousman F. Feika of Criminal Court “C,” describes Mrs. Howard-Taylor as “currently being detained while undergoing investigation by National Joint Security authorities.”

That language, a month after the arrest writ was issued, suggests the investigation was still underway while she was held. The lawyers argue that an ongoing investigation does not by itself justify continued detention, particularly under a Constitution that expressly bars preventive detention.

FROM CENTRAL PRISON TO HOUSE ARREST

The former Vice President’s journey from arrest to the Monrovia Central Prison and then to house arrest forms another pillar of the defense case.

Her lawyers argue the Constitution protects accused persons from being treated as convicted prisoners, and that housing an unconvicted former Vice President at the country’s main penitentiary raises questions about both the legal basis for her confinement and the conditions she faced.

The later move to house arrest, they argue, is itself a restriction on constitutionally protected freedom of movement, one that must rest on a clear court order and a lawful basis.

THE SEARCH: ‘ALL TELEPHONES, MOBILE PHONES’

Perhaps the most concrete dispute concerns the search of her home.

The September 22 interim order directed the Sheriff of Criminal Court “C” to “immediately move into” her residence, conduct a “comprehensive inspection,” and seize “all telephones, mobile phones, communication gadgets and/or devices” found on the premises or in her possession, then produce an inventory.

The order was served on one of her lawyers at 6:27 p.m. that Tuesday.

According to the defense, officers removed a desktop computer, a printer, an internet connection device, and several mobile phones reportedly belonging to other people, along with other electronics.

The breadth of the order is likely to be contested. It covers every device “found in the premises,” not only those belonging to the accused. The Constitution requires search warrants to specifically identify the place to be searched and the objects sought. Whether an order to seize every phone in a house, regardless of owner, meets that standard is a question the courts may be asked to settle.

“What was the legal basis for taking property belonging to persons other than the accused?” the lawyers ask.

THE BAIL BATTLE

The bail question may prove decisive. Article 21 of the Constitution provides that accused persons shall be bailable on recognizance or sufficient sureties, except for capital offenses or grave offenses as defined by law, and prohibits excessive bail.

Mrs. Howard-Taylor’s bail application was denied at trial level. Her lawyers have excepted to the ruling and are pursuing an appeal.

‘EACH OFFENSE STANDS ON ITS OWN STATUTE’

The defense’s sharpest bail argument centers on the money laundering count.

Attorney Gbawou Kowou, a prominent Liberian lawyer, criminal justice professor and former law enforcement official who represents the former Vice President, argues that money laundering under Section 15.2.1 of the AML/CFT Act of 2021 is not classified as a capital, grave or non-bailable offense. The statute, he notes, expressly makes money laundering a first-degree felony without designating it as grave or non-bailable.

In his view, the presence of drug charges in the same writ should not automatically make the separate money laundering allegation non-bailable. “The bailability of each offense should be determined according to the specific statute creating and classifying that offense,” Kowou said.

Unless the government can point to a specific provision of law making money laundering itself a grave or non-bailable offense, the defense will argue that the count remains subject to the constitutional and statutory right to bail.

The argument puts the burden squarely on the State. It forces prosecutors to show, statute by statute, the legal basis for denying bail, rather than relying on the overall gravity of the case.

THE STATE’S LIKELY ANSWER
