World.title: SpaceX launches supersized Starship into orbit
World.content:
Starship is the biggest and most powerful spacecraft ever built and it is meant to support NASA's Artemis moon program.

US airspace giant SpaceX on Monday launched its Starship spacecraft into orbit. The firm hoped the Starship could complete six full laps around Earth in order to prove its readiness for NASA's Artemis moon program.

"Starship is orbital," Mission Control announced to cheers. The Launch took place at Starbase, Texas. The laps were supposed to last around 10 hours, ending with a Pacific splashdown near Chile.

But just an hour after liftoff, SpaceX said it planned to bring Starship back to Earth after about three hours in orbit, cutting the 10-hour trip short.

Starship launches 26 satellites

NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman praised SpaceX for reaching orbit and "managing every step in a safe, responsible and especially inspirational way."

Starship is the biggest and most powerful spacecraft ever built, it was propelled by a 407-foot (124-meter) rocket that was designed from the start to be fully reusable.

The spacecraft was loaded with 26 of the latest and most advanced Starlink satellites, which were released one by one, to join the 11,000 older models already providing internet service.

"All 26 Starlink V3 operational satellites deployed and operating nominally," SpaceX CEO ElonMusk wrote on X.

SpaceX's so-called V3 satellites are designed to unfold their antennas and solar panels after release before establishing connections with Earth and other Starlink satellites.

SpaceX began flying Starship in 2023 and the program has seen its successes and failures of successive tests. Technical challenges remain before Starship can fulfill its mandates, such as conduct commercial flights, deploy data centers in orbit or reach the Moon or the Red Planet.

World.title: Turkey: Comedian convicted for 'insulting' Erdogan in show
World.content:
Deniz Goktas was convicted of two of three charges, including "insulting" the president, but was released pending the appeal process. Nominally, Turkey is a secular country with free speech.

A Turkish comedian was convicted in Istanbul on Monday on charges of "insulting" President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and "insulting religious values" during a stand-up performance in June.

The judge provisionally sentenced Deniz Goktas to 19 months in prison, but ordered his release pending the judicial review and appeal process that would finalized the verdict.

It was not immediately clear how long this process might take.

NATO member and EU aspirant Turkey routinely tries people on speech-related offenses, particularly and famously when it comes to supposed "insults" of its longserving leader Erdogan.

What was the case about?

Deniz Goktas, 32, was arrested on July 3, a week after releasing a YouTube video of his show that was watched nearly 9 million times and a few days after shorter clips he posted on X enjoyed similar rapid success.

He faced an array of charges related to content in his "Dead Sea" show. Goktas referred to his impending court appointment online on Sunday, in one of his irreverent social media posts from his cell.

Goktas was accused of insulting Erdogan, of inciting public hatred and hostility — via jokes about Islam — and of praising crime and criminals, an additional charge added by prosecutors tied to a joke about an organized crime family, the Daltons

His trial is the latest in a widening crackdown on people seen as critical of Turkey's moderate Islamist government. Hundreds of politicians, artists, musicians, journalists and LGBTQ activists are among those to face detention or trial.

LGBTQ+ communities in Turkey fear intensifying clampdown To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

What did Goktas say in his defense in court?

Goktas did not dispute the content from his popular show, but did argue in court that he had committed no crimes with his jokes.

Prosecutors had for instance singled out a pair of references he made to President Erdogan as a "dictator" as illegal insults.

"Dictator is not an insult: it is a political characterization," Goktas told the court. "As the president and leader of the party that has ruled the country for 25 years, a political comedy show in which Erdogan's name is never mentioned would be neither sincere nor have any connection to reality."

He said that Erdogan should be "open to the art of satire," as he said past presidents in Turkish democracy were.

"The joke hasn't changed. What has changed is the increasingly fragile leadership that can no longer tolerate the joke," he said.

The judge nevertheless convicted Gotkas of insulting Erdogan, and downgraded the charge he faced of "inciting hatred and hostility" with jokes about Islam, instead convicting him of the lesser supposed crime of "insulting religious values."

He cleared the comedian of the third charge of allegedly praising criminality.

Goktas has spent just under three months in pretrial detention, which should count as time served in any potential custodial sentence.

News of Goktas' arrest in early July prompted protest in Istanbul [FILE: July 3, 2026] Image: Yasin Akgul/AFP

Erdogan the only claimant, Diyanet religious authority among those to complain

According to the Turkish NGO the Media and Law Studies Association (MLSA) , prosecutors cited more than 500 applications to prosecute the performer regarding the show.

They were issued to the Presidential Communication Center that monitors such issues. One of the groups to provide a tipoff was the government-sponsored Presidency of Religious affairs, better known as Diyanet.

Erdogan, in charge of Turkey either as prime minister or later president since 2003, was named as the sole complainant.

His government has attracted attention in recent years for its prosecution of people deemed to have unfairly criticized the authorities, and for the various lawsuits against leading members of the opposition, particularly the CHP. The Turkish president's litigious streak also became headline news in Germany around a decade ago, when he pursued star TV comedian Jan Böhmermann.

Meanwhile the MLSA said that Goktas' jokes alleged to have the potential to "publicly incite hatred and hostility" took aim at fundamentalist Islam, including a reference to women in full-coverage swimsuits being "divers" and joking about "suicide bombers who fast."

Turkey nominally has a secular constitution and guarantees of free speech. However, the EU and the US have often criticized its application of these standards.

The US Commission on International Religious Freedom wrote in a 2022 report that Erdogan's government increasingly relied on speech-based prosecution to "silence individuals who express criticism in religious terms, disclose beliefs or a lack thereof that differ from those of the majority of the population, or engage with religion in a way perceived as 'mocking' or 'irreverent.'"

Edited by: Elizabeth Schumacher

World.title: What do Manchester City's charges mean for German football?
World.content:
Manchester City have reportedly been found guilty of major financial rule breaches. What does this mean for German football?

What has happened to Manchester City?

Manchester City have reportedly been found guilty on 114 of the 115 Premier League charges over alleged breaches of financial regulations. They relate to a period between 2009 to 2018 and include allegations around financial reporting, disclosure of player and manager payments, compliance with UEFA and Premier League financial rules, and cooperation with the investigation. The Premier League has yet to comment, with the news having first been reported by The Athletic.

The process started when the charges were brought in February 2023. The review was started in 2024 before the reported verdict of guilty on almost all charges arrived on September 25, 2026.

The English champions, owned in practice by the United Arab Emirates' ruling family, deny all charges and insist their case is supported by a "comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence."

Has this happened before?

The Premier League has long had a reputation for rampant capitalism, but it has started to enforce financial regulations that control spending in recent years.

In 2026, Chelsea were fined €11.6 million ($13.8 million) and given a suspended ban from registering new players for two transfer windows for breaching rules relating to payments to agents between 2009 and 2022. The club did avoid a six-point deduction though. In the recent years before, Everton and Nottingham Forest were docked Premier League points for breaking profit and sustainability rules (PSR).

City previously won, for the most part, a similar battle with UEFA. The 2023 UEFA Champions League winners were hit with a huge fine by UEFA in 2014 over a breach of the organization's FFP (Financial Fair Play) rules. Then, in February 2020, UEFA handed City a €30-million fine and banned the club from competing in the Champions League for two years for falsely inflating sponsorship revenues between 2012 and 2016. But in July of the same year, the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) overturned the ban and reduced the fine to €10 million. City denied all charges and did not miss a game in Europe's premier club competition.

The key difference in City's current case to Chelsea's earlier in the year is that Chelsea self-reported and admitted guilt, which allowed them to negotiate with the Premier League over the sanction. City have stressed that they are innocent throughout.

Has something like this happened in Germany before?

German football is by no means immune to scandals or corruption. The most prominent examples are the 1971 match-fixing scandal in which players took bribes to throw matches, and the 2005 match-fixing scandal involving referee Robert Hoyzer, who confessed to fixing and betting on matches in the second division and German Cup.

The majority of financial breaches have come from clubs not being able to prove they were financially viable. Both 1860 Munich and Uerdingen are examples of this, but major systematic abuses or breaches have not happened because the structure of German football is designed to prevent it.

The 50+1 rule: What is it? To play this audio please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 audio

Why is something like this not possible in Germany?

Mainly because of the 50+1 rule. In place since 1999, the rule stipulates that the parent club, for example Bayern Munich, must hold at least 50% plus one vote in its spun-off professional football company – in this case, FC Bayern München Fußball AG. This ensures that the majority of voting rights always lie with the club and its members.

The rule prevents external investors from taking complete control of a club and managing it solely according to financial criteria. It is also meant to ensure a certain level of equality, as it is not possible for a club to invest disproportionately more money than other clubs thanks to its powerful investor with a controlling stake.

The vast majority of organized fans in Germany oppose the commercialization of football. The 50+1 rule makes many fans in Germany not just paying spectators but active club members who can, for example, have a say inimportant club decisions.

Critics argue that the rule puts German football clubs at a financial disadvantage. Spending in the Premier League proves that to be true, but City's reported offenses are also proof of why the league's sustainable structure matters. The Bundesliga has been approached by DW for comment.

Do these charges have an impact in Germany?

Not until the ruling and punishment are final. However, one of the main talking points is what City's success prevented other teams from claiming, whether it be prize money, Champions League places or transfer opportunities. These are compensatory claims that might be explored should the charges remain after appeals.

Reforming English football To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

What happens next?

Manchester City face possible points deductions, expulsion, financial penalties or the stripping of their titles. It is unclear when the decision on what the punishment will be will come, especially given that City are expected to appeal.

The outcome also has significant impacts for the Premier League. In taking on one of its biggest clubs, having successfully punished two smaller ones, they risk appearing toothless. Certainly the eyes of European football will be on them as the impact of the decision will put the integrity of the competition into focus.

It may also see more English fans call for a model like the 50+1 rule to be integrated. Some voices were raised in England after the Saudi sovereign wealth fund PIF took over Premier League club Newcastle United in 2021, and others continued during the attempted establishment of a European Super League in 2021.

Edited by: Chuck Penfold

World.title: Ciberseguridad: el socio que toda pyme debe tener
World.content:
Las pequeñas y medianas empresas están expuestas a ataques cada vez más sofisticados con los que los ciberdelincuentes acceden a los sistemas para robar datos y dinero. Pero se puede reducir el impacto de muchos de estos incidentes o directamente evitarse si la empresa está preparada y los empleados saben cómo actuar

La era digital permite a las pequeñas y medianas empresas desempeñarse con una agilidad nunca vista y ser más eficientes y productivas. Un mundo de ventajas en el que también se cuelan los ciberdelincuentes. Ya no hay que forzar una cerradura de madrugada para entrar en un negocio; basta con enviar un SMS o hacer una llamada y que el empresario o el empleado confiado haga clic donde no debía para que los ladrones accedan al corazón informático de la empresa.

Las pymes también son objetivo de los ciberdelincuentes, asegura Alfredo Díez, coordinador del grupo de trabajo de ciberseguridad de la Confederación Española de Organizaciones Empresariales (CEOE). Y resultan, en muchos casos, más vulnerables que las grandes compañías: suelen carecer de personal especializado y trabajan con menos recursos. “Incluso en el caso de las microempresas y los autónomos, en ocasiones, el propio empresario tiene un único dispositivo para uso personal y profesional, lo que aumenta el riesgo”, advierte el experto.

Díez considera que es especialmente importante que este colectivo, el mayor del tejido empresarial español (el 99,8%), preste atención a la ciberseguridad para la supervivencia de su negocio y que, sobre todo, invierta en ello y dedique una partida de sus presupuestos a blindarlo digitalmente. Especialmente, continúa Díez, en este momento en el que la inteligencia artificial (IA) multiplica la efectividad de los ataques. “Hasta ahora, la mayoría de los ataques podían ser masivos e indiscriminados, pero ahora se crean estafas a medida para cada empresa o para cada empleado con mucha más facilidad. La IA permite personalizar y escalar ataques dirigidos que antes requerían mucho más tiempo y trabajo”, advierte el coordinador de CEOE.

La inteligencia artificial (IA) permite a los atacantes crear esos mensajes más personalizados y creíbles, que imitan el tono profesional de cada sector y eliminan señales que antes los delataban, como las faltas de ortografía o una personalización defectuosa. Incluso pueden traducir sus comunicaciones a varios idiomas, o suplantar mediante voz e imagen a algún miembro de la empresa para llevar a cabo su estafa. La IA también les da la posibilidad de recabar información de sus objetivos con mayor rapidez, como conocer la situación por la que pasa y adaptar su ataque.

Una empresa ciberresiliente

Las pymes que priorizan la ciberseguridad cuentan con una ventaja respecto a las demás. El daño económico es una de las principales consecuencias de un ataque, pero no es la única. A él se puede sumar la pérdida de reputación y de confianza por parte de los clientes, cuyos datos, en ocasiones, también se ven expuestos. Recuperar el prestigio suele requerir tiempo y esfuerzo. Hoy, las grandes empresas tienen en cuenta la seguridad a la hora de elegir proveedores en su cadena de suministro, por eso, la defensa digital no es solo protección, también es un factor de competitividad. Una pyme fiable es más sólida y presenta más garantías a la hora de contar con sus servicios.

En este contenido repasamos los principales ataques a los que hoy están expuestas este tipo de compañías y qué pueden hacer empresarios y trabajadores para no caer en ellos, porque hoy, señala Jesús Cristóbal, profesor de IA y análisis de datos de OBS Business School, la cuestión no es asumir que nunca ocurrirá, sino estar preparados si ocurre.

Cuando el ataque empieza con un mensaje, el ‘phishing’

La suplantación de identidad es una de las amenazas más habituales para las pymes. Puede llegar por correo electrónico, SMS, llamada o incluso videollamada, haciéndose pasar por un banco, un proveedor, un cliente o un miembro de la propia empresa. El phishing, especialmente a través del correo electrónico, sigue siendo una de las vías más utilizadas. Los ciberdelincuentes imitan comunicaciones legítimas y recurren a pretextos como una incidencia con la cuenta bancaria, el acceso al correo o los servicios en la nube para provocar una reacción rápida. El objetivo suele ser que la víctima haga clic en un enlace, facilite sus credenciales o abra la puerta a un acceso no autorizado.

El fraude guiado que utiliza varios métodos de comunicación para convencer a la víctima es cada vez más común precisamente por su efectividad. Los estafadores envían un mensaje en el que avisan de un problema que se debe solucionar llamando a un número de teléfono que indican. A partir de ahí guían a la víctima para conseguir sus propósitos.

Ejemplo de correo fraudulento Fuente: Instituto Nacional de Ciberseguridad (Incibe)

En algunos casos, el phishing también se utiliza para instalar programas maliciosos (malware) en los equipos o sistemas de la víctima. Su propósito es infiltrarse con fines fraudulentos: robar información, espiar la actividad del usuario y la empresa o dañar los equipos para aprovechar sus vulnerabilidades. En un ataque de ransomware, los delincuentes pueden cifrar los sistemas para impedir su uso y exigir un rescate para recuperarlos. En otros casos, además, roban información y amenazan con publicarla.

El ransomware puede tener graves consecuencias para una pyme, señala Jesús Cristóbal, profesor de análisis de datos e IA en OBS Business School. Paraliza la actividad de la empresa, puede exponer sus datos privados y generar posibles sanciones por la filtración de información de clientes. Genera pérdidas económicas y un daño reputacional del que cuesta mucho recuperarse.

Cuando la estafa se disfraza, el proveedor o el directivo falsos

Los ciberdelincuentes pueden adoptar la identidad de alguien conocido por la empresa para llegar a cabo su engaño. Se aprovechan de las redes de confianza tejidas en el entorno laboral para sustituir a proveedores y empleados. Con el propósito de preparar el ataque, llevan a cabo una labor de investigación en torno a la compañía. En muchas ocasiones, ya se han adentrado en su sistema en un ataque previo de phishing. El principal objetivo de esta estafa es obtener dinero o información sensible y puede presentarse de diversas formas:

Suplantación de un proveedor. Los ciberdelincuentes envían un correo electrónico en el que se hacen pasar por un proveedor habitual. Se imitan los elementos que lo identifican, como los colores, el logotipo, y manejan un lenguaje cercano, incluso familiar, para avisar deque desde ese momento en adelante los pagos deben hacerse a una nueva cuenta. Este tipo de fraude suele encuadrarse en el llamado business email compromise (BEC), en el que los atacantes manipulan o suplantan comunicaciones empresariales para desviar pagos o conseguir información sensible.

Fraude del directivo o del CEO. En esta modalidad, los atacantes envían correos electrónicos o realizan llamadas o videollamadas haciéndose pasar por un cargo con responsabilidad y capacidad de decisión, como un directivo o gerente, para pedir información confidencial, credenciales para entrar en el sistema o solicitar una transferencia urgente. Aunque puede parecer una orden legítima, el objetivo es desviar dinero o facilitar un acceso que permita cometer un fraude mayor. Esta modalidad ha incorporado recientemente la clonación de voz y la imagen generada mediante IA para hacer el engaño más creíble, gracias a la técnica del deepfake. Los ciberdelincuentes crean una imagen en movimiento del directivo que se utiliza durante una videoconferencia.

Fraude de desvío de nómina. Existe un tipo de estafa que afecta a los empleados. Los ciberdelincuentes suplantan la identidad de un trabajador para conseguir que la empresa modifique la cuenta bancaria en la que se ingresa su salario. ¿Cómo lo hacen? Envían un correo electrónico en el que solicitan el cambio de cuenta, en ocasiones, incorporando documentación falsificada. Si la empresa no verifica esa petición por otra vía, la nómina siguiente se transfiere a una cuenta controlada por los atacantes.

Las herramientas que protegen la pyme, mucha formación y ‘phishing’ ético

Cualquier empresa, por pequeña que sea, puede convertirse en objetivo de los estafadores. La diferencia está en su capacidad para detectar el engaño, impedir que una decisión equivocada se convierta en un incidente mayor y reaccionar con rapidez si finalmente ocurre. Para ello, la preparación debe combinar personas formadas, procesos de verificación y medidas de protección.

Anticipación: personas y procesos que frenan el engaño Verificar las operaciones sensibles. Los cambios de cuentas bancarias, los pagos excepcionales, los accesos a información delicada o cualquier solicitud fuera de lo habitual, deben comprobarse por una vía adicional, aunque la petición parezca legítima. La verificación no debe depender solo de la intuición de una persona. Formar a los empleados. La concienciación es una de las primeras líneas de defensa. Los trabajadores deben conocer las señales de una posible comunicación fraudulenta y saber cómo actuar ante ellas. Conviene partir de hábitos sencillos, como revisar el remitente, comprobar los enlaces y evitar abrir archivos adjuntos inesperados o sospechosos. Reconocer las señales de manipulación. Hay determinados indicios que deberían activar una alerta: Una urgencia que no es habitual

Una petición de confidencialidad

Un tono distinto al esperado

Presión para saltarse verificaciones

Instrucciones para completar una operación fuera de los canales habituales Entrenar a los equipos con phishing ético. Estas simulaciones reproducen intentos de phishing en un entorno controlado para comprobar cómo reaccionan los empleados e identificar áreas de mejora. Los resultados permiten orientar la formación hacia los comportamientos que presentan mayor riesgo y reforzar progresivamente la capacidad de respuesta de la organización. Reducir el impacto si algo falla Limitar los accesos. Cada empleado debe disponer únicamente de los permisos necesarios para hacer su trabajo. Así, si una cuenta resulta comprometida, el atacante tampoco obtiene acceso automático a toda la empresa. Activar la autenticación multifactor. Añadir una segunda prueba de identidad al entrar en el correo, la banca online o las aplicaciones de gestión dificulta el acceso incluso cuando las credenciales han sido robadas. Realizar copias de seguridad periódicas. Las copias de seguridad permiten recuperar información tras un ransomware u otro incidente, siempre que estén actualizadas y se mantengan separadas del sistema principal. Si el incidente ocurre: responder y seguir funcionando Actuar rápido y comunicarlo internamente. Si un empleado ha pulsado un enlace fraudulento, ha facilitado credenciales o detecta una actividad sospechosa, debe comunicarlo cuanto antes al responsable correspondiente. Comunicar un error cuanto antes ayuda a contener el incidente y reducir su impacto. Activar un plan de continuidad. La empresa debe tener previsto cómo mantener las funciones críticas mientras se contiene el ataque y se recuperan los sistemas. Esto implica saber qué operaciones son imprescindibles, cómo pueden seguir funcionando y cómo mantener informados a empleados, clientes y proveedores cuando sea necesario. Denunciar y pedir ayuda. Ante un incidente, la empresa puede solicitar asesoramiento especializado y, cuando corresponda, denunciarlo ante las Fuerzas y Cuerpos de Seguridad del Estado. Incibe ofrece apoyo a empresas en la gestión de incidentes de ciberseguridad. No pagar el rescate. Incibe desaconseja pagar en caso de ransomware: no existe garantía de recuperar la información, se financia a los ciberdelincuentes y se puede aumentar el riesgo de nuevos ataques. Contar con apoyo externo especializado. Las pymes pueden apoyarse en proveedores y servicios de ciberseguridad adaptados a su tamaño y presupuesto, con capacidades de monitorización, protección, gestión de accesos, respuesta ante incidentes y formación.

Prepararse frente a estas amenazas no consiste en esperar que nadie se equivoque nunca. Consiste en construir una empresa capaz de poner barreras cuando se incrementa el riesgo, limitar el impacto de un incidente y seguir operando si ocurre. Y esa preparación ya no afecta solo a la propia compañía. Una empresa forma parte de las cadenas de suministro, comparte datos, sistemas y procesos con clientes y proveedores. Su nivel de seguridad también puede convertirse en riesgo, o en confianza, para quienes trabajan con ella.

World.title: Porto Ercole, el pueblo de Italia donde la ‘dolce vita’ sigue mirando al mar
World.content:
Entre barcos de madera, terrazas frente al puerto y hoteles que forman parte de la historia del Mediterráneo y de la visión del fotógrafo Slim Aarons, en este enclave al sur de la Toscana la vida cotidiana sigue marcando el ritmo

Cuando llega la última hora de la tarde, la italiana Porto Ercole recupera su mejor versión. Los barcos regresan al puerto, las terrazas se llenan lentamente y la luz suaviza las fachadas de color ocre que trepan por la colina. Una Vespa atraviesa el paseo. Alguien recoge la ropa del balcón. Los camareros se mueven entre las mesas cuando llega la hora del aperitivo. En realidad nada parece extraordinario, y ahí está parte del encanto de este enclave en la costa del Argentario. La escena podría repetirse hoy o dentro de una década.

Este es uno de los lugares a los que la gente regresa. Las familias romanas que llevan generaciones pasando los veranos aquí. Los navegantes que conocen cada cala y quienes buscan un Mediterráneo que conserva su ritmo. Argentario no se parece demasiado a la Toscana que se suele imaginar. En vez de los campos infinitos de cipreses, aquí aparecen pinares que descienden hacia el mar y acantilados esculpidos por el viento.

Una callejuela en el casco antiguo de Porto Ercole. Atlantide Phototravel / GETTY IMAGES

Apenas a una hora y media en coche desde el aeropuerto de Roma (o en tren hasta Orbetello-Monte Argentario, a 10 kilómetros del pueblo), y a poco más de dos horas desde Pisa, los casi 3.000 vecinos de Porto Ercole han conseguido preservar algo cada vez más difícil de encontrar en el Mediterráneo: la sensación de estar en un lugar donde la vida cotidiana parece seguir marcando el ritmo.

Antes de que llegara Instagram, el fotógrafo estadounidense Slim Aarons (1916-2006) convirtió esta costa en uno de sus escenarios favoritos. Sus fotografías ayudaron a construir el imaginario de la dolce vita, retratando comidas interminables, barcos de madera, piscinas frente al mar y una elegancia que parecía surgir sin esfuerzo. Por delante de su cámara pasaron Gianni Agnelli, Lee Radziwill, los Getty o la familia Missoni… y muchas de aquellas escenas inmortalizadas siguen pareciendo posibles.

El encantador pueblo de Porto Ercole se encuentra en la costa del Argentario. Roberto Nencini ( GETTY IMAGES )

Las mañanas transcurren despacio en Porto Ercole; hay quienes comienzan el día con un expresso mirando al mar y los que prefieren perderse por las calles que rodean el puerto, donde se suceden pequeñas boutiques. Fue en una de esas tiendas donde empecé a entender mejor el pueblo. Había llegado la noche anterior y, después de descubrir que durante las noches aquí a veces corre un poco de fresco (aunque durante el verano son muy calientes, con temperaturas que suelen rondar los 30 grados de día y 25 grados de noche o más), entré en Ester Gi en busca de una capa ligera. Mientras me la probaba, Ornella, la encargada, empezó a hablar de Porto Ercole como solo hablan los italianos de los lugares que quieren. La Sirena para cenar pescado. O la Hosteria Alicina. O Il Gambero Rosso. Una recomendación llevaba a la siguiente y, antes de darme cuenta, ya no hablábamos de restaurantes, sino del pueblo. Ornella lo conoce bien, porque durante 14 años trabajó en la boutique del Hotel Il Pellicano y ha visto pasar generaciones de familias que repiten cada temporada. “Es como una pequeña joya”, dice al hablar del pueblo. “La gente vuelve porque aquí se sienten como en casa”.

Escuchándola, es fácil entender por qué, tarde o temprano, cualquier conversación sobre Porto Ercole acaba desembocando en el hotel Il Pellicano. “En realidad, toda su historia es una historia de amor”, explica. Y es difícil encontrar una mejor prueba de ello. Patricia Daszel, una socialité estadounidense, quedó fascinada por el piloto británico de guerra Michael Graham después de verlo fotografiado en un periódico como superviviente de un accidente aéreo. Años después se conocieron en Pelican Point, en California, se enamoraron y encontraron en unos terrenos de la familia Borghese, suspendidos sobre una cala de aguas cristalinas de Argentario, el lugar perfecto para construir una casa e invitar a sus amigos. Aquella residencia acabaría convirtiéndose en el hotel, que inauguraron en 1965.

Vista aérea del hotel Il Pellicano, en Porto Ercole. Pellicano Hotels

Ahora, 60 años después, Il Pellicano parece haber conservado una manera de entender el verano. Una buena parte de las fotografías más conocidas de Slim Aarons se tomaron aquí. El embarcadero, las plataformas junto al mar y las icónicas toallas de rayas amarillas y blancas siguen formando parte del paisaje. También la forma de vivirlo: un baño antes de comer, una sobremesa que se alarga y, al caer la tarde, el Bar Roberto, donde Federico Morosi lleva 18 años detrás de la barra.

La familia Sciò ha sido clave para conservar el carácter del alojamiento. Roberto Sciò llegó primero como huésped, se enamoró del lugar y lo hizo suyo en 1979. Desde entonces, el hotel ha mantenido esa combinación de elegancia relajada y discreción, hoy bajo la dirección de su hija Marie-Louise, y que también se percibe en La Posta Vecchia, la histórica propiedad familiar cerca de Roma.

Terraza junto al Mediterráneo de Il Pellicano. Pellicano Hotels

El espíritu de Il Pelicano también se percibe fuera del hotel. Ornella me insistió varias veces en que pasara por Medusa a la hora del aperitivo, un pequeño local abierto por Stefano y Alin, dos antiguos miembros del equipo que decidieron emprender su propio proyecto. Pedí una bruschetta de tomate y mozzarella mientras observaba la escena. Solo se escuchaba hablar italiano y sentí nostalgia de ese Mediterráneo de antes, con más veraneantes que turistas.

Cuando le pregunté a Ornella qué explicaba mejor Porto Ercole, no mencionó los hoteles ni los famosos. Habló de quienes crecieron veraneando aquí y siguen regresando cada año. Aunque esa fidelidad de la que hablaba no ha impedido que el pueblo empiece a escribir un nuevo capítulo. LA ROQQA es probablemente el mejor ejemplo. Inaugurado en 2023, hacía años que la apertura de un hotel no generaba tanta conversación en el pueblo. Mientras que Il Pellicano está más escondido sobre el acantilado, aquí el hotel forma parte de la vida cotidiana. Al cruzar la puerta, una puede mezclarse con las calles del centro o improvisar un aperitivo antes de regresar. Desde la entrada, donde suele descansar un pequeño Fiat descapotable que parece sacado de una fotografía de los años sesenta, LA ROQQA deja clara su personalidad. El interiorismo combina referencias retro, diseño contemporáneo y una paleta inspirada en los colores del puerto.

La mejor hora para subir a su rooftop Scirocco quizá no sea la cena, sino ese momento previo en el que el sol empieza a caer sobre Porto Ercole y el puerto cambia de color. La barra rinde homenaje a Caravaggio, con creaciones inspiradas en algunas de sus obras más célebres y reinterpretaciones del clásico Negroni. En la cocina también manda el producto local. Pescados del Tirreno, pasta fresca preparada a mano, verduras de temporada y vinos de la Toscana dan forma a la carta. Uno de los platos preferidos de la casa es su spaghetto otto pomodori, preparado con distintas variedades de tomate cultivadas en los alrededores de Porto Ercole.

La terraza Scirocco del hotel LA ROQQA, en Porto Ercole.

Explorando los alrededores

Quienes tienen algunos días más encuentran motivos de sobra para seguir explorando Argentario. A pocos minutos a pie desde Porto Ercole está la cala Le Viste. Hacia el norte, La Feniglia es una playa de arena bordeada por un pinar protegido perfecta para pasar la mañana, mientras que Spiaggia Lunga es más tranquila y salvaje.

Vista de la playa de La Feniglia. Andrea Pistolesi ( GETTY IMAGES )

La historia aparece donde menos se la espera. En Forte Filippo, fortaleza que los españoles levantaron en el siglo XVI para proteger la ruta marítima entre sus territorios italianos, y que sigue dominando la bahía a lo alto de las colinas. O en el último viaje de Caravaggio, que pasó aquí sus últimos días y murió en 1610 mientras intentaba regresar a Roma. A pocos kilómetros, Porto Santo Stefano es el punto de partida de los ferris hacia las islas de Giglio y Giannutri. Están integradas en el parque nacional del Archipiélago Toscano, el mayor parque marino protegido de Europa.

Porto Ercole conserva algo que resulta cada vez más difícil de encontrar, porque aquí las tardes siguen midiendo el tiempo en baños, aperitivos y conversaciones que se alargan sin mirar el reloj. Quizá por eso la dolce vita, más que una promesa, sigue pareciendo una forma de vivir.

World.title: Odemira, una ruta por el concejo del Alentejo más salvaje
World.content:
Cerca de 50 kilómetros de costa, pueblos blancos y arenales vírgenes desfilan por el concejo más extenso de Portugal, una tierra marcada por la fuerza creativa y donde el interior rural choca con el océano

Es muy común encontrar al escalabardo por el Alentejo, irrumpiendo de pronto en los caminos o cruzando temerario la carretera. El escalabardo, conocido también como meloncillo, es un mamífero pequeño y alargado, de pelaje pardo y cabeza afilada, similar a un hurón o una comadreja. Un icónico animalito que, por su conexión con esta tierra portuguesa, también da nombre a una interesante iniciativa ambiental, social y comunitaria desarrollada en la localidad de São Luís. “Damos un nuevo uso a la ropa que se deshecha para que, en lugar de acabar en la basura, pueda reutilizarse de manera creativa”, explica Ana Baleia desde su sede en esta freguesia de la región de Odemira, trazada con casas blancas y calles empedradas.

La creatividad es, de hecho, la enseña que enarbola este concejo, el más extenso de Portugal, erigido en un importante foco de inspiración al que acuden numerosos artistas y creadores para desarrollar su talento. Odemira, parte del parque natural del Suroeste Alentejano y Costa Vicentina, está considerado uno de los rincones más salvajes del litoral portugués. Aquí, donde el interior rural se da de bruces con el océano, se concentra la naturaleza más pura. “Puede que sea la diversidad (el mar, el río, la llanura, la sierra) pero lo cierto es que todo en esta zona estimula la creación artística”, apunta Baleia, a propósito de tradiciones tan arraigadas como la cerámica, el mimbre o el trabajo en telares, que conviven con otras disciplinas más contemporáneas.

Más información Recorriendo Esposende, un museo moderno al aire libre único en Portugal

Los secretos del océano

A juicio de los artesanos, es la belleza del entorno la que mantiene vivas las costumbres en un rincón marcado por la presencia del agua. Considerado uno de los ríos más limpios de Europa, el Mira atraviesa la región del Alentejo con la peculiaridad de fluir de sur a norte y el privilegio de dejar a su paso todo un despliegue de paisajes vírgenes. Recorrer Odemira es descubrir llanuras doradas por el sol, colinas ondulantes y campos alfombrados de viñedos hasta donde alcanza la vista. Estampas que chocan de pronto con una costa escarpada que da lugar a acantilados, dunas y calas solitarias.

Cigüeñas blancas anidan en los salientes de los acantilados marinos, en cabo Sardão. Cristina Candel

Nada como aventurarse por este litoral embravecido para dar con playas tan espectaculares como Almograve, encajada entre oscuras formaciones rocosas, o Carvalhal, donde el oleaje favorece la práctica de surf, o la pequeña y recogida Nossa Senhora, a la que se accede por pasarelas de madera. Pero es cerca de la playa de Cavaleiro, concretamente en el cabo Sardão, donde acontece un fenómeno sin igual: este lugar es el único punto conocido en el planeta en el que las cigüeñas blancas anidan en los salientes de los acantilados marinos, en vez de hacerlo en los árboles o los tejados. Un comportamiento especial que se puede observar muy de cerca, sobre los farallones y con el Atlántico de fondo, especialmente durante la primavera.

Villas de ambiente marinero

Más allá de la naturaleza, esta región atesora toda la magia de los pueblos alentejanos, con su peculiar arquitectura de fachadas encaladas que contrastan con los zócalos pintados en azul. Pueblos que, fuera de la temporada alta, hacen gala de un ritmo pausado y de un ambiente acogedor en el que se respira una estrecha conexión con el mar. Empezando por el propio Odemira, que da nombre al concejo, allí donde el río comienza a ser navegable hasta toparse con el océano. Esta es una población encaramada sobre una colina, cuya actividad cultural se concentra en el Café-Librería Mirabolante, que a menudo organiza tertulias, recitales y exposiciones de arte.

Vila Nova de Milfontes, en la desembocadura del Mira, con la fortaleza de São Clemente integrada entre las playas fluviales y las casas blancas del casco antiguo. Cristina Candel

Situada en la desembocadura del Mira, a Vila Nova de Milfontes se la distingue por la majestuosa silueta de la fortaleza de São Clemente, integrada entre las playas fluviales y las casas blancas del casco antiguo. Un castillo que fue levantado para contener el ataque de los piratas que asolaron este tramo de costa, ya por entonces ribeteado de playas dunares y recoletas calas salvajes. Hoy, para descubrirlas a pie, a caballo o en bicicleta, existe toda una red de senderos que atraviesan esta localidad que, al no ser ni villa, ni nueva, ni disponer de mil fuentes, comparte con la cántabra Santillana del Mar el sambenito de “las tres mentiras”.

Vecinos de la pequeña villa marinera de Zambujeira do Mar. Cristina Candel

Estos mismos caminos discurren por Zambujeira do Mar, una pequeña villa marinera que se posa sobre un acantilado para asomarse a uno de los arenales más impactantes del sur de Portugal. En su entramado, apenas compuesto por unas cuantas callejuelas que siempre acaban en el océano, no falta alguna fachada señorial, pequeñas muestras de arte urbano y la Capela de Nossa Senhora do Mar, la cual, por su posición sobre un promontorio con vistas a la playa y el pueblo, resulta una localización excelente para contemplar la puesta de sol.

Unas notas de ‘saudade’

Fue la calma de esta región la que logró cautivar a la reina portuguesa del fado. Cuentan que Amália Rodrigues, quien eligió como refugio vacacional al discreto pueblo de Brejão (entre Odemira y Zambujeira) para huir del bullicio de Lisboa, alumbró muchas de sus canciones mirando a ese Atlántico que irrumpía de pronto tras sortear un camino de juncos. En su honor, este mismo paraje fue rebautizado como la Praia da Amália, en el punto donde la artista acudía para guarecerse del mundo.

Mural con la imagen de Amália Rodrigues firmado por el artista urbano Ivo Santos, en Brejão. Cristina Candel

Pero también su memoria ha quedado impresa en las paredes de Brejão a través de los murales pintados por el artista urbano Ivo Santos en el verano de 2018. Cuatro retratos gigantescos de quien conjugó su voz única con hermosos versos de poetas antiguos para hacer de este género musical un desgarrado canto a la nostalgia. Con su recuerdo permanece viva la saudade de esta tierra impregnada de océano: “Ven a saber si el mar tendrá razón / Ven acá a ver bailar mi corazón”.

World.title: Inspectors demand urgent action on youth detention centres
World.content:
Staff shortages at the Dutch youth detention centres are putting detainees and staff under “persistent and serious” pressure and threatening their safety, three government inspectorates have warned.

Around 450 young people who have been convicted of a crime or are suspected of one are held in the country’s six youth detention centres, known as JJIs. The centres take young people who were aged between 12 and 23 when they committed the offence, though most are between 14 and 21.

Unlike adult prisons, they are meant to focus on education and treatment rather than punishment, to reduce the risk of reoffending.

In a letter to junior justice minister Claudia van Bruggen, the justice, education and health and youth care inspectorates said young people held in the centres are the victims of an “ever-increasing, worrying” erosion of care, treatment, education and daily activities. They called for an urgent action plan.

“Temporary emergency measures such as a shortened daily programme have now become standard practice,” said Elske van Amelsfort, chief inspector at the justice and security inspectorate. “That is why an action plan is needed from the state secretary in the short term.”

By law, young people in JJIs should spend 77 hours a week in group activities. Emergency measures introduced in 2023 set a reduced floor of 62 hours. The inspectorates said the centres are not meeting the requirements of either, because daily programmes are regularly cut back or cancelled at short notice when staff are unavailable.

As a result, young people spend too much time in their rooms, miss school and leave, and cannot always contact their families. Young people told inspectors they found it frustrating to be kept in their rooms, often without warning, and that repeatedly broken promises made it harder to stay motivated.

Warning signs

The inspectorates also said staff are becoming less experienced and more overstretched. Staff are regularly moved at short notice to units where they do not know the young people, which makes it harder to spot warning signs in time. The constant turnover of supervisors is causing frustration and tension among both young people and staff.

The inspectorates have raised concerns about the centres since 2019. The decision to phase out freelance staff in 2025 made the staffing crisis worse, the letter said.

In July, children’s ombudsman Margrite Kalverboer said there had been barely any improvement since the inspectorates’ previous warning a year earlier. She said almost all children’s rights were being violated in the youth detention centres.

World.title: Pro tables bill to remove abortion from Dutch criminal code
World.content:
Opposition party Pro has put forward a bill to remove abortion from the Dutch criminal code and officially regulate it as a part of healthcare. Currently, abortion is still technically a crime, although allowed under specific circumstances by professionals.

MP Lisa Vliegenthart, a former midwife, handed the bill to campaigners from feminist group Dolle Mina outside parliament on Monday morning, broadcaster NOS reported.

“This is incredibly important because abortion is healthcare, and as far as I am concerned healthcare has no place in the criminal code,” she said. “That is why we want to remove abortion from the criminal code and include it in healthcare legislation.”

Already legal

Abortion has been legal in the Netherlands since the 1980s, but the legal framework is unusual. Under an article of the criminal code, performing an abortion is a crime. The exception is if it is carried out by a doctor in a licensed clinic or hospital under the conditions set out in the Termination of Pregnancy Act.

Those conditions include a limit of 24 weeks and a requirement that the woman indicates she is in a situation of distress. Women themselves cannot be prosecuted for having abortions, but people administering them can be.

Pro says it wants to keep all the current care requirements, including the time limit, but move them into healthcare law. “Of course abortion has to be carried out carefully,” Vliegenthart said. “But you don’t need the criminal code for that.”

Proponents of the bill say that having abortion in the criminal code adds to the stigma around it and makes the rules harder to update.

The current law was a hard-fought compromise, passed by 76 votes to 74 in the lower house in 1980 and by 38 to 37 in the Senate. The rules have since been loosened, with the mandatory five-day waiting period was scrapped in 2023, and family doctors can now prescribe the abortion pill.

VVD support

Whether the bill passes depends largely on the right-wing liberal VVD. In 2023, the VVD joined the CDA, ChristenUnie, PVV, SGP and FvD to vote down a similar attempt to remove abortion from the criminal code. But its 2025 election manifesto committed the party to “actively work” to do so.

With support from the VVD, D66 and smaller opposition parties, the bill could have a narrow majority. However, the parties’ coalition partner, the CDA, remains against it.

The VVD has not yet said whether it will back the bill. “We are going to read the proposal and wait for the Council of State’s response,” the party said.

Constitution

If the bill passes, Pro wants to go further and enshrine the right to abortion in the Dutch constitution, as France did in 2024. Vliegenthart pointed to the United States, where the Supreme Court overturned the federal right to abortion in 2022. “That pressure exists in Europe and the Netherlands too,” she said.

In practice, access rather than legality is often the bigger issue for women. Last month, the health inspectorate allowed the country’s only online abortion service, which now issues around a quarter of all abortion pills, to keep operating after it changed its practices.

World.title: Market watchdog calls for transparency on AI in price setting
World.content:
The Dutch consumer markets authority ACM has called for more transparency on the role of AI in setting ticket prices after an investigation found wide discrepancies in the amounts charged for airline tickets.

The ACM said some airline seats had 35 different prices, while one-third of tickets cost 40% more than the average price, but there was no easy way for passengers to find the cheapest fare.

ACM chairman Martijn Snoep said the investigation into airline tickets was relevant because “similar techniques are being applied in other sectors”. Online retailers, concert ticket sites and even petrol stations are also using AI to set prices.

Commercial companies are using AI to drive dynamic pricing, based on supply and demand and competitors’ rates, but customers are unable to see how the prices are set.

Sometimes two people looking at the same product at the same time can be charged different prices, the ACM said. The impact of AI also means consumers spend longer searching for the best deal.

“We expect that AI and the availability of data means companies will increasingly use computer-aided prices, including personalised prices,” Snoep said.

The ACM has called on companies to be more open about how they set their prices and explain what factors influence the algorithms.

“Transparency is necessary so we can have a public debate about the desirability and the consequences of this development and how we want to proceed, keeping an eye on the way markets function and preventing people’s vulnerabilities being abused.”

World.title: Budget deal in sight after coalition agree to scrap welfare cuts
World.content:
Coalition parties D66, CDA and VVD hope to have a deal with the opposition parties finalised by Tuesday evening after talks over the weekend brought progress on the key issues of welfare and wealth taxes.

The left-wing parties Pro and Volt said the cabinet had agreed to drop its planned €6 billion cuts to social security in full, a key demand of the two parties and trade unions.

The two-year maximum term for the WW unemployment payments will be retained, while the long-term incapacity benefit WIA will remain untouched.

The government had already abandoned plans to cap benefits such as sick pay and maternity pay at a lower level and raise the retirement age in step with life expectancy.

Volt leader Laurens Dassen said the talks would need to continue to identify where the cabinet plans to find the money that will not be raised from welfare cuts, adding that “the devil is in the detail”.

Capital gains tax

The main concession to parties on the right is the introduction of a capital gains tax to replace the “box 3” asset taxes, which need to be reformed after the Supreme Court ruled that they breached European human rights laws.

The new system is expected to leave a €10 billion hole in the public finances in the short term because assets will only be taxed when they are sold, rather than on their annual gains, as is currently the case.

The Telegraaf, which has seen leaked copies of the plans, said the cabinet planned to raise the “box 2” tax on income from shares and dividends from business owners, to offset the loss.

The right-wing parties JA21 and SGP, who have also teamed up for the negotiations, were less enthusiastic about the proposed deal after meeting prime minister Rob Jetten and finance minister Eelco Heinen on Sunday.

“Nothing about migration”

JA21 leader Joost Eerdmans said the plans were “more left than right”, adding he had heard “nothing about tax cuts, migration or security”.

Chris Stoffer, of the orthodox protestant SGP, said his party’s concerns about abortion and surrogate parenting had also not been addressed.

Jetten and Heinen also held talks with ChristenUnie leader Mirjam Bikker, whose party could act as a go-between for the two sides. Bikker said she had seen “urgency, unity and movement” in the government parties after meeting the ministers on Saturday.

The cabinet needs 10 opposition votes to pass the budget in the lower house and 16 seats in the Senate.

Pro and Volt have 21 seats between them in the Tweede Kamer and just enough senators to secure a majority, while the right-wing duo can only provide enough votes in the lower house.

World.title: Hospitals block access to patients’ records after cyber threat
World.content:

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Some Dutch hospitals denied patients access to their medical records over the weekend because of security issues with the online gateway Citrix.

The national cybersecurity centre NCSC advised hospitals to disconnect their Citrix applications from the internet after discovering a “critical vulnerability” that could allow hackers to operate the system remotely.

The US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency issued an alert on Sunday, saying it had “received reports and partner threat intelligence confirming that threat actors are actively exploiting these vulnerabilities globally”.

The Amphia Ziekenhuis in Breda, the Elisabeth-TweeSteden Ziekenhuis in Tilburg and the Frisius medical centre in Leeuwarden were among the Dutch hospitals that reported problems at the weekend.

Doctors were still able to look at patients’ records, but the patients themselves could not during online consultations.

The Frisius MC said on Sunday it had blocked access as a precautionary measure in response to the alerts by the NCSC and Z-Cert, the agency specialising in digital security in healthcare, but its systems were now back online.

The interior ministry said some of its civil servants had been unable to work remotely at the weekend after its Citrix applications were switched off.

It is not the first time Dutch institutions have experienced security issues with Citrix and its access program, NetScaler. Last year the public prosecution service (OM) restricted access for two months after hackers exploited a gap in its security systems.

World.title: Amsterdam top destination for young people leaving home
World.content:
Most young people leaving home in the Netherlands head to Amsterdam, according to new figures from national statistics office CBS.

More than 174,000 people aged 18 to 30 moved out of their parents’ home in 2024, and a third of them settled in Amsterdam, one of ten councils tracked by the research. The city drew 12,760, well ahead of Rotterdam and Groningen.

The city was also the most popular destination for students, attracting 5,475, followed by Utrecht and Groningen. Nijmegen had the highest share of students

among young newcomers at 53.1%, followed by Utrecht and Leiden at 49.5% each.

The Hague was the exception: 65.4% of the young people who moved there were not students.

Just under a third of those leaving home were students, and half of them (49.9%) moved into privately rented housing. The rest went into social housing or owner-occupied homes. Non-students were most likely to move into an owner-occupied home (42.6%).

The figures only cover young people registered as living with their parents in the Netherlands at the start of 2024. They exclude anyone who moved to the country from abroad that year, such as newly arrived international students.

World.title: Israel strips Dutch diplomats’ status over settlement goods ban
World.content:
Israel is revoking the diplomatic status of Dutch diplomats in the West Bank city of Ramallah in the latest pushback against the Netherlands’ ban on goods produced in illegal Israeli settlements in occupied territories.

In a statement on social media, Israeli foreign minister Gideon Saar said the diplomats must return their Israeli-issued diplomatic documents within seven days, after which their diplomatic privileges and immunities will expire. He said the move was intended as a response to the ban that came into force last week.

“If the Netherlands wishes to continue representing its interests with the Palestinians, it may do so from Palestinian Authority territory, rather than from the territory of the State of Israel,” he said.

Dutch foreign minister Berendsen said in response that the move was “unnecessary” and that he “deeply regrets” it, adding that the ban on settlement goods “is not directed at Israel” but rather an obligation to comply with international law.

Last month, Israel expelled two Dutch officials from the US-backed centre in Kiryat Gat that coordinates the Gaza ceasefire.

Settlement ban

The Netherlands is the main EU import hub for goods produced in settlements in the West Bank, East Jerusalem and the Golan Heights – all of which are considered occupied under international law.

The cabinet agreed to the ban in May. It covers imports of and trade in settlement goods, and also applies to Dutch companies operating abroad.

Saar said that “Israel will not ignore measures intended to harm it. Any country that acts in a hostile and unilateral manner against Israel will lose influence and relevance in the region.”

He also spoke of “growing antisemitism and incitement openly seen on the streets of the Netherlands. Not only are this antisemitism and incitement not being seriously addressed, but the anti-Israel policies of the Dutch Government are fueling them.”

Saar did not specify what he was referring to. This spring there were four attacks on Jewish and pro-Israel targets in the Netherlands, which Dutch investigators believe were coordinated by an Iraqi man arrested in the US. Experts have said the attacks were very likely directed by Iran.

Economic ties

Despite the dispute over settlement goods, the Netherlands is the biggest destination for Israeli capital in the world, holding €44.9 billion in investment in 2024 – nearly four times as much as the US, according to research by Amsterdam-based corporate watchdog SOMO.

It is also the world’s second biggest investor into Israel, with €27.3 billion invested there in 2024 alone.

Earlier this month, more than 230 former Dutch ministers, ambassadors, diplomats and civil servants called on the cabinet to take tougher measures against Israel, including a full arms embargo and the suspension of the European Union’s trade agreement with the country.

World.title: Dutch river cruise stranded as Rhine falls to new record levels
World.content:

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

The river Rhine dropped to a new record low level at the weekend at the Dutch-German border, with no sign of fresh rainfall in the days ahead.

The river measured 6.1m at Lobith, the point where it flows into the Netherlands, on Sunday, below the previous record of 6.12m set in August.

Further upstream in Cologne, a Dutch cruise ship became stuck in mid-river as water levels dropped to just 40 centimetres on the gauge, leaving around 1.5 metres of navigable depth.

The Dutch Melody, which carries 140 passengers, was able to continue downriver after being assisted by another ship, German river police said. The four-deck vessel is due to arrive in Nijmegen later on Monday.

River levels are expected to drop further this week due to low rainfall in the Alps. At Lobith the flow of water has fallen below 600 cubic metres per second for the first time on record.

Dutch water authorities have had to impose restrictions on river traffic as channels became narrower and shallower during the summer drought.

Vessels using the IJssel to travel from Arnhem to Zutphen are having to take a 300km detour after Rijkswaterstaat imposed a one-way system.

Some ferries across the rivers have been cancelled and river cruises have had to cancel trips or shorten their itineraries because sections of the Rhine have become impassable.

World.title: Ninth-century Arabic silver coins found near Viking trading centre in Poland
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Several early medieval Arabic silver coins have been found in a forest near Elbląg in northern Poland. Experts believe they may have belonged to merchants travelling to or from the Viking Age port of Truso, which was situated nearby. The silver dirhams date back around 1,200 years, to the first half of the ninth century, before the founding of the Polish state. They may have remained in circulation until the turn of the 10th/11th century, the time of the settlement’s collapse. The discovery of the “new treasure” was announced last week by the Archaeological and Historical Museum in Elbląg. It did not reveal who had unearthed them, but said that the find had taken place during a legal search in a forest near the town of Młynary, just east of Elbląg. After conservation and processing work, the coins will be included in the collection of the museum, whose archaeologists will also visit the site hoping for further finds. The museum’s Jakub Jagodziński told the Polish Press Agency (PAP) that the find consists of “six early medieval Arabic dirhams and two fragments of these silver coins”. He said that they are provisionally dated to the first half of the 9th century, but a more precise estimate will be possible after they are processed. The coins could have belonged to merchants travelling along the routes leading to or from Truso or to Prussian guards who later collected tolls on these routes, Jagodziński explained. Truso was a Viking Age port of trade set up by the Scandinavians on the shores of lake Druzno near the Vistula river delta. Established by the late 7th century and active until the early 11th century, its location enabled trade extending towards Kyivan Rus, Byzantium and the Islamic world. Historians knew of Truso’s existence because of the account of the Anglo-Saxon traveller Wulfstan of Hedeby. Centuries-long efforts to find the precise site proved fruitless until it was finally discovered in the early 1980s by the young archaeologist Marek Jagodziński, Jakub’s father. Finds of Arab coins in Poland are not unprecedented. A silver deposit was discovered in 1986 on the site of Truso itself, consisting of 11 complete coins and five fragments. Coins found there were minted in places including Baghdad and Damascus, according to the Medievalists.net website. More recently, in 2024, a fragment of an early medieval Arabic dirham was found during renovations of an old manor house on the Baltic coast in northwestern Poland. In transactions involving dirhams, it was the value of the silver that mattered, so the coins were often broken into pieces, archaeologist Grzegorz Kurka told PAP. “Therefore, when hoards of Arab coins are discovered in Poland, they are divided into several pieces. Whole coins are also found, but much less frequently,” he explained. World.title: Poland offers to host facility producing Patriot missiles for Ukraine
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland has proposed that, if the United States grants Ukraine permission to produce its own missiles for Patriot air-defence systems, the factory could be located on Polish territory to ensure its security. The news was revealed by deputy defence minister Magdalena Sobkowiak-Czarnecka, who also confirmed that Poland would seek to establish a Patriot servicing and production facility even if it does not host Ukraine’s. Poland wants to host Patriot production Poland has proposed that the US and Ukraine launch joint production of Patriot missiles. Warsaw is citing security concerns and is proposing to host the facility in Poland instead of Ukraine: “If such a factory is planned to be built in… pic.twitter.com/syCkNt0o0V — Belsat in English (@Belsat_Eng) September 27, 2026 Patriot missile systems have been a key part of Ukraine’s defence against Russian aerial attacks. However, Kyiv has suffered from a shortage of missiles used in the system, prompting President Volodymyr Zelensky to appeal to allies to transfer their interceptors as well as to allow Ukraine to produce them itself. US President Donald Trump initially told Zelensky at a meeting in July that “we are gonna give you a licence to make Patriots”. However, he then backtracked on that offer later the same month. But, following weeks of uncertainty, on Friday last week Zelensky claimed that Trump had personally told him he had made a “final decision” to approve a licence for Ukraine to produce Patriot missiles. Washington has not confirmed that development. Asked about the issue on Saturday, Sobkowiak-Czarnecka told broadcaster TVN, “let’s see if it happens”. However, she added that, “we proposed that, if such a factory is planned to be built in Ukraine, we propose building it in Poland, so that it would be in the so-called safe territory”. Poland is already the primary hub for military equipment, goods and people being transported in and out of its eastern neighbour. Sobkowiak-Czarnecka added that, regardless of where the plant serving Ukraine is located, Poland would also still seek to establish a facility for servicing and, eventually, production of Patriots. “What my interlocutors in Washington confirmed is that, even if such a decision is made regarding Ukraine, it does not change our efforts and does not rule out consent for Poland,” she said. Sobkowiak-Czarnecka was in Washington last week for talks with US officials. In May this year, another deputy defence minister, Cezary Tomczyk, told TVN that Poland had “received preliminary approval from the US State Department to produce missiles for Patriot systems”. The Polish government has confirmed that it has transferred Patriot missiles to Ukraine following opposition criticism It also released a list of all military donations to Ukraine since 2022, showing that the former PiS government gave much more equipment https://t.co/8BmDy5BjiB — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 7, 2026 In 2018, as part of its Wisła air defence programme, Poland signed a $4.75bn contract to purchase Patriot launchers and missiles from the US. In October 2023, the first Patriot systems procured from the US were deployed at Warsaw Babice airport. In December 2025, Poland announced full operational readiness of its US-supplied Integrated Battle Command System (IBCS), an air-defence network that includes Patriot missile batteries. Poland also has an agreement to domestically produce launchers for Patriot systems through cooperation between Polish state-owned defence contractor Huta Stalowa Wola SA and US defence giant Raytheon. Poland has announced a $1.2bn deal that will see a Polish state-owned defence firm manufacture 48 launchers for Patriot missile systems domestically in cooperation with US defence giant Raytheon https://t.co/PQOjKvhqYM — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) August 12, 2024 The issue of Ukraine’s need for more Patriot missiles caused domestic political controversy in Poland earlier this year, when the right-wing opposition reacted angrily to reports that the government had handed over some interceptors to Ukraine. In July, the government confirmed that it had done so. However, Prime Minister Donald Tusk later revealed that only five missiles had been transferred to Ukraine. In late July, the Center for Strategic and International Studies reported that the Iran war had depleted America’s stockpile of Patriot missiles to 800 interceptors from roughly 2,300 before the war began. Last week, Germany’s defence minister, Boris Pistorius, confirmed that his country has also proposed that it could manufacture interceptors and perhaps even entire Patriot systems. World.title: “Don’t blame Ukrainian nation,” says Polish priest injured in deadly knife attack
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! We cannot do what we do without your support. One of the priests injured in a knife attack by a Ukrainian man at a Catholic abbey in Poland last week – which left one of his colleagues dead and another fighting for his life in hospital – has delivered a homily calling for people to forgive the attacker and not to blame Ukrainians as a whole for his actions. “I ask you not to repay evil with evil, but with love, support, understanding and care,” said a visibly injured Father Adrian Mantykiewicz. “I ask you to respect and support each other as two brotherly nations.” 🙏 Poruszające słowa ks. Adriana po ataku nożownika w Opactwie w Jarosławiu. W swojej pierwszej homilii po napaści duchowny mówił o przebaczeniu, miłości do bliźniego i odpowiadaniu dobrem nawet na doznaną krzywdę. pic.twitter.com/zGEGvC5meB — Goniec.pl (@GoniecPL) September 28, 2026 On Thursday last week, a 31-year-old Ukrainian man, who can be named only as Ihor H. under Polish privacy law, entered the grounds of the Benedictine abbey in the town of Jarosław. Using a knife he took from a kitchen, he attacked five people before he was stopped. One priest, Stanisław Zbojnowicz, died from his injuries shortly afterwards. Another, Marek Pieńkowski, is still being treated in hospital. Ihor H. was arrested at the scene and, on Saturday, a court approved a request from prosecutors for him to be placed in detention for three months. For now, he is being held in a psychiatric facility, with prosecutors saying that he “displayed symptoms of mental illness”. President @Zelensky has condemned an "evil" knife attack by a Ukrainian man at a Catholic abbey in Poland today, which left a priest dead and others injured Polish Prime Minister @donaldtusk says the perpetrator will face the “full severity of Polish law” https://t.co/SIonlR4JpJ — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) September 24, 2026 On Saturday, in a church that is part of the Benedictine abbey complex, Mantykiewicz celebrated the Eucharist for Zbojnowicz. With bruising under his left eye and bandages on his head and hand, he delivered a homily in which he addressed the attack, its victims, and the perpetrator. “I am a disciple of my master, a disciple of my lord, and Christ teaches me love,” he said. “And from this place, as a disciple of Jesus Christ, I wish to say very clearly in my name, in the name of Father Marek, and in the name of Father Stanisław, that we forgive.” “I ask you to pray for our tormentor,” he continued. “He needs this prayer most of all. Because no matter what happened, we must overcome the evil that occurred here in our abbey with goodness, love, and forgiveness.” Mantykiewicz also appealed for people not to blame Ukrainians more broadly for the incident. There have been fears that the attack could prompt a backlash against Ukrainians, Poland’s largest immigrant group, who have already been experiencing a growing number of hate crimes this year. “I also want to ask you not to blame the nation from which the perpetrator came,” said the priest. “The evil was committed by a specific person…responsible for their own actions. It was not done by other people. It was one person, one person alone.” “Let us be disciples of Christ. Disciples who help others with love, care, respect, help and kindness,” he continued. “It does not matter who they are, what nation they come from, what religion they are, or what colour their skin is; they are human beings…and we must not deprive anyone of their dignity.” On Friday, the head of the Polish Catholic church’s council for migrants and refugees, Bishop Krzysztof Zadarko, gave a press conference at which he condemned the “outpouring of aggression and artificially stoked hatred towards Ukrainians that this event [in Jarosław] has fuelled”. “The church can only appeal to the consciences, primarily of Catholics and Christians, but also of all people, that this is not the right response; it is downright reprehensible, and incompatible with the Gospel,” he added, quoted by broadcaster RMF. “We are dealing with a tremendous tragedy, but shifting the blame of one person onto an entire society, ethnic group, or nationality is wrong,” he added. Agresja i niechęć do kogokolwiek jest nie do pogodzenia z wiarą chrześcijańską – mówił przewodniczący Rady KEP ds. Migrantów i Uchodźców bp Krzysztof Zadarko podczas konferencji prasowej przed 112. Światowym Dniem Migranta i Uchodźcy.https://t.co/M46RXggVTR pic.twitter.com/uZWodfR7sG — EpiskopatNews (@EpiskopatNews) September 25, 2026 Thursday’s attack caused widespread shock and mourning in Poland, and also prompted condolences from Ukraine, including President Volodymyr Zelensky, who said that “we are shocked by this evil”. On Saturday, Ukraine’s ambassador to Poland, Vasyl Bodnar, told broadcaster TVN that he had spoken with Ihor M.’s mother and was able to provide more information about him. He confirmed that the man had left Ukraine in 2022 and lived in Germany. Bodnar, however, said that media reports claiming Ihor M. had served in the Ukrainian military were false. Regarding the motive, Bodnar said that it appears Ihor M. “had some kind of mental illness”. He pledged that the Ukrainian authorities would cooperate and were “working on all the information we can provide to the Polish side”. World.title: Russia condemns Polish city’s “barbaric” removal of Monument of Gratitude to the Red Army
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Russia has criticised the removal of a monument in the Polish city of Rzeszów expressing “gratitude” to the Soviet Red Army. It called the move “barbaric” and “sacrilegious”. The monument – part of which will be moved to a nearby Soviet cemetery and another to a museum – has been the subject of a long-running legal and political battle, amid wider debate in Poland about “decommunising” public spaces, especially in the wake of Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine. ⚡️Komentarz Ambasady Rosji w Polsce 23 września 2026 r. w Rzeszowie (województwo podkarpackie), decyzją władz polskich i z naruszeniem dokumentów rosyjsko-polskich dotyczących ochrony obiektów dziedzictwa memorialnego, rozpoczęto proces demontażu pomnika wdzięczności żołnierzom… pic.twitter.com/HYuNeLG5dy — Russian Embassy, PL (@rusemb_pl) September 24, 2026 The Monument of Gratitude to the Red Army, standing 8.5 metres tall and weighing 6.6 tons, was erected in Rzeszów, southeastern Poland, shortly after the end of World War Two, when the Soviets had pushed Nazi Germany out of Poland and then installed their own communist government. It is located on Ghetto Victims Square, a public space also created after the war on the grounds of the city’s former Jewish cemetery, which had been destroyed by the German occupiers in 1942. Poland’s Institute of National Remembrance, a state historical body, notes that the monument was erected just a few metres from where two Polish anti-communist resistance fighters who had been members of the wartime Home Army (AK) had been publicly hanged by the communists. The monument’s plinth featured bas-relief sculptures depicting Red Army Generals Ivan Konev and Karol Świerczewski, soldiers, and industrial and agricultural workers carrying a hammer and sickle. At the top of the 8.5-metre column was a statue of a woman and child. In 2016, the then-ruling national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) government introduced a law requiring local authorities to “decommunise” public spaces by removing objects and names that “propagate communism”. That triggered a legal battle over the monument in Rzeszów. The government-appointed provincial governor and the Institute of National Remembrance (IPN), a state historical body, moved to have it dismantled, arguing that the monument glorified communism. But city hall – led by left-wing mayor Tadeusz Ferenc, who had been a member of the communist party before 1989 – challenged the decision. It argued that the monument did not promote communism and noted that its name, referring to gratitude to the Red Army, was not an official one. In 2019, the provincial administrative court sided with the city and overturned the decision to remove the monument. However, Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022 prompted many Polish municipalities that had not removed Soviet-era monuments to begin doing so. In April 2022, Rzeszów’s current mayor, Konrad Fijołek, announced that his city’s monument would be taken from its current location and placed in a Soviet soldiers’ cemetery elsewhere in the city. “In principle, I am not in favour of dismantling or demolishing monuments, as they are a testament to history,” said the mayor. “But in light of the current wartime reality, this monument should not remain in its current location. But we are not barbarians; we will not demolish the monument, but relocate it.” However, the IPN opposed the idea of relocating the monument and refused to cover the costs of doing so. It wanted it to be eliminated entirely. Another Soviet memorial has been demolished in Poland – the 43rd since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine. "We say ‘no’ to Russians who believe these lands somehow belong to their sphere of influence,” declared the Institute of National Remembrance https://t.co/aG9VQVlUQI — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) December 12, 2025 As a result, the city is paying 156,000 zloty (€35,700) for the monument to be taken away, reports news website Wirtualna Polska. The bas-reliefs will go to the Soviet cemetery while the statue of mother and child will go to the city’s Museum of Technology and the Military. Work to remove the monument began this week and is expected to last until November. Once the above-ground section has been removed, a special conservation committee, including a representative of Poland’s Rabbinical Commission for Cemeteries, will determine how to proceed with the monument’s foundation. The beginning of the removal work prompted anger from Moscow, with the Russian embassy in Warsaw issuing a statement that called it a “sacrilegious step”. It demanded “the immediate cessation of work” and restoration of the monument to its previous state. “With regret, we must state once again: the barbaric policy of the Polish authorities, consisting of destroying everything that serves as evidence of the invaluable feat of the soldiers and officers of the Red Army in liberating Poland from Nazi occupation, is being continued at an ever faster pace,” they continued. Russia regards the Soviet Union’s driving Nazi Germany out of Central and Eastern Europe at the end of World War Two as a “liberation”. However, many in the region reject that term, given that it involved bringing their countries under brutal Soviet domination instead. In its statement, the Russian embassy also claimed that the actions in Rzeszów are a “violation of Russian-Polish documents concerning the protection of memorial heritage sites”. Moscow regularly claims that Poland’s removal of Soviet memorials violates a 1994 agreement between the two countries on respect for graves and other places of memory. It did so in August this year, when protesting the demolition of a monument in the town of Pyrzyce. However, Poland points out that the agreement relates to graves and war cemeteries, not separate monuments and symbols, which can be legally removed. Russia has criticised the "sacrilegious" demolition of a Soviet monument in Poland, calling it a “flagrant violation” of a bilateral agreement. But Poland's @ipngovpl says it was a "propaganda object" that had to be removed under a "decommunisation" law https://t.co/73T99ZlPqU — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) August 4, 2026 Rzeszów is also home to one of the famous – or infamous, depending on one’s perspective – communist-era monuments in Poland, the 38-metre-tall Monument to the Revolutionary Struggle. It has become a landmark of the city. In 2017, the IPN recommended that it be removed under the “decommunisation” law. The owners of the land upon which it sits also wanted to demolish it. However, mayors Ferenc and Fijołek sought to protect the monument, and their efforts succeeded last year, when it was added to Poland’s list of protected monuments, preventing it from being destroyed.
