World.title: Polish president “doesn’t like” Trump inviting Putin to G20 but will still attend summit
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Polish President Karol Nawrocki “does not like” the fact that the Trump administration has invited Vladimir Putin to this year’s G20 summit in the United States, says his chief foreign policy aide. However, Nawrocki, who is a close ally of Donald Trump, still plans to attend the event – which Poland has been invited to as a guest rather than a full G20 member – in order to represent Polish interests and push for full membership of the group. 🔴 "Nie podoba nam się to". Nawrocki ma problem po decyzji Trumpa Prezydent Karol Nawrocki weźmie udział w grudniowym szczycie G20 w Miami, na który zaproszono również Władimira Putina. Szef Biura Polityki Międzynarodowej Kancelarii Prezydenta Marcin Przydacz przyznał na antenie… — Wirtualna Polska (@wirtualnapolska) September 26, 2026 The G20, a major intergovernmental forum, holds an annual summit whose location rotates among members. This year’s event will take place in December at a golf resort in Miami owned by Trump. On Wednesday this week, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio announced that Trump has invited Putin to attend the summit, saying that “we think it’s an opportunity for him to engage…with other world leaders” and “we hope that’s an invitation he’ll accept”. “If you only meet with people that you agree with, then these are very nice meetings but nothing happens,” added Rubio. “In order to solve problems, you have to meet with people that you disagree with or the people that you might have some issues with.” Marco Rubio on Russia: We’ve invited President Putin to the G20. We think it’s an opportunity for him to engage not just with Trump, but with other world leaders. We hope that’s an invitation he will accept. pic.twitter.com/e0GSz7Y8gm — Clash Report (@clashreport) September 23, 2026 Last December, Rubio also announced Poland’s invitation to the summit as a guest, saying that it would be “assuming its rightful place in the G20”. In May this year, the US also “expressed its strong support for Poland’s accession to the G20 as a permanent member”. Poland will be represented by Nawrocki, who is a vocal critic of Putin and Russia, and is himself on a Russian wanted list for his work leading efforts to demolish Soviet-era monuments in Poland. In an interview on Sunday with news website Wirtualna Polska, the head of Nawrocki’s international policy office, Marcin Przydacz, was asked if the US was right to invite Putin. “We don’t like it,” he replied. “But we were invited to the G20 summit as guests, and it’s not our role to tell the participants who should be part of it,” he added, noting that Russia is a founding member of the G20. However, “if it were up to us, Russia should be isolated in all international forums.” Nevertheless, “President [Nawrocki] is going to Miami and doesn’t intend to change his plans at this stage”, confirmed Przydacz. “Poland will be at the G20 summit because it’s in our interest…This isn’t the only format in which we sit with countries we disagree with.” However, he also added that, “if the Russian leader actually intends to come, and is not just invited, we will discuss this with our European and Euro-Atlantic allies”. Putin has not attended a G20 summit in person since 2019, initially due to the COVID-19 pandemic and later amid the fallout from Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine and the International Criminal Court’s arrest warrant against him. The US is not a member of the ICC, so the arrest warrant does not apply on its territory. Przydacz told Wirtualna Polska that Putin “should be held accountable for his crimes”. Asked if Nawrocki would shake hands with the Russian president at the G20, Przydacz said that he “doesn’t think any interactions will occur”. The United States has expressed "strong support for Poland’s accession to the G20 as a permanent member" following talks in Warsaw, after which it also emphasised "strong and growing" Polish-American relations https://t.co/qTpCACnMfu — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) May 2, 2026 He also emphasised that Poland’s invitation to the summit was a “major success, demonstrating our growing role”. He said that Nawrocki would use the event to push its ambition to become a full member of the group. He added that it would also seek to “bring a Central European perspective” to the event, representing the entire region, which has so far been excluded from the G20. Earlier this week, Polish foreign minister Radosław Sikorski said that, in his opinion, the US should make Putin’s invitation to the G20 conditional upon Russia implementing a ceasefire in Ukraine, reported news website Interia. However, he noted that, when a G20 meeting of finance ministers took place in the US earlier this year, Poland had attended alongside Russia. President @NawrockiKn says that a planned new permanent US military base in Poland is “confirmed” because his American counterpart, Donald Trump, is “famous for keeping his word”. He also suggested that the new facility will be called “Fort Trump” https://t.co/uGGJSBe5nr — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) September 23, 2026 Since Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine, Poland has been one of Kyiv’s closest allies, providing extensive military, humanitarian and diplomatic support to its eastern neighbour. Poland has also been one of the primary targets of Russia’s hybrid actions against European countries, including airspace violations, acts of sabotage, cyberattacks and disinformation. World.title: Poland extends tax rights to same-sex couples with foreign marriages
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. The Polish government has granted same-sex couples who married abroad and have had their wedding certificates transcribed into the Polish registry the same tax rights as other married couples. The decision follows a ruling by the Court of Justice of the European Union (CJEU) requiring Poland – whose domestic law does not allow same-sex couples to form any type of legal union – to recognise same-sex marriages contracted in other EU member states. Podpisałem dziś interpretację ogólną, która zapewnia, że osoby, które uzyskały transkrypcję aktu małżeństwa będą miały w polskich urzędach skarbowych takie same prawa i obowiązki podatkowe jak wszyscy małżonkowie. — Andrzej Domański (@Domanski_Andrz) September 24, 2026 “Today, I signed a general interpretation ensuring that persons who have obtained a transcription of their marriage certificate will have the same tax rights and obligations in Polish tax offices as all other married couples,” announced finance minister Andrzej Domański in a social media post. A general interpretation is an official position taken by the finance ministry aiming to clarify the application of tax law in a specific area. Among the benefits that couples with a transcribed foreign marriage certificate can now receive include preferential treatment under inheritance and gift tax rules and the ability to file joint personal income tax returns. Couples may also pay tax on behalf of a spouse and refuse to testify as a witness in proceedings involving their spouse. “This is about basic equality, justice and fairness,” Domański told broadcaster TVN. “We want these rights to be enforceable in an effective way.” The finance minister said that the decision would have a “negligible” impact on the state budget. He also noted that such couples would be subject to the obligations that apply to other married couples in Poland, which include liability for their spouse’s tax obligations. Osoby, które uzyskały tak zwaną transkrypcję aktu małżeństwa, będą miały przed polskimi urzędami skarbowymi dokładnie takie same prawa i obowiązki jak pozostali małżonkowie – powiedział minister finansów Andrzej Domański w rozmowie z Grzegorzem Kajdanowiczem w @faktypofaktach w… pic.twitter.com/uVwDaD3ZDk — tvn24 (@tvn24) September 24, 2026 The finance minister’s decision has drawn criticism from right-wing politicians, who argue that recognition of same-sex marriage violates the constitution, which states that “marriage, being a union of a man and a woman, shall be placed under the protection and care of the Republic of Poland”. Paweł Szefernaker, chief of staff to President Karol Nawrocki, who is aligned with the right-wing opposition, said Domański’s actions were “inconsistent with the constitution” and had been carried out “without legislation, without debate, without honestly telling Poles what is really happening”. “Everyone has the right to a private life,” he added. “However, the state has a duty to protect the legal order and provide tax support for marriage.” Patryk Jaki, a deputy leader of the national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS), Poland’s largest opposition party, said that the finance minister’s actions “clearly violate Polish law and will have legal implications in the future” for Domański, who is “writing additional points in the indictment against himself”. Sławomir Mentzen, one of the leaders of the far-right Confederation (Konfederacja) group, said the tax interpretation “will be revoked on the very first day” if his party comes to power. To jest niezgodna z Konstytucją próba faktycznego zrównania małżeństwa ze związkami jednopłciowymi. Bez zmiany Konstytucji, bez ustawy, bez debaty, bez uczciwego powiedzenia Polakom, co naprawdę się dzieje. Każdy ma prawo do prywatnego życia według własnych wyborów. Ale państwo… https://t.co/0CQ9Lnfl02 — Paweł Szefernaker 🇵🇱 (@szefernaker) September 24, 2026 The changes follow a ruling issued by the CJEU in November 2025 ordering Poland to recognise same-sex marriages contracted in other EU states. The court found that failing to do so infringes the freedom to move and reside within the EU as well as the right to respect for private and family life. In light of that ruling, in March this year, Poland’s own Supreme Administrative Court (NSA) ordered Warsaw’s registry office to recognise a marriage conducted by two Polish men in Germany by transcribing it into the Polish civil registry. In May, the Polish government issued a regulation allowing such transcriptions of foreign same-sex marriages to take place nationwide. It went into force in August. However, even before then, some cities had begun transcribing marriage certificates, beginning with Warsaw and Wrocław in May. At the end of August, digital affairs minister Krzysztof Gawkowski reported that 84 same-sex couples had already transcribed their foreign marriages under the government’s new regulation. Poland has begun paying benefits to same-sex couples who married abroad then entered their marriage into the Polish registry. The EU court ordered Poland to recognise such marriages, even though domestic law does not allow for any form of same-sex union https://t.co/svnRjyBO8Q — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) September 22, 2026 While foreign same-sex marriages can now be entered into Poland’s civil registry, questions have remained as to what that will mean in practice for such couples, especially as domestic law does not recognise same-sex relationships. In another development, labour minister Agnieszka Dziemianowicz-Bąk announced last week that the Social Insurance Institution (ZUS) has begun paying care allowances to qualifying same-sex couples who married abroad and have had their wedding certificates transcribed into the Polish registry. Prosecutors have ended a decade-long case in which former president and Nobel Peace Prize winner Lech Wałęsa was accused of falsely claiming not to have authored documents relating to his alleged cooperation with the communist authorities. Wałęsa, who led the Solidarity movement that helped bring down the communist regime in the 1980s, has always denied longstanding claims that, in the 1970s, he acted as an informant to the communist security services. The case has become highly politicised, with right-wing figures – especially from the Law and Justice (PiS) party that ruled Poland from 2015 to 2023 – critical of Wałęsa. By contrast, the former president, who turns 83 next week, enjoys good relations with the current ruling coalition of Prime Minister Donald Tusk. Waldemar Żurek, Tusk’s justice minister and prosecutor general, welcomed the decision to drop the case against Wałęsa, saying that, under PiS, “a politicised state apparatus hounded the legend of Solidarity, deliberately ignoring facts and basic logic”. Now, “truth has triumphed over an attempt to rewrite history”. Prokuratura ostatecznie umorzyła śledztwo przeciwko Lechowi Wałęsie. Przez lata upolityczniony aparat państwa ścigał legendę „Solidarności”, celowo ignorując fakty i elementarną logikę. Zignorowano bezsporny fakt historyczny – SB masowo fałszowała dokumenty i podpisy Wałęsy w… — Waldemar Żurek (@w_zurek) September 24, 2026 The case in question stems from statements made by Wałęsa in 2016 during an investigation by the Institute of National Remembrance (IPN), a state historical body that also has prosecutorial powers. Those proceedings, in which the former Polish president testified as a witness, were launched after documents apparently carrying his signature were found in the home archives of former communist interior minister Czesław Kiszczak. The files indicated that Wałęsa, working under the code name TW Bolek, signed a commitment to collaborate with the communist Security Service (SB). They also included payslips and informant’s notes. The former president had told the media at the time when the documents were discovered that they had been forged. When speaking to IPN investigators, he also denied having drafted or signed all but one of the documents. However, prosecutors subsequently claimed that – after comparing the documents from Kiszczak’s file with others they said had been written and signed by Wałęsa, as well as consulting forensic handwriting experts – Wałęsa’s testimony was false in the case of over 50 of the documents. In 2021, the former president was charged with giving false testimony. Then, in 2023, he was indicted, meaning the case was sent to court. However, in 2024, after Tusk’s government had taken power from PiS, prosecutors asked that the case be returned to them by the court, which agreed to the request. Now, the district prosecutor’s office in Warsaw has announced that it is discontinuing the case entirely, after finding that there are no grounds for Wałęsa to be prosecuted. Lech Wałęsa will face trial accused of falsely testifying not to have signed documents of cooperation with the communist authorities. If convicted, he can be jailed for up to 3 years. He calls the claims against him "terrible insults and monstrous lies" https://t.co/X0eb4e5ahm — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) November 30, 2023 In a statement explaining the decision, prosecutors claimed that there had been significant “methodological errors” made previously in attributing handwritten texts to Wałęsa and in handwriting comparisons between them. “There was no evidence to assume with 100% certainty that the comparative material actually came from Lech Wałęsa,” they wrote. In fact, “the evidence collected clearly indicated that Lech Wałęsa did not write long manuscripts during his life, and especially not in the 1970s”. “Some witnesses explicitly stated that, at that time, he was a secondary illiterate,” meaning someone who has lost their ability to read and write, said the prosecutors. “He was not able to write and could barely read.” This, along with other concerns over how the case was previously conducted, “led to the conclusion that there was no certain basis to assume that Lech Wałęsa was the author of the documents disclosed in the ‘Kiszczak files’, and therefore there was no evidence that he lied during the interrogation”. Hit! Ekipa Tuska ogłosiła Wałęsę analfabetą by wybronić go przed Bolkiem! To się nie dzieje! To niemożliwe! pic.twitter.com/PQnOn5XDb0 — Sławomir Cenckiewicz (@Cenckiewicz) September 24, 2026 Prosecutors also said that “the testimony of numerous witnesses proves that the files of TW Bolek, discovered in the possession of General Kiszczak’s widow, were most likely fabricated. Finally, they argued that, even if Wałęsa had given false testimony, he was protected by the constitutional right against self-incrimination while being interviewed as a witness. “The prosecution found that Lech Wałęsa could have feared that if he admitted to having prepared or signed the documents from the ‘Kiszczak files’…all his testimonies in which he denied being secret collaborator “Bolek” in previous proceedings…would be deemed false and would lead to his being held criminally liable.” Lech Wałęsa, Angela Merkel and Volodymyr Zelensky have been named the first distinguished members of the European Order of Merit. The award was created by the European Parliament to "honour those who did not simply believe in Europe, but helped build it" https://t.co/inosiiRQkW — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) March 11, 2026 In response to the announcement, Wałęsa shared on his Facebook page the post by Żurek praising the prosecutors’ decision. Wałęsa then added a comment claiming that Jarosław and Lech Kaczyński, the founders of PiS, had ordered a right-wing historian, Sławomir Cenckiewicz, to fake the Kiszczak files. Cenckiewicz has written extensively about Wałęsa, including about his alleged collaboration with the communist security services. He also recently served as national security advisor to current Polish President Karol Nawrocki, who was elected last year with the support of PiS. In a series of social media posts on Thursday, Cenkiewicz said that he had “never read a bigger lie” than the prosecutors’ statement justifying dropping the case. He also ridiculed the idea that Wałęsa could have led the Solidarity movement in the 1980s and served as president in the 1990s if he was a “secondary illiterate”. Większego kłamstwa przebranego w wymiar sprawiedliwości RP nigdy nie czytałem! To większe kłamstwo niż skandaliczny wyrok Kapińskiego i spółki z 2000 r.! Reżim Tuska uznał, że Wałęsa nie był Bolkiem, a Instytut Sehna niczego kategorycznie nie ustalił! I powtórzyli brednie… — Sławomir Cenckiewicz (@Cenckiewicz) September 24, 2026 The accusations of communist collaboration have tarnished Wałęsa’s reputation among some Poles. In 2017, shortly after the Kiszczak files were uncovered, a poll by IBRiS for the Rzeczpospolita daily found that 28% believed Wałęsa was not a national hero. However, 62% said that he was. Earlier this year, Wałęsa was named as one of the first three distinguished members of the European Order of Merit, a new initiative launched by the European Parliament, alongside Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky and former German Chancellor Angela Merkel. World.title: Smartwings Cuts Prague Flights as Winter Schedule Shrinks
World.content:
Smartwings is reducing its winter flight schedule from Prague, with several routes being cancelled, frequencies cut and new connections postponed until spring 2027.

The biggest changes will affect Spain, a popular choice for Czech travelers looking for warmer weather during the autumn and winter months.

The airline will suspend flights between Prague and Valencia from November 2 until the beginning of March.

Flights to several other Spanish destinations will also be reduced. Smartwings will cut its Málaga service from two flights a day to one, while Barcelona will move from daily flights to four to six services a week.

Flights to Mallorca will be reduced from four per week to two. The Prague–Madrid route will continue, but flights will operate on an irregular schedule.

Smartwings is also suspending flights from Prague to Nice until early March.

New Prague routes pushed back

Several routes that were expected to launch this year will now have to wait until spring 2027.

The postponed connections include new services to Venice and Bergen, Norway. Smartwings has also delayed the return of flights to Brussels and Bucharest.

Both Brussels and Bucharest were suspended in the spring, with Smartwings originally planning to restore the routes in October.

Eurowings also reduces Prague services

Eurowings is making changes to its Prague schedule as well. The German carrier has cancelled its planned winter flights to Madeira, Portugal.

The route had been scheduled to return for the winter season, but Eurowings will instead offer tickets to Madeira through a partnership with Smartwings, which continues to operate flights to the Portuguese island.

Eurowings will also suspend its Prague–Stockholm service for most of January.

Higher fuel costs affect airline schedules

The changes come as airlines face higher operating costs linked to fuel prices.

According to Eurocontrol, the European organization responsible for coordinating air traffic management, jet fuel prices in Europe more than doubled between the beginning of the year and mid-September.

Airlines around the world have been adjusting schedules as fuel costs fluctuate amid the conflict in the Middle East. Route cancellations and reduced frequencies are among the measures carriers are using to adapt to changing market conditions.

World.title: Home Baking Returns to Czech Kitchens as Flour Sales Rise
World.content:
Home baking is gaining momentum in the Czech Republic, with online supermarket Rohlik.cz reporting a sharp increase in demand for baking ingredients this year.

Flour has been at the center of the trend. Sales of organic flour have risen by almost 72 percent compared with the previous year, while conventional flour sales increased by around 23 percent.



The change has also affected the balance of sales. Organic flour previously accounted for about 19 percent of flour purchases at Rohlik.cz. That figure has now climbed to almost 25 percent.

The figures suggest that customers are not simply buying more flour but are also paying greater attention to the type and quality of the ingredients they use.

Rohlik.cz CEO Miroslava Vopatová says baking continues to play a role in family life, particularly as an activity shared across generations. The supermarket has responded by offering products at different price points, from private-label options to organic and farm-produced ingredients.

Yeast sales tell a different story

The increase in demand for flour has not been mirrored by yeast.

Sales of yeast have been gradually falling since the surge in home baking during the coronavirus pandemic. One shift remains noticeable, however: shoppers are increasingly choosing fresh yeast rather than dried yeast.

Home baking in the Czech Republic is also strongly seasonal. Christmas remains the busiest period of the year, while a smaller increase usually occurs in March and April. Demand drops during the summer months.

For experienced bakers, the quality of the final product often depends on relatively simple details. Yeast dough needs enough time and warmth to rise properly, while rushing the process can affect the result.

The preparation of the filling matters as well. Curd cheese should be drained thoroughly before being added to a cake or pastry, reducing the risk of excess moisture making the dough soggy. Fruit fillings should also be sufficiently thick rather than watery.

These practical details can make a noticeable difference, particularly in traditional Czech pastries whose recipes are often passed down through families.

World.title: New Flights from Prague to Asia Boost Competition on Airfares
World.content:
Travelers flying from Prague this autumn have more options as airlines add capacity and new direct connections, particularly to Asia.

At the same time, increased competition is putting pressure on carriers to keep fares under control, according to data from Czech booking portal Letuška.cz.



The biggest changes are visible on long-haul routes. New services from Prague are making destinations in Asia more accessible, while airlines already serving the Czech market are responding with promotional fares.

“Thanks to high competition and new capacity from Prague, the autumn flight market offers very favorable travel conditions,” said Josef Trejbal, commercial director of Letuška.cz. He said the arrival of new Asian connections has helped revive demand for long-haul travel and encouraged established airlines to introduce more competitive offers.

Direct flights strengthen Prague’s links with Asia

Asia is once again attracting greater interest from Czech travelers. One factor is the growing number of direct or more convenient connections from Prague, which can reduce the need for lengthy transfers through major Middle Eastern hubs.

STARLUX Airlines, for example, is offering flights from Prague to Taipei from around CZK 21,000. The direct service provides an alternative to itineraries involving a stopover and can save travelers both time and, depending on the itinerary, money.

Another new option will be available from October 10, when flights to Hanoi are scheduled to begin on the Prague–Almaty–Hanoi route. Tickets listed through Letuška.cz start at around CZK 18,000.

The expansion comes as airlines compete more aggressively for passengers on long-haul routes departing from Prague.

Caribbean and Latin America see strong growth

Europe remains the most popular region for Czech travelers, but demand for long-haul destinations is also changing. According to Letuška.cz, Latin America and the Caribbean have recorded the sharpest year-on-year increases, with demand growing by hundreds of percent in some cases.

The Caribbean in particular has benefited from rising interest among travelers looking beyond Europe. Latin American destinations have also seen a significant increase in bookings compared with the same period last year.

The stronger demand is coinciding with changes in the competitive landscape. New routes from Prague are challenging airlines that have traditionally carried passengers to Asia and Australia through Middle Eastern hubs.

Major Gulf carriers including Emirates, Qatar Airways and Etihad are responding with promotional fares, adding further pressure to ticket prices.

World.title: Five Free Things to Do in Prague This October
World.content:
Prague will offer a range of free cultural events in October, from exhibitions and science films to family entertainment and hands-on craft workshops.

Several major institutions will also open their doors to the public on October 28, Czech Independence Day.



Here are five events where the main program is free, followed by a guide to some of the places that can be visited without charge on the October 28 public holiday.

Free admission at the National Gallery

October 3–4 and October 28, 10:00 AM–6:00 PM

The National Gallery Prague will offer free access to selected exhibitions on two occasions in October.

On October 3 and 4, visitors can see 1956–1989: Architecture for Everyone at the Trade Fair Palace (Veletržní palác) without paying an entrance fee. The offer forms part of Architecture Day, this year’s festival built around the theme “I Dwell, Therefore I Am.”

The Architecture Day program will also include free tours and workshops at several National Gallery sites, including the Trade Fair Palace, the Convent of St. Agnes of Bohemia and Schwarzenberg Palace. Some activities require advance registration.

Another opportunity comes on October 28, when the National Gallery will waive admission to its eight permanent exhibitions. The program includes medieval and Old Master collections as well as exhibitions covering the First Republic, the period from 1939 to 2021 and Asian art.

The free admission applies to the specified permanent collections and does not cover all temporary exhibitions. The gallery is also preparing additional activities for the public holiday.

Midnight Circus brings family entertainment to Prague 8

October 3, 10:00 AM–7:00 PM and October 4, 10:00 AM–12:00 PM – DDM Prague 8 – Spirála, Přemyšlenská 15

The Spirála Children and Youth Center in Kobylisy will become a temporary circus venue during the first weekend of October.

Midnight Circus will feature clowns, fortune tellers, a storyteller and a House of Horrors, alongside other attractions aimed at families. Visitors can also enter a themed bathhouse.

The daytime program is free and does not require advance registration. Instead of paying directly for individual attractions, visitors receive “Principálky” at the entrance, a special circus currency that can also be earned through activities during the event.

An evening show on Saturday will feature a UV light performance followed by a fire show. Unlike the daytime program, this performance requires a ticket costing CZK 50, payable in cash at the venue. It is not recommended for children younger than five.

Try traditional crafts at the New Town Hall

October 13–14, 8:00 AM–4:00 PM – New Town Hall, Karlovo náměstí 1/23, Prague 2

The New Town Hall will host the 13th edition of Crafts Live (Řemesla živě), an event designed to introduce visitors to traditional and practical trades and the schools where they can be studied.

Visitors will have the opportunity to try different crafts for themselves and speak directly with representatives of vocational schools about their courses and study programs.

Admission to the event is free, although some individual workshops may charge a fee.

Science documentaries come to Suchdol

October 19–22 – Czech University of Life Sciences Prague, Suchdol

The Prague Science Film Fest returns with a program of international science documentaries, including several Czech premieres.

The films explore subjects ranging from the way the human brain can mislead us to the role of fungi and the behavior of otters. Among the scheduled titles are How the Brain Tricks Us, My Otter Diary and The Kingdom of Fungi.

Film screenings will be accompanied by discussions with scientists, filmmakers and other experts, giving visitors an opportunity to explore the topics beyond the films themselves.

The festival will also include an outdoor screening of the Oscar-nominated documentary Fire of Love, an exhibition focused on antelope conservation in Africa and a filmmaking workshop.

Admission is free, and this year’s program does not require registration.

Where to go for free on October 28

October 28 is a public holiday in Czechia, marking the establishment of the independent Czechoslovak state in 1918. Several important Prague buildings traditionally open to visitors on the day.

Straka Academy

The seat of the Czech government will open its meeting rooms, press rooms and garden to the public. The exact visiting hours had not yet been announced at the time of publication.

Wallenstein Palace and Kolowrat Palace

The Czech Senate will open both buildings from 7:30 AM to 5:00 PM. Visitors will be able to see, among other areas, the Senate meeting hall.

Thun Palace

The Chamber of Deputies will open Thun Palace on Sněmovní Street from 9:00 AM to 4:00 PM. Tours start at the main entrance at Sněmovní 4.

Municipal House

The representative rooms on the first floor, including Smetana Hall and the Mayor’s Hall, will be accessible free of charge from 9:00 AM to 3:00 PM. Guided commentary in Smetana Hall will be available every 15 minutes.

World.title: Czech Women Win Billie Jean King Cup Again After Eight Years
World.content:
Czech Republic eased past Ukraine to win the Billie Jean King Cup for the 12th time.

This year’s Wimbledon finalists Linda Noskova and Karolina Muchova breezed past their opponents to secure a 2-0 victory and deny the Ukrainians a first title in the competition.



Muchova, the runner-up at Wimbledon, comfortably beat Anhelina Kalinina 6-2 6-3 in the opening singles match before Noskova’s 6-3 ⁠7-6 (7-5) win over world number seven Elina Svitolina ‌secured the title.

It is the Czechs’ first win at the event since 2018, making them the second-most successful nation in its history after the United States, who have 18 titles.

In her first year as Czechia captain, Barbora Strycova has made history.

Former Grand Slam doubles champion Strycova is just the fourth woman to win the Billie Jean King Cup as both a player and a captain. Strycova joins a Hall of Fame cast of Margaret Court, Chrissie Evert and Billie Jean King in achieving that feat.

CZECHIA'S NEW ALL-STARS ARE WORLD CHAMPIONS 🇨🇿🏆#BJKCup pic.twitter.com/W8B2WucxI0 — Billie Jean King Cup (@BJKCup) September 27, 2026

She’s also the first player in event history to win the Billie Jean King Cup juniors title as a player and the Billie Jean King Cup title as a player and a captain. Strycova won the Billie Jean King Cup juniors title alongside Petra Cetkovska and Lucie Safarova in 2001.

The Czechs also knocked out Great Britain in the quarter-finals in Shenzhen, China, which led GB captain Anne Keothavong to describe them as “the strongest team here”.

World.title: Bolt and Lucid Plan 25,000 Autonomous Vehicles Across Europe
World.content:
Bolt and U.S. electric vehicle maker Lucid Group have announced a partnership to develop autonomous mobility services in Europe, with plans to deploy more than 25,000 fully autonomous vehicles across European cities over the coming years.

The vehicles will be based on Lucid’s upcoming Midsize platform and use NVIDIA Hyperion, a reference architecture and development platform for autonomous vehicles.



The companies plan to develop the vehicles for SAE Level 4 autonomous driving, which allows vehicles to operate without human control within defined conditions.

Bolt says the project is part of its wider ambition to have 100,000 autonomous vehicles operating on its platform by 2035.

The companies will work together from the early stages of vehicle development. Bolt will contribute traffic and mobility data, operational experience and knowledge of European markets, while Lucid will provide its software-defined vehicle platform and automotive technology.

Bolt will also define requirements covering the vehicle, software, safety and passenger experience. Its autonomous driving division will oversee the partnership and develop the infrastructure needed to operate the fleet.

This will include vehicle dispatch, charging, maintenance, remote assistance and customer support. Bolt also plans to own and operate the autonomous vehicles itself.

Rollout will depend on local regulations

The companies have not yet announced which European cities will receive the service first.

Bolt and Lucid said launches will take place city by city and depend on local regulations, official approvals and operational readiness. The companies also plan to work with autonomous driving technology providers, European regulators and policymakers before introducing the service.

For the foreseeable future, autonomous vehicles on the Bolt platform will operate alongside vehicles driven by human drivers.

Lucid’s side of the project will be led by Lucid Technologies, a newly established division bringing together artificial intelligence, advanced driver-assistance systems, autonomous driving and other digital technologies.

Bolt currently operates in more than 850 cities across 50 countries and says its platform serves more than 200 million customers. Its services include ride-hailing, car-sharing, electric scooters and food and grocery delivery.

Lucid Group, listed on the Nasdaq under the ticker LCID, develops electric vehicles and related technologies. The company operates manufacturing facilities in Arizona and Saudi Arabia.

World.title: Prague Airport Works to Speed Up Border Checks for Non-EU Travellers
World.content:
Prague Airport and the Czech Ministry of the Interior are preparing additional measures to reduce waiting times for passengers arriving from non-Schengen countries following the introduction of the EU Entry/Exit System (EES).

The new system has made border checks more complex, particularly for travellers from outside the EU. Prague Airport says it has already introduced several measures aimed at keeping passenger flows moving during busy periods.



Airport staff, known as the Red Team, are assisting passengers in the terminal, directing them through the new procedures and providing information where needed. The airport has also adjusted passenger flow corridors based on data collected since the system was introduced.

One of the main issues identified so far is the self-service registration process. According to the airport, a significant number of passengers do not complete their registration at the kiosks, which can lead to additional delays at passport control.

Prague Airport is therefore examining the entire journey from the registration kiosks to passport control and looking at ways to make the process easier, particularly for families and older passengers.

“Data has shown us that the most common delays occur when people interrupt the registration process at the terminals,” said Radomír Lašák, Chairman of the Board of Prague Airport. “Together with the Police of the Czech Republic, we are not merely putting together temporary stopgaps but are redesigning the entire process so that it remains resilient even during peak periods.”

Further measures are also being prepared at the European level, including the possibility of allowing passengers to complete parts of the EES registration before departure. Airlines could also provide passengers with information about the process during flights.

The Czech Ministry of the Interior and the Immigration Police are working with Prague Airport on the next steps and have committed additional resources to help manage the new system.

Interior Minister Lubomír Metnar said the authorities’ priority was to maintain security standards while limiting the impact of the new procedures on passengers.

The airport said it will continue monitoring passenger flows and adjusting its procedures based on actual operations, particularly during peak travel periods.

World.title: Czech Statehood Day 2026: What Is Open and What to Do in Prague
World.content:
September 28 is a public holiday in the Czech Republic, marking Czech Statehood Day and the feast of St. Wenceslas. This year, the holiday falls on a Monday, giving many people a three-day weekend.

For anyone planning to spend the day in Prague, however, there are two practical questions: which shops will be open, and what can you do around the city?



Where you can shop on September 28

Under Czech legislation regulating retail opening hours, shops with a sales area of more than 200 square meters must close on September 28.

The restriction applies throughout the day and covers large supermarkets, hypermarkets and home improvement stores.

Smaller shops with sales areas of up to 200 square meters are exempt and can open at their owners’ discretion. Petrol stations and pharmacies can also operate.

Other exceptions include shops located at airports, railway stations and bus terminals, as well as retail outlets inside healthcare facilities.

Why September 28 is Czech Statehood Day

The holiday commemorates Prince Wenceslas, a member of the Přemyslid dynasty who became one of the central figures in Czech history.

Wenceslas was killed by his brother Boleslav I on September 28, 935, in Stará Boleslav. His death later became the foundation of a cult that developed around him from the late 10th century onward.

His remains were transferred to Prague in 938 on Boleslav’s orders and buried in the Rotunda of St. Vitus. The reasons behind the transfer are not known with certainty, but the move helped strengthen Wenceslas’s status as a religious figure while also reinforcing Prague’s position as the center of the emerging Czech state.

Over the following centuries, Wenceslas became the patron saint of the Czech lands and an important symbol of Czech statehood.

The connection between Wenceslas and Czech political tradition was further strengthened under Charles IV, who commissioned the Crown of Saint Wenceslas. The crown became one of the principal symbols of the Czech monarchy and remains part of the Czech Crown Jewels.

See the Czech Crown Jewels at Prague Castle

September 28 is also the final day of this year’s exhibition of the Czech Crown Jewels at Prague Castle.

The jewels are being displayed in Vladislav Hall as part of the exhibition Habsburgs 500. Admission is free, and the display also includes a coronation robe dating from 1653 and other historical objects.

The exhibition closes at the end of the day on September 28.

Government buildings open to visitors

Several normally restricted buildings will also be accessible to the public.

Straka Academy, the official seat of the Czech government, will open its doors on September 28. Visitors can see the government meeting room, ceremonial areas and the building’s garden.

The program also includes an interactive exhibition called Journey of the Republic. Tours are free and begin at 10 a.m., with the final group scheduled to leave at 5 p.m.

The Ministry of Finance on Letenská Street will also welcome visitors. Tours start at 9:30 a.m. and include the ministry’s historic premises and the former monastery.

Museums and other attractions

The National Technical Museum in Letná will remain open on September 28, giving visitors access to its permanent exhibitions.

The Postal Museum will also be open.

For those looking for a more traditional Prague attraction, September 28 will be the final chance this year to ride the historic Letná Carousel.

Another option is the National Museum, where the Přemyslids exhibition examines the history of the dynasty that ruled the Czech lands during the country’s early medieval period.

The exhibition runs until October 15, 2026, making the public holiday particularly relevant for visitors interested in the history behind Czech Statehood Day.

World.title: Breaking: Former Orbán-era minister Hankó detained and taken to Kecskemét
World.content:
Former Culture and Innovation Minister Balázs Hankó has been detained after Parliament lifted his immunity over the National Cultural Fund corruption case. His lawyer says Hankó was taken from Budapest to Kecskemét for further procedural measures.

Hankó detained after arriving for questioning

Balázs Hankó, a Fidesz–KDNP MP and former minister responsible for the National Cultural Fund (NKA), was detained late on Monday and taken from Budapest to Kecskemét, according to his lawyer, Gábor Tóth M.

Hankó had received a summons from the prosecutor’s office after Parliament suspended his immunity earlier that day. He went to the National Tax and Customs Administration (NAV) facility on Huszti Road in Budapest as requested, but was subsequently detained.

“Somewhat illogically, my client was detained at the NAV facility on Huszti Road, where we had been summoned and, naturally, complied with the summons,” Tóth told Telex. “He was then taken to Kecskemét by a NAV tactical unit, where procedural measures will take place overnight.”

The Bács-Kiskun County Prosecutor’s Office said it could not provide information about an ongoing procedural measure.

Hankó denies wrongdoing

Hankó’s immunity was suspended by Parliament on Monday, alongside that of former National Development Minister Miklós Seszták and Prime Minister Péter Magyar.

The decision cleared the way for proceedings against Hankó in connection with allegations surrounding the NKA. Prosecutors allege that the NKA’s Temporary College for Priority Cultural Programmes used public funds for purposes outside those defined by law in 1,079 cases between September 2025 and March 2026, causing HUF 17.3 billion (around EUR 44 million) in financial damage.

Hankó has rejected the allegations, saying that neither he nor anyone else stole money from the NKA and that the funds were used to support cultural programmes, as intended.

Earlier on Monday, he described the case as politically motivated and said he was prepared to have his immunity lifted in order to clear his name and that of his colleagues.

A dramatic end to a long day

Hankó spent much of Monday inside Parliament as speculation grew about his whereabouts. He later said he had not been hiding and had been working inside the parliamentary building.

After receiving his summons in the evening, he left Parliament. His departure was broadcast live, and an awkward moment followed when the car waiting to take him to the prosecutor’s office drove away without him after he had said goodbye to his family and placed his bags inside.

He eventually made his way to the NAV facility, where he was detained.

The NKA case has already resulted in several arrests, including former NKA vice-president Balázs Bús and several other people linked to the distribution of the disputed funds. Hankó is now the latest high-profile figure to face criminal proceedings in the investigation.

World.title: Former minister Hankó’s dramatic departure takes an awkward turn as his car drives off without him – Video
World.content:
Fidesz–KDNP MP Balázs Hankó left Hungary’s Parliament on Monday evening after receiving a summons from prosecutors, but his emotional farewell took an unexpected turn when the car waiting to take him away drove off without him.

Hankó leaves Parliament after receiving summons

Balázs Hankó, a former culture and innovation minister and current Fidesz–KDNP MP, left Parliament shortly after 7:30 PM on Monday after receiving a summons from the relevant prosecutor’s office.

Earlier in the day, Parliament had voted 139–0, with no abstentions, to suspend his parliamentary immunity. Prosecutors are investigating him in connection with the National Cultural Fund (NKA) case, alleging that decisions made while he was minister and president of the NKA caused HUF 17.3 billion in financial damage.

Hankó has rejected the allegations and described the case as a politically motivated prosecution. He said earlier on Monday that he had refuted all the accusations and that his conscience was clear. His lawyer had also informed prosecutors that Hankó would appear whenever summoned.

An emotional farewell outside Parliament

Hankó had spent much of Monday inside the Parliament building, after previously saying that he would remain there and wait for the authorities to arrest him. After receiving the summons at around 7:20 PM, however, he finally left.

His departure was broadcast live on former Prime Minister Viktor Orbán’s Facebook page, giving viewers a front-row seat to an unusually dramatic farewell.

Hankó paused outside Parliament and reflected on the Budapest skyline, saying:

“If you look at how beautifully we built this capital and renovated it…”

He then approached a car that had apparently been waiting to take him to the prosecutor’s office.

Before getting in, Hankó asked for a moment to say goodbye to his wife, his three sons, his daughter and his father. Members of his parliamentary group also gathered around him, with supporters calling out phrases including “We are with you, Balázs”, “Stay strong” and “We’ll be waiting for you.” Then things took an unexpected turn.

The car drives away without him

After Hankó placed his bags on the back seat and closed the car door, the vehicle suddenly pulled away,

without Hankó.

The former minister tried to call after the car, but the driver was already heading away, apparently believing that his passenger had got into the vehicle. Hankó was then seen hesitantly walking after the departing car before the live broadcast ended:

What is Hankó accused of?

The case concerns the National Cultural Fund, which Hankó headed while serving as minister. According to prosecutors, the NKA’s Temporary College for Priority Cultural Programmes improperly allocated public funds 1,079 times between 3 September 2025 and 30 March 2026, using money for purposes outside those defined by law. Prosecutors say this caused HUF 17.3 billion in financial damage, Telex writes.

Hankó denies wrongdoing. He has said that all decisions in the NKA case complied with the law and that neither he nor anyone else stole money from the fund. With his parliamentary immunity now suspended, the legal obstacle to investigating him as a potential suspect has been removed. However, the suspension itself does not constitute a finding of guilt.

Hankó’s former government colleague Miklós Seszták also had his immunity suspended on Monday in a separate corruption case and was later detained at the Central Investigative Prosecutor’s Office.

World.title: Budapest Assembly ends free parking for electric cars
World.content:
A petition challenging Budapest’s planned parking changes has gained momentum, even after the city council voted to soften some measures affecting electric cars.

The original rules, due to take effect on 1 January 2027, would have ended free parking for vehicles with green number plates and introduced double parking fees for cars weighing more than two tonnes. The Budapest General Assembly has now amended both measures.

Electric cars to receive 50 per cent discount

Under the latest decision, purely electric and hydrogen-powered vehicles with green number plates will receive a 50 per cent parking discount until 1 July 2030. As villanyautósok.hu reported, the assembly rejected a proposal to extend free parking until 2030.

The change means electric vehicles will lose their completely free parking status from 2027, but will not immediately face the standard parking rate. The petition, launched through the Budapest Municipality’s official civic initiative platform, calls for the new rules to be withdrawn and for electric cars to retain more favourable parking conditions.

The initiative attracted almost 2,000 signatures within its first two days, reportedly making it the most successful civic initiative on the capital’s platform at that point. If it reaches 1,000 supporters, the mayor or a deputy mayor must consult its initiator; at 10,000 signatures, the General Assembly must put the proposal on its agenda. Only private individuals with a Budapest residential address can sign.

Petition argues for EV incentives

The initiative, launched by Ádám Bálint and supported by the Hungarian Electromobility Association, argues that electric cars should retain preferential treatment because they produce no tailpipe emissions and generally generate less brake dust through regenerative braking. Supporters also point to their lower noise emissions.

The petition does not demand permanent free parking, instead highlighting European cities where electric cars receive reduced rather than zero parking charges.

More on Budapest’s transport: Dangerous goods train derails in the Hungarian capital, causing major rail disruption

Double charge delayed

The planned double parking fee for vehicles weighing more than two tonnes has also been postponed. It will now not take effect until 1 January 2028. The measure is intended to reflect the greater space occupied by larger vehicles and the additional pressure heavier cars place on road infrastructure.

Critics argue that the two-tonne threshold could disproportionately affect electric vehicles, whose large battery packs can make them heavier than comparable petrol or diesel models. The latest amendments have therefore changed, but not ended, the dispute.

Electric vehicle owners will lose free parking from 2027, while the controversial weight-based surcharge has been pushed back by a year. The petition remains active as supporters seek further changes to Budapest’s parking policy.

World.title: Former Fidesz minister gives interview before being detained over EUR 34 million bribery scheme
World.content:
Former Hungarian National Development Minister Miklós Seszták has been detained after Parliament suspended his immunity on Monday, as prosecutors accuse the Fidesz-KDNP politician of accepting HUF billions in bribes during his time in government.

According to details presented to Parliament’s Immunity Committee, the alleged corruption scheme involved HUF 12.6 billion (EUR 34.24 million) in illicit payments connected to state-owned transport contracts, bus purchases and construction projects. The Fidesz MP denies committing any crime and has questioned the basis of the investigation.

Allegations linked to Volánbusz contracts

Seszták served as Fidesz’s national development minister between June 2014 and May 2018. His responsibilities included oversight of state assets, public procurement and the Hungarian National Asset Management Company (Magyar Nemzeti Vagyonkezelő, MNV), as well as transport development.

The most substantial allegation concerns companies holding contracts with state-owned bus operator Volánbusz. According to the prosecution’s case as presented to Parliament, Seszták and the then head of MNV, Norbert Szivek, allegedly received HUF 7.076 billion (almost EUR 19.25 million) in corruption payments between May 2015 and July 2018.

The allegation is that three companies initially paid HUF 115 million (almost EUR 313,000) a month to an intermediary interest group to retain their Volánbusz contracts. The amount was subsequently increased to HUF 130 million (around EUR 353,500), with the payments allegedly redirected to Seszták and Szivek through couriers, writes 444.hu.

A second part of the case concerns bus procurement. Prosecutors allege that 645 new and used buses were purchased through 14 transactions between 2015 and 2017, with suppliers allegedly paying a further HUF 3.7066 billion (appr. EUR 10.1 million) in illicit benefits.

Further payments alleged

The case also includes alleged payments connected to construction projects. According to the parliamentary briefing, one person allegedly delivered more than HUF 1.05 billion (EUR 2.85 million) to Seszták through intermediaries in connection with projects linked to a company named in the investigation. A further HUF 270 million (EUR 734,000) is alleged to have been paid in connection with projects, particularly swimming-pool construction.

Prosecutors allege that the former Fidesz minister used his official position to ensure that companies linked to the people involved repeatedly received contracts and that final contract prices were determined in their favour. The allegations are contained in an 11-page prosecution submission comprising 51 paragraphs.

Seszták rejects the allegations

Seszták has repeatedly denied any wrongdoing. Before entering the Central Investigative Prosecutor’s Office on Monday on his own, the former Fidesz minister said he wanted to give evidence and maintained that he had committed no crime. He was subsequently detained, according to his lawyer.

In an interview with 24.hu conducted before his detention, Seszták said he could not explain the allegations and claimed he suspected that prosecutors had reached a plea agreement with somebody else involved, but he did not name anyone, although he said it is not hard to figure out who the person who knew about everything is.

He did not know there was an ongoing investigation until last week, mainly because he did not speak to the Fidesz leaders, former PM Viktor Orbán and deputy PM Zsolt Semjén due to the case being a criminal proceeding. Seszták also said he would not voluntarily surrender his parliamentary mandate, arguing that there was no reason to do so, while insisting that he was entitled to the presumption of innocence.

Furthermore, Fidesz’s ex-minister highlighted he finds the general sentiment in the country so volatile he can imagine almost anything to happen during the process of holding members of the former government politicians accountable. Seszták also claimed he’s certain that the prerequisites of his arrest do not apply.

Stay up-to-date: Former Fidesz minister detained over alleged corruption – here’s what happens if he’s convicted

Immunity suspended unanimously

Parliament suspended Seszták’s immunity on Monday in a 139–0 vote, clearing the way for prosecutors to proceed against him. Shortly afterwards, he voluntarily went to the prosecutor’s office, where he was detained. The case now moves from the parliamentary stage into the criminal investigation, with the allegations and Seszták’s defence set to be examined by the Hungarian authorities and, ultimately, the courts.

World.title: Dangerous goods train derails in Budapest, causing major rail disruption
World.content:
Three carriages of a freight train carrying kerosene derailed at Rákos station in Budapest on Monday afternoon, with two carriages overturning and one reportedly leaking fuel. Major disruption is expected on several railway lines.

Three carriages derailed at Rákos

Three carriages of a freight train carrying hazardous material derailed at Rákos railway station in Budapest’s 10th district on Monday afternoon, according to Mávinform.

The train was carrying kerosene. Two of the tankers overturned, while a third was left dangerously tilted near Jászberényi Road.

One of the overturned carriages was reportedly leaking kerosene. Firefighters quickly contained the leak, according to Hungary’s disaster management authority. Rail traffic at Rákos station was suspended at 4:30 PM to allow technical rescue operations to begin. A complete track closure is currently in effect on the affected section.

Major disruption on Budapest–Miskolc and Budapest–Békéscsaba routes

The incident is expected to cause significant disruption during the afternoon on the Budapest–Hatvan–Miskolc and Budapest–Szolnok–Békéscsaba railway lines.

Several services have been shortened or diverted as a result.

Budapest–Miskolc InterCity services, including the Tokaj and Hernád-Zemplén, only run as far as Hatvan from Miskolc and depart from Hatvan in the opposite direction.

Budapest–Békéscsaba InterCity services only run as far as Szolnok.

The Agria and Mátra InterRégió services operate between Gödöllő and Gyöngyös/Eger.

Tokaj and Nyírség InterCity services are being diverted via Cegléd.

S76 trains only operate between Újpalota and Pilisvörösvár.

S60/Z60 services to Sülysáp and Szolnok depart from Rákoshegy instead of Rákos.

If you missed it: Budapest transport update: Major tram changes from Monday, Sziget bridge renovation ahead

Replacement buses and alternative transport

Replacement buses are operating between Keleti railway station and Pécel instead of S80 and InterRégió services, and between Keleti and Hatvan instead of InterCity services. Additional replacement buses are running between Keleti and Rákoshegy.

MÁV is also recommending the H8 HÉV suburban railway line as an alternative. Passengers holding valid railway tickets can use several BKK services at no additional cost, including:

M2 metro;

H8 HÉV;

M3 metro between Deák Ferenc tér and Kőbánya-Kispest;

M4 metro between Keleti pályaudvar and Kálvin tér;

168E, 161 and 262 buses;

97E and 169E buses, which also stop at Rákos railway station;

98, 98E and 198 buses.

Passengers travelling through Budapest this afternoon should allow extra time and check the latest service information before setting off, as the restrictions may change while the technical rescue operation continues.

World.title: Hungary’s largest bank OTP could quit Russia as potential new deal reshapes plans
World.content:
Hungary’s largest bank, OTP, is reviewing its strategy in Russia and is considering a complete withdrawal from the country, Chief Executive Officer Péter Csányi has told Bloomberg.

The review comes as OTP seeks regulatory approval for its planned acquisition of Baltic banking group Luminor, a deal that would significantly expand its presence in the euro area. OTP expects the review to be completed by the end of 2026, with the decision taking into account long-term shareholder value and the bank’s strategic commitment to the Baltic region.

Luminor deal sharpens focus on Russia

The Russian operation remains profitable. According to figures reported by Bloomberg, its profit reached approximately HUF 202 billion (about EUR 550.3 million) last year, having increased more than fivefold since 2021. OTP has also repatriated around EUR 774.4 million in dividends from its Russian subsidiary. Csányi said limited progress in bringing additional dividends out of Russia was one reason for the strategic review.

OTP agreed in July to acquire Luminor Holding from DNB and funds managed by Blackstone. The Baltic banking group operates across Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania. The deal would strengthen OTP’s position in the euro area while putting renewed focus on its continued presence in Russia. Estonian Finance Minister Jürgen Ligi has said the bank’s Russian operations are a moral shame, while Baltic regulators have also raised concerns.

OTP has already scaled back in Russia and laid eyes on something else

OTP Bank Group has continued operating in Russia since the full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, although it says it has substantially reduced its activities there. The bank suspended corporate lending after the outbreak of the war and withdrew intra-group financing from its Russian subsidiary. Its current Russian operations are largely focused on retail consumer lending and deposits.

OTP said it has reduced its Russian workforce by 25 per cent and its branch network by 40 per cent. At the same time, its Ukrainian business has expanded, with the bank reporting a 35 per cent increase in its loan portfolio in 2025.

Bloomberg documents raise questions

Bloomberg reported that documents it reviewed show that some OTP customers included companies controlled by Gazprom, while other customers provided services to organisations linked to Russian intelligence. One set of emails from April and May 2026 discussed a potential payment arrangement involving Gazprom Export, Gazprom-controlled Yugorosgaz and Gazprom subsidiary Rosingaz.

Under one proposed arrangement, money would have been transferred from a Yugorosgaz euro account at OTP Serbia to a Rosingaz account at Serbia’s state-owned Banka Poštanska Štedionica. The documents do not establish that the transaction was completed. OTP said it conducted an internal review following Bloomberg’s questions and found no evidence that any member of the OTP Group had breached applicable sanctions. The bank reiterated its commitment to complying with UN, EU, US and UK sanctions.

Leaving won’t be so easy

Selling the Russian subsidiary could prove complicated. OTP says Russian rules and international restrictions make finding an acceptable buyer difficult, while sellers leaving Russia can realise only a fraction of an asset’s market value. The bank has previously said that selling its Russian business is currently “practically impossible”.

OTP therefore faces a strategic choice between retaining a profitable but increasingly isolated operation and pursuing a deeper European focus through its planned Luminor acquisition. The outcome of the review, expected by the end of the year, could determine the future of OTP’s two-decade presence in Russia.

World.title: Green light for 280 new Budapest homes as huge development acquires permits
World.content:
Belgian property developer Atenor has secured a building permit for BakerStreet II, a new residential development in Budapest’s 11th district that will bring 280 apartments to the capital’s housing market.

Three buildings and 26,700 square metres of residential space

The project is a big change in direction for the site, which was originally intended for office development. Atenor has reassessed the concept in response to changing conditions in Budapest’s property market and the company’s growing focus on residential projects. Construction and pre-sales are expected to begin in the first quarter of 2027, with completion scheduled for the second quarter of 2029.

BakerStreet II will comprise three buildings containing a total of 280 homes, with approximately 26,700 square metres of residential space. A landscaped inner courtyard will form a central feature of the development, incorporating substantial green areas as well as communal facilities designed for residents. The project is situated in an established and developing part of the 11th district, with access to the Danube and nearby university campuses.

Atenor Hungary managing director János Martin said BakerStreet II, together with the company’s Lake 11 development, would strengthen its residential offering in a well-connected and rapidly developing part of Budapest, quotes Portfolio. The shift towards residential development reflects a broader change in Atenor’s strategy in the Hungarian capital, where housing projects are becoming an increasingly important part of its assets.

The inner park of the planned project. Source: Atenor

BakerStreet II joins Lake 11

The new development will complement Lake 11, another major Atenor residential project in Budapest’s 11th district, near Lake Kána. Lake 11 is being developed in several phases and is ultimately planned to include nearly 900 apartments, alongside approximately 2,300 square metres of commercial space. The first phase, Lake 11 Home&Park, consists of 265 apartments and has already been completed.

World.title: Former Orbán-era minister detained over alleged corruption: here’s what happens if he’s convicted
World.content:
Former National Development Minister Miklós Seszták has been detained at Hungary’s Central Investigative Prosecutor’s Office after Parliament suspended his immunity over corruption allegations dating back to his time in government.

Seszták detained after going to prosecutor’s office

Miklós Seszták, a Christian Democrat MP and former Minister of National Development, was detained on Monday at the Central Investigative Prosecutor’s Office, his lawyer, Gábor Papp, told 24.hu.

Seszták did not attend Parliament for the vote on his immunity. Instead, he went to the prosecutor’s office, saying that he intended to give a statement. He maintains that he is innocent.

Earlier on Monday, Parliament voted 139–0, with no abstentions, to suspend Seszták’s parliamentary immunity. The decision allows criminal proceedings against him to move forward in connection with corruption cases outlined by prosecutors last week.

If convicted, Seszták could face up to 10 years in prison.

Prosecutors allege billions in illegal benefits

The Central Investigative Prosecutor’s Office has alleged that there are well-founded grounds to suspect that Seszták accepted bribes worth hundreds of millions or even several billion forints from construction contractors while serving as Minister of National Development between 2014 and 2018.

According to prosecutors, Seszták and Norbert Szivek, who was CEO of the Hungarian National Asset Management Company at the time, obtained HUF 11 billion (approximately EUR 30 million) in unlawful benefits.

The prosecution has also referred to other incriminating testimony against Seszták. These are allegations, and Seszták has denied committing any crime.

After prosecutors requested the suspension of his immunity, he previously said that every element of the allegations was unfounded.

“I have not committed any crime, and I am not aware of any crime having been committed,”

he said at the time.

Living, working or doing business in Hungary?

Make things easier with professional support in English. Explore Daily News Hungary’s Services in English and find the help you need.

A political career spanning decades

Seszták, born in 1968, graduated in law from Eötvös Loránd University in Budapest in 1994 and began working as a lawyer two years later, Telex writes.

He entered local politics in Kisvárda in 1998 and became a member of the National Assembly for the Fidesz–KDNP alliance in 2010. He won the Kisvárda constituency again in 2014, 2018 and 2022.

He served as Minister of National Development from 2014 to 2018, overseeing a ministry with responsibility for a wide range of economic and state-owned assets.

Seszták remained a member of Parliament after leaving government and was among Hungary’s wealthiest MPs for years. He entered the current Parliament from the Fidesz–KDNP national list as a member of the KDNP parliamentary group.

However, he lost his Kisvárda constituency in the 2026 election, when Tisza candidate Viktória Dicső defeated him by six percentage points.

If you missed it: Breaking: Hungarian parliament suspends PM Magyar’s immunity over alleged phone theft

Previous controversies surrounding Seszták

These corruption allegations are not the first controversy to have surrounded Seszták. In 2013, before he became minister, Átlátszó reported that five companies had won a combined HUF 12.5 billion in funding in a tender for developing broadband optical networks. The companies had reportedly been established shortly beforehand and registered at the same address, while belonging to a group in which Seszták had served as a supervisory board member.

In 2014, Index reported that Seszták had been involved over several years in establishing hundreds of companies, many registered in the names of Russian and Ukrainian nationals at addresses in Kisvárda. According to the report, more than 700 companies were involved, many of which were later liquidated with outstanding debts.

Seszták has also remained one of the wealthier members of Parliament. His 2026 asset declaration lists two properties in Budapest and three in Kisvárda, as well as HUF 869 million in government securities, HUF 103 million in investment funds and HUF 32.7 million in shares. He declared HUF 66 million in bank deposits and HUF 20 million in cash.

The current corruption allegations concern events from Seszták’s period as minister between 2014 and 2018. The suspension of his immunity and his detention do not amount to a finding of guilt; any criminal liability will ultimately be determined through the judicial process.

World.title: Kosovo MPs Voice ‘Deep Concern’ Over Guerrilla Leaders’ Conviction
World.content:
This post is also available in this language: Shqip Bos/Hrv/Srp



Kosovo MPs in session on September 28, 2026. Photo: BIRN.

In a rare show of unanimity, Kosovo MPs on Monday adopted a statement expressing “deep concern” over this month’s Hague court conviction for war crimes of four former leaders of the Kosovo Liberation Army, KLA – Hashim Thaci, Kadri Veseli, Rexhep Selimi and Jakup Krasniqi.

The statement supported by 99 MPs calls on Kosovo’s institutions to take action “to protect the truth and purity of the liberation war of the people of Kosovo”. Ethnic Serb MPs from the Belgrade-backed Srpska Lista party were not present for the vote.

The text calls for the drafting of a common state strategy that would coordinate actions “for the protection and affirmation of the full historical truth about the just war for freedom and liberation of Kosovo.

“[Parliament] considers the conclusion [of the verdict] on the existence of a common criminal intent unacceptable,”= the statement added.

Kosovo’s ex-President, Thaci, and his co-defendants, former parliament speakers Krasniqi and Veseli and former MP Selimi, were sentenced to 25, 25, 18 and 13 years in jail respectively on September 16.

All four were found guilty of responsibility for crimes carried out while they were senior officials of the KLA during the 1998-99 war with Serbian forces.

They were found not guilty of crimes against humanity, of persecution, imprisonment, other inhumane acts, torture, murder and enforced disappearances.

Thaci, Veseli, Krasniqi and Selimi all pleaded not guilty to all charges and will appeal the verdict.

Since the verdict was announced, hundreds of people have been protesting in the capital, Pristina, and in other cities in Kosovo and abroad. Many Kosovo Albanians deem the Hague verdict an attack on the KLA’s just war for liberation.

The Kosovo Specialist Chambers was created specifically to try former members of the KLA, under pressure from Kosovo’s Western allies. The court is widely disliked in Kosovo, where it is seen as denigrating the KLA’s struggle.

Parallel with the statement, the opposition Democratic Party of Kosovo, PDK, is urging parliament to support amendments to the law on Specialist Chambers, approved in 2015, which would limit the scope of the chambers.

“Parliament has done its job, now it’s for the government to address the draft law [on the Specialist Chambers] responsibly. It should address it with urgency because there is no reason for delays. We saw with the Statement that there is a will. We expect the government to work on it today and send it to parliament tomorrow, or the day after,” Arian Tahiri, head of the PDK parliamentary group, said on Monday.

World.title: Serbia’s Vucic Pardons ‘Novi Sad 12’ as ‘Act of Mercy’ Before Resigning
World.content:
Serbian President Aleksandar Vucic on Sunday said he had pardoned 12 anti-government activists from the city of Novi Sad who are on trial for allegedly preparing “acts against the constitutional order”, in one of his final decisions as President as he announced his resignation before next month’s elections.

Vucic said he had pardoned a total of 49 people, including 23 who are connected to what he called “all these terrible events over the past year and a half” – a reference to mass student-led protests that have shaken his government – including the so-called ‘Novi Sad 12’.

“I made the decision to pardon 12 people from the Novi Sad group led by [activist] Mila Pajic, just as I decided to pardon 11 people who, on the other [pro-government] side, took part in incidents against protesters involved in the blockades,” Vucic said in a speech in Belgrade before submitting his resignation.

He described the decision as an “act of mercy because of their age, not because they are not guilty of something or did not do something. I did so because I know they would have been sentenced to several years in prison in any country, in any other country in the world. And I want to protect every young person because I believe there is hope that they will change and behave much more responsibly in the future,” Vucic said.

He said he had made the decision despite advice from the security services.

The 12 activists, linked to the opposition Free Citizens Movement, PSG, and the activist group Students Against Authoritarian Rule, STAV, were charged with preparing acts against Serbia’s constitutional order and security.

The charges arose from a recording of the meeting between the indictees ahead of a March 2025 rally that became the largest in Serbian history.

Six of them spent more than seven months in detention and house arrest before being released to defend themselves at liberty.

The other six were outside Serbia when the arrests took place and have remained abroad, with proceedings against them conducted in absentia.

One of the six activists in exile, Doroteja Antic, told BIRN that none of them wanted the case to end with a pardon from Vucic, who she claimed was again using the group “for his own political purposes, to score political points”.

“He did not do this out of kindness but solely because it is politically advantageous for him at this moment. And this is the final proof that the case was fabricated and politically constructed from the very beginning, and that there was never really a case at all,” Antic said.

She acknowledged that this should end the court proceedings being conducted against the 12 activists.

“We are now waiting for the final confirmation and official notices from the court that the proceedings have been discontinued, but that is expected to happen soon, at least according to our lawyers,” Antic explained.

However, she said that her plan is to remain outside Serbia while Vucic remains in power, to ensure she is safe.

“My plan is to stay here at least until the elections, in the great hope that after October 25 we will all meet again in a free Serbia, because this really feels like the final moment, the last gasp and cry of a government that people have long wanted to see the back of,” she said.
