World.title: Finance Minister: Moldova Mustn’t Waste EU Funds Intended for Reforms
World.content:
Moldova is preparing draconian but necessary economic and financial reforms designed to align the country with EU standards, says Finance Minister Victoria Belous, and turn the post-Soviet republic into a European one.

However, turning EU financing into better public services is not simple, Belous told BIRN in an interview. Administrative delays are holding up investment, even as the government seeks to finance higher public-sector salaries and prepares tax changes for 2027, she explains.

“The problem for public investment projects is not lack of money but the capacity and efficiency of certain processes which, unfortunately, delay implementation,” Belous said.

This distinction runs through the government’s reform plans generally: spending commitments require dependable income, while investment requires institutions capable of putting projects into practice.

World.title: Hostile Reactions to Kosovo Wartime Leaders’ Verdict Miss Key Point: the Victims’ Ordeal
World.content:
This post is also available in this language: Shqip Bos/Hrv/Srp

The first-instance verdict in the trial of Hashim Thaci, Kadri Veseli, Rexhep Selimi and Jakup Krasniqi before the Kosovo Specialist Chambers was received in Belgrade and Pristina in a predictable manner: as yet another event interpreted through national political narratives.

Belgrade believes the sentences were not severe enough, that the court protected the interests of the Kosovo Liberation Army, KLA, and that it failed to sufficiently take into account the crimes committed against Serbs.

In Pristina, politicians deemed the verdict unjust, and thousands of people took to the streets to express support for the convicted former KLA leaders.

There is nothing new in such reactions. We have witnessed similar responses regarding the verdicts of the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia, ICTY.

World.title: Failings of Bosnia’s ‘Trojka’ Offer Unreformed SDA a Path Back
World.content:
For months, the leadership of Bosnia and Herzegovina’s main Bosniak opposition party, the Party of Democratic Action, SDA, has carefully nurtured a singular political narrative: their return to power is not just an ambition, but a mathematical certainty.

After being pushed into the opposition benches in 2022 by a diverse coalition of civic and multi-ethnic parties known as the ‘Trojka’ [The Trio], the SDA under Bakir Izetbegovic has used the campaign for next month’s elections to frame the current administration as a failed foreign-imposed experiment.

However, beneath the confident rhetoric and aggressive campaign videos, independent analysts say the SDA’s triumphant comeback might be more of an internal propaganda illusion than a reality reflected in public sentiment.

Instead of a structural resurgence, the political landscape reveals a deeper, more systemic stagnation where voters feel trapped between an uninspired opposition and a ruling coalition that has rapidly absorbed the very governing vices it once promised to dismantle.

World.title: Bosnia Court Blocks Republika Srpska From Funding Secessionist Lobbying
World.content:
Bosnian lawmaker Denis Zvizdic, who initiated teh legal challenge. Photo: EPA/FELIPE TRUEBA.

Bosnia’s Constitutional Court on Friday declared that budgetary funds used by Bosnia’s Serb-dominated Republika Srpska entity to pay foreign consulting firms to lobby for independence violate the state’s constitutional architecture.

The ruling targets a consulting agreement signed between the Republika Srpska Representative Office in Vienna and a Montreal-based firm, Dickens & Madson Canada Inc., which listed “the independence of Republika Srpska” as a core political objective.

The legal challenge was initiated in April by a state-level lawmaker, Denis Zvizdic, who argued that using taxpayers’ funds to lobby against Bosnia’s sovereignty and territorial integrity was unconstitutional.

A 2008 ruling allowed the entity to engage foreign firms for general economic promotion. However, the court has now established that funding campaigns explicitly promoting secession represents an assault on the constitutional order.

“The Constitutional Court hereby prohibits all payments from the budget of Republika Srpska regarding the consulting services contract concluded with Dickens & Madson Canada Inc.,” the court said. “Financing lobbying services for goals that run counter to the Constitution of Bosnia and Herzegovina is strictly incompatible with the constitutional order.”

The applicant, Zvizdic, welcomed the announcement, saying the entity had weaponised massive public funds for anti-state campaigns.

“Public money cannot be used to finance lobbying aimed against the state of Bosnia and Herzegovina, its territorial integrity, sovereignty and its institutions,” Zvizdic stated.

“This binding decision establishes a clear legal standard: citizens’ money must serve development and investment, not the undermining of the state,” he added.

Under Bosnia’s state-level laws, entities possess no constitutional right to unilateral secession. Furthermore, ignoring or violating a binding order of the Constitutional Court carries severe penalties.

The court said the full text of the judicial decision will be delivered to all parties and published on its official website within the month.

World.title: Week in Review: Spyware, AI and Arrests
World.content:
Montenegro’s parliament failed to debate a motion to dismiss Andrija Mandic of the right-wing New Serbian Democracy party as speaker because there was no quorum to hold the session. The motion came after Mandic sent a message of condolence to the son of the former Bosnian Serb military commander and genocide convict Ratko Mladic following his recent death.

This episode has renewed questions about how much Mandic’s politics have changed. The one-time opponent of Montenegro’s independence and NATO membership has become a speaker of parliament who now regularly speaks about Montenegro’s European future and works with European officials.

World.title: 3 drones target Iranian opposition camp in northern Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Three drones targeted the Azadi camp, a facility affiliated with the opposition Democratic Party of Iranian Kurdistan (PDKI) in the Koya district southeast of Erbil in the Kurdistan region of Iraq early on Monday.

According to the Kurdistan Regional Government’s (KRG) security agency, Asayish, the attacks took place in two waves between 1:40 and 2:10 a.m. local time.

The attack damaged the facility but resulted in no casualties.

Local Kurdish media, citing anonymous PDKI sources, claimed that the drones used in the attack were Iranian-made “Hadid” versions.

According to Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps-affiliated media agencies, the attacks targeted separatist organizations in the region.

Officials in Iraqi Kurdistan warned that the camp, which has housed displaced Iranian Kurds and the families of the party’s Peshmerga forces for over 25 years, has come under fire several times amid rising regional tensions.

The attack is the latest in a series of drone and missile strikes against Iranian Kurdish dissident sites in Iraq’s Kurdistan region.

World.title: Iraq officially declared as host of 2028 Arabian Gulf Cup
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq has been officially announced as the host country for the 2028 Arabian Gulf Cup, which will be held in either Basra or Baghdad.

The Executive Office of the Arabian Gulf Cup Football Federation (AGCFF) ratified the decision during a meeting in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, where Iraq made the only formal bid to host the event.

The tournament will take place from December 9 to December 22, 2028.

The 27th Arabian Gulf Cup is currently underway in Jeddah, running from September 23 to October 6, 2026.

While Basra is anticipated to be the primary location following the successful conclusion of the 2023 edition, Baghdad is still in contention.

The Iraqi Football Association (IFA) has set a deadline to formally confirm the host city and will be expected to meet all organizational criteria in accordance with authorized standards.

The decision marks the third time Iraq hosts the tournament, with the fifth edition in Baghdad in 1979 and the 25th edition in Basra in 2023.

World.title: Iraq’s oil exports to Jordan completely halt
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s oil exports to Jordan have completely stopped since the end of December 2025, despite ongoing negotiations this year aimed at resuming crude supplies to Amman.

The spokesperson for the Iraqi Oil Ministry, Salim al-Rikabi, told Attaqa News that the halt in exports is linked to commercial matters and other factors involving Iraq’s State Oil Marketing Organization (SOMO) and the Jordanian side.

Al-Rikabi’s remarks come amid ongoing disputes regarding the terms of a new agreement. Informed sources had previously revealed Baghdad’s insistence on reducing tanker transport fees, while months of negotiations failed to result in a resumption of supplies.

Jordan used to receive approximately 10,000 barrels per day of Iraqi crude—representing about seven percent of its oil needs—before shipments ceased at the end of 2025.

In January, Amman has not imported oil from Iraq, compared to approximately 309,712 barrels the previous month.

Iraq’s oil supplies to Jordan stood at around 299,824 barrels in November 2025, reflecting a steady flow of approximately 300,000 barrels per month during the period before the suspension takes place.

The previous annual contract expired on June 26, 2025, prior to a three-month extension running from October through December. The extension was intended to ensure the completion of the delivery of specified volumes that had been impacted by logistical challenges.

World.title: US troops completely withdraw from Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – An Iraqi government official announced on Sunday that the withdrawal of the US troops from Iraq has been completed.

The official stated that both combat and logistical support personnel have departed the country, although there has been no formal confirmation from the US side, Sky News Arabia reported.

In 2024, Iraq and the United States agreed on a timeline to end the US military presence in the country. According to the US Department of Defense, approximately 2,500 US troops had been stationed in Iraq in the past few years.

Prior to the withdrawal, US forces were deployed across Erbil in the Kurdistan region of Iraq, a base near Baghdad International Airport, and locations within the Green Zone in the capital, Baghdad.

US forces returned to Iraq in 2014 in response to a request by the Iraqi government—as part of the international coalition to combat ISIS—three years after their withdrawal following the 2003 US invasion.

While the terrorist group’s defeat in Iraq was announced in 2017, its cells remain in remote areas.

The withdrawal comes as Iraq faces security consequences linked to the conflict involving Iran, amid recent attacks targeting US facilities and forces.

World.title: India buys two million barrels of Iraqi oil at $28 discount per barrel
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Indian Oil Corp. (IOC), India’s largest state-owned refiner, has acquired 2 million barrels of Iraqi oil at a discount of almost $28 per barrel compared to the October Dubai benchmark.

The acquisition includes Basrah medium and heavy crude oil grades. IOC contracted to receive the cargo from the international trading business Mercuria on a free-on-board (FOB) basis, according to Reuters.

The crude is expected to be loaded and lifted between October 21 and October 31, 2026.

The enormous $28 reduction is due to significant regional logistics challenges. Shipping disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz, which are associated with wider geopolitical tensions, have led to substantial increases in marine freight prices, insurance costs, and transit risks for buyers.

To address these export restrictions and ensure that its oil remains attractive to major global consumers like India, significant price discounts have been introduced. These discounts aim to offset the heightened risks that refiners encounter when arranging their own transportation.

This acquisition comes after IOC purchased one million barrels of October-loading Iraqi crude straight from Iraq’s State Oil Marketing Organization (SOMO) at a discount ranging between $23 and $28 per barrel only a few days ago.

World.title: Iraq recovers 80 smuggled artifacts
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s Ministry of Justice successfully repatriated 80 smuggled historical artifacts and rare artworks on Monday, September 28, 2026, marking another breakthrough in federal legal campaigns to recover looted antiquities from abroad.

According to an official statement issued by the ministry, the restitution was finalized through intensive international legal proceedings managed by the Directorate of External Litigation, executed in direct operational coordination with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Embassy of the Republic of Iraq in Washington, D.C.

The ministry stated that the legal recovery operations, directed and monitored by Minister of Justice Dr. Khaled Shwani, form an integral part of Baghdad’s overarching policy to safeguard Iraq’s cultural heritage and reclaim sovereign historical assets dispersed through illicit trading networks.

Through its dedicated Department for the Recovery of Antiquities and Assets, the Directorate of External Litigation manages active cross-border claims, targeting antiquities illegally excavated from unmonitored archaeological digs as well as stolen cataloged pieces traded internationally in violation of Iraqi heritage statutes and UNESCO conventions.

Federal judicial authorities emphasized that these coordinated actions reflect the justice ministry’s structured legal mandate to track, document, and pursue stolen national assets worldwide.

By leveraging bilateral judicial agreements and working through diplomatic missions across North America and Europe, the Iraqi government aims to ensure the comprehensive preservation of Mesopotamia’s civilizational legacy and institutionalize robust legal frameworks against the illicit trafficking of cultural antiquities.

World.title: Gulf Cup 27: Saudi Arabia, UAE, and Qatar clinch semifinals as Iraq eyes decisive clash
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Matchday Two of the group stage at the 27th Arabian Gulf Cup in Jeddah concluded with three national teams securing early qualification for the semifinals, leaving the remaining knockout berth in Group A contested ahead of the final group round.

Host nation Saudi Arabia confirmed its place in the final four alongside Group B qualifiers the United Arab Emirates and Qatar, while regional football powerhouses Kuwait, Bahrain, and Yemen suffered early mathematical elimination from tournament contention.

In Group A, tournament hosts Saudi Arabia solidified their standing at the summit of the table with a maximum of 6 points and a positive four goal difference following back-to-back victories. Iraq occupies second place with 4 points and a plus-one goal differential, having recorded one win and one draw across their opening fixtures.

Oman sits third with 1 point and a negative three goal differential, while Kuwait trails at the bottom of the group with zero points and a negative two goal difference. The distribution leaves Iraq positioned for a decisive final-round Gulf derby against Saudi Arabia, coinciding with the simultaneous encounter between Oman and Kuwait to determine the group’s second qualifying spot.

Group B witnessed a decisive resolution as both the United Arab Emirates and Qatar secured semifinal qualification with a match to spare, each accumulating 6 points from two consecutive victories. The UAE maintains the top position by virtue of an advantageous goal difference of plus-seven compared to Qatar’s plus-three.

Yemen and Bahrain sit eliminated at the foot of the table without points, both carrying identical negative five goal differentials. The final group fixtures will settle group positioning between the two leading sides as the tournament bracket prepares for the knockout stage.

World.title: Iraq officially licenses Starlink satellite internet
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s Communications and Media Commission (CMC) confirmed on Sunday, September 27, 2026, that satellite internet provider Starlink has secured an official operational license, formally legalizing its low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite broadband services across Iraqi territory.

Speaking to the official state news agency, CMC Chief Executive Officer Baligh Abu Kalal dismissed claims that Iraqi telecommunications traffic and user data are hosted or routed through Qatar, stating that federal security authorities maintain complete sovereign oversight over all network operations and registered hardware within the country.

The licensing milestone follows public contention between federal regulatory bodies and the Ministry of Communications. In mid-August 2026, Minister of Communications Mustafa Sanad argued that the ground gateway servicing Iraq was located in Qatar, raising sovereignty concerns regarding regional content filtering, pornography blocks, and executive internet throttling during national examinations and public demonstrations.

Sanad had framed terrestrial Fiber-to-the-Home (FTTH) expansion as Iraq’s premier digital priority against foreign satellite conglomerates. Responding to these concerns, Abu Kalal clarified that Starlink’s regulatory framework incorporates a rigorous security annex, granting Iraqi intelligence and regulatory apparatuses real-time visibility into all active terminals, user registries, and equipment distributed nationally.

Abu Kalal explained that while initial deployment encountered minor delays due to multi-agency security vetting, the first batch of customer subscription terminals has been released, with sequential hardware shipments proceeding smoothly to fulfill pending consumer orders via the company’s official portal.

Although Starlink originally scheduled the construction of domestic terrestrial ground stations within two years, surging local demand has prompted expedited bilateral negotiations to install local ground gateways across Iraq ahead of schedule.

The CMC executive stressed that satellite internet governance relies fundamentally on sovereign licensing frameworks, statutory compliance, and contractual obligations, ensuring that national security protocols remain fully enforced regardless of atmospheric broadcast mechanics.

World.title: Dhaka begins search for missing Assam woman
World.content:
The Gauhati High Court

NEW DELHI:

Tribunal declared Assam woman a foreigner, but Gauhati HC set it aside

Bangladesh's home ministry told TOI on Monday that it has launched a search for 43-year-old Assam woman Mumtaz Begum, who was sent to Bangladesh in the intervening night of June 13-14 and has been untraceable since. Top bureaucrats in Dhaka also said they were awaiting official communication from India on the case.Dr Ziauddin Ahmed, additional secretary (Political and Immigration), Bangladesh home ministry, whose office deals with border enforcement, illegal crossings and cross-border deportations, said officials were trying to locate Mumtaz but had no information as of Sunday. The matter was sent to police and other depts late on Sept 27, days after TOI reached out.Gauhati HC on Sept 3 directed MEA to "endeavour to locate Mumtaz in Bangladesh and bring her back". The HC also directed Assam govt to pay her husband Mujammel Hoque Rs 2 lakh interim compensation, observing "she was expelled without her husband or an adult family member being informed". HC found it denied her a chance to challenge it, a violation of democratic due process.Underscoring that basic human rights extend to anyone on Indian soil, the bench directed Assam Police and home dept to "ensure that declared foreign nationals are informed about tribunal orders and that their adult family members are notified before they are moved outside their district".The court criticised the tribunal for stripping her of the "opportunity to challenge the Foreigners Tribunal's opinion before Gauhati HC".With no information in India, TOI contacted journalists, human-rights activists, officials and govt and security establishment sources across Bangladesh, focusing on Sylhet division and adjoining districts, where she could have ended up.A senior Dhaka-based businessman, who wishes to stay anonymous, joined authorities in the search and is working with govt and security contacts. An appeal with her photo and identification details, including Foreigners Identification Portal ID, was published in prominent Bengali newspapers on Sept 22. Bangla daily Manob Kantha also carried her photo and reported on the family's search.Official efforts in Sylhet, however, have found no lead. Sylhet Metropolitan Police Commissioner Sarwar Murshed Shamim said police had "tried to locate Mumtaz within the metropolitan area but had not found her and were continuing the search."Mumtaz, from Nagaon, was declared a foreigner by a Foreigners Tribunal. The HC set aside the opinion and ordered fresh consideration, finding deficiencies in its assessment of evidence including 1965 and 1970 voter-list records of her grandfather, her father's 1977 voter-list record and voter ID, Gaonburah and Gaon Panchayat certificates, a school transfer certificate and land records.She appeared before the tribunal on May 30 with her lawyer, after which police took her into custody. She was taken to Juria and Nagaon Sadar police stations, Matia holding centre in Goalpara, then Eraligool holding centre in Sribhumi (June 4-13).Handed to BSF on June 13, she was sent to Bangladesh on June 14 from Kalaincherra, Cachar, BSF told the HC. Three months on, police, authorities and civil-society members are trying to establish where she is.

World.title: Why is Kejriwal silent on women safety in Punjab: Delhi minister
World.content:
Delhi minister Parvesh Verma hit out at AAP chief Kejriwal for visiting the Tilak Nagar area Monday. "I want to tell Kejriwal that while you visit such sites, young girls are being beaten up in our Punjab.

... so please say a word or two about them as well," Verma said, adding Kejriwal was also silent on the issue of women's safety in Lovely Professional University. He claimed Jarnail Singh's aide Sahib Singh, whom he slapped, was held earlier and is out on bail in a case related to alleged assault and abduction of an MCD worker.

World.title: SC: Cops, government have failed to ensure public safety in Delhi
World.content:
Delhi womenâs safety under SC scanner after âdeeply disturbingâ crimes against girls

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: In view of a "series of deeply disturbing" egregious crimes against girls and women in Delhi, Supreme Court Monday said it was a systemic failure on the part of Delhi govt and police that they can't provide a safe and secure environment to the public, which is their basic fundamental right, and sought an explanation from the authorities.Referring to the gang rape of a 17-year-old girl at Aastha Kunj Park, the gang rape and murder of a girl in Swaroop Nagar, and the sexual assault of a girl inside a moving bus that covered a distance of over 47km from Greater Noida to Delhi, SC said that these have raised serious concerns about the safety and security of public spaces in and around the city, and took suo motu cognisance and registered a case. "The right to live with dignity, free from the fear of violence, is an intrinsic facet of the fundamental guarantee of life and personal liberty enshrined under Article 21 of Constitution," a bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K V Chandran said."Public spaces, including parks, roads, buses, Metro stations, subways, foot bridges, etc, cannot be permitted to become zones of high risk due to grossly inadequate illumination, poor surveillance, lax patrolling, or other preventable administrative deficiencies," it said.

World.title: To recover fines, link traffic challans to power bills: Supreme Court
World.content:
SC seeks new way to recover traffic fines

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Monday asked govt to adopt an innovative approach to make traffic law violaters pay fines and suggested challans should be linked with electricity bill to force them to pay the penalty or face power disconnection.A bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and Justice K V Viswanathan also suggested that authorities should take steps for blacklisting vehicles with unpaid challans and also block ownership transfers."It is not just sufficient to keep issuing e-challans. Police may issue thousands and lakhs of such e-challans. Question is recovery of fines as sought to be imposed by way of the e-challans...If people are not paying traffic challans, add it to their electricity dues bill. They'll have to pay electricity bills, otherwise the power line will be disconnected. Work it out. In this country, you have to find a way out," the bench said.The court was informed that challans of Rs 45,000 crore have been issued but Rs 25,000 crore has been recovered so far.It also suggested random checks of vehicles to identify those against which e-challans remained unpaid.

World.title: Jails are hiring grounds for pro-Khalistan groups; dead drops of ISI modules also under intel lens
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Intelligence agencies have flagged attempts by pro-Khalistan groups, including Sikhs for Justice (SFJ), to infiltrate jails in north India and recruit operatives.

The move comes amid revelations made by a recently detained operative who disclosed having been inducted and given Gurpatwant Singh Pannun's contact while serving time in Patiala jail.

Agencies are now investigating the digital footprint, dead-drop financial channels, and the broader jail recruitment network, sources said. Agencies have also noted how ISI-backed modules are increasingly relying on dead-drop methods to channel funds, supply weapons, and execute covert tasks and have largely replaced physical handovers with pre-designated drop points along isolated highway stretches and border and rural sectors.

Drawn straight from the classic spycraft playbook, this method ensures that foreign masterminds or handlers remain completely insulated from the foot soldiers executing their commands on the ground. Arms, ammunition, and untraceable cash, frequently delivered across the border via drones or covert couriers, are hidden at specific coordinates, with retrieval instructions transmitted to local operatives over end-to-end encrypted messaging platforms like Signal.





The tactic of leveraging prison networks draws from a pattern highlighted by high-profile incidents like the 2016 Nabha jailbreak, which exposed the nexus between terror outfits and incarcerated criminal groups. Within these facilities, handlers and radicalised inmates target vulnerable, economically distressed prisoners - frequently first-time offenders or petty criminals lacking legal representation and financial support.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

In the latest instance, agencies recently busted an SFJ-backed module and arrested operative Preetpal Singh, who, along with his associates, had spray-painted anti-Brics and pro-Khalistan graffiti across Delhi and Punjab, filmed the act and sent the video to Pannun. Singh, it turned out, had a prior history of pro-Khalistan activities, having been arrested in 2023 for a similar crime.

While in prison, he was provided with a phone number to contact Pannun and execute future tasks. After his release in 2026, Singh established direct contact with Pannun and received Rs 1.5 lakh through a dead-drop location on the Faridkot-Amritsar highway. Preetpal subsequently recruited another inmate, also on bail, for the Delhi assignment.

World.title: AAP donations fall 68%, BJD reports zero contributions
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Aam Aadmi Party's receipts from contributions in 2025-26 fell to Rs 12.1 crore, which is less than one-third of its Rs 38.1 crore inflow through this route in 2024-25. Of this, Rs 10 crore, or 83% of its total donations, came from Prudent Electoral Trust and Trident Group founded by Rajya Sabha MP Rajendra Gupta, who switched loyalties from AAP to BJP earlier this year.

AAP is the only party that declares all donation receipts and not just those above Rs 20,000 as required by the law. According to its latest contribution report filed with Election Commission (EC), both Prudent and Trident contributed Rs 5 crore each to AAP; in 2024-25, Prudent had donated Rs 16.4 crore to the party.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Among regional parties, TDP, which is in office in Andhra Pradesh since 2024, declared its donation receipts at Rs 58.3 crore, though this is less than the Rs 83 crore contributions it had reported the previous year.

Prudent contributed over 77% of TDP's total receipts through six donations in 2025-26. In 2024-25 too, Prudent was TDP's biggest donor, having contributed Rs 40 crore in all.

YSR Congress Party, the main opposition party in Andhra Pradesh, received a total of Rs 24.3 crore in donations in 2025-26, though this figure is way less than its Rs 140 crore inflow in 2024-25.

BRS, which was voted out of office by Congress in Telangana in 2023, declared its total contributions in 2025-26 at Rs 16.4 crore, up from Rs 15.1 crore in 2024-25. The 2025-26 contribution report for Biju Janata Dal (BJD), which was defeated in Odisha in 2024, records nil donations, as against Rs 60 crore declared in 2024-25.

Part of AAP's donations in the last fiscal came from its MLAs, including former Delhi CMs Arvind Kejriwal (Rs 30,000) and Atishi Marlena (Rs 42,000).

World.title: High-speed corridors to link UP with North East
World.content:
NEW DELHI: A 630-km corridor connecting Siliguri in West Bengal with Guwahati (Assam) and Shillong (Meghalaya) will be built at a cost of Rs 61,500 crore, announced road transport and highways minister Nitin Gadkari Monday.

The road transport ministry has also taken up an expressway connectivity project from Gorakhpur (UP) to Siliguri.

Once completed, the two corridors will provide high-speed connectivity between Uttar Pradesh and North East.

Speaking at an event, Gadkari added that the 630-km corridor, which will be the "lifeline" of North East, will have the mix of construction of greenfield (new) stretches and upgradation of existing highway connectivity to make the end-to-end travel seamless. He said the first leg of the corridor, Siliguri to Guwahati (400 km), will be built at an investment of Rs 30,000 crore and the project alignment is in approval stage.

World.title: Ancestral home of '62 war hero in Uttarakhand to be made museum
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Rifleman

's inimitable bravery in the battle of Nuranang against the advancing Chinese troops in 1962 is an indelible part of popular lore. A memorial to honour him was built by the Army at the site of his supreme sacrifice in the border region of Arunachal Pradesh.

A biographical movie '72 Hours: Martyr Who Never Died' depicting his remarkable story as a soldier of the 4th battalion of Garhwal Rifles was made too. However, what remained missing was a befitting memorial to the Mahavir Chakra awardee at his ancestral village in Uttarakhand.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

BJP MP Anil Baluni, who represents Garhwal constituency in Lok Sabha, said the late soldier's home at Baryun village of Pauri Garhwal will be developed into a modern museum.

He will perform 'bhoomi pujan' for the project on Nov 17.

While the 'Jaswant Garh War Memorial' in Arunachal Pradesh is a draw for visitors and tourists, a museum at the place of his birth is expected to further cement his legacy in his home state, which sends men to the armed forces in large numbers when compared to its relatively small size.

Baluni said he had met the martyred soldier's family members who consented to the initiative and appreciated the project. Rawat had enlisted in 4th Garhwal Rifles on Aug 19, 1960, at the young age of 19. He was just 21 when he laid down his life on Nov 17, 1962.

World.title: Delhi HC seeks jail authorities’ response on Sharjeel Imam’s plea to access e-record to complete PhD
World.content:
The Delhi High Court on Monday (September 28, 2026) asked the jail authorities to respond to a plea by student activist Sharjeel Imam, who is in custody in a February 2020 northeast Delhi riots case, seeking access to research material stored on a pen drive to complete his PhD.

Justice Sanjeev Narula issued notice to the jail authorities and directed them to file a status report in the matter. The court fixed November 2 for next hearing.

Mr. Imam has sought access to research material on a pen drive using a standalone computer inside the prison premises, without any internet connectivity and under the supervision of Tihar jail staff.

Mr Imam’s counsel said he has been in custody since January 2020 and was in the final year of his PhD at the time of his arrest. His synopsis has been approved by the University Grants Commission (UGC) and Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU), he added.

The special public prosecutor for Delhi Police said the State has not opposed the plea even before the trial court, and only the jail authorities have objected to the pen drive and not to the books before the trial court.

The prosecutor said the pleading could be allowed under the supervision of jail authorities if the accused is ready to show the material he was seeking to access.

Mr. Imam was arrested on August 25, 2020, and booked under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) for being one of the “masterminds” of the February 2020 riots in northeast Delhi that left 53 people dead and more than 700 injured.

World.title: 16-point safety audits in Delhi schools, colleges begin; over 3,000 DU women students march for safer campuses
World.content:
At least 3,000 women students from Delhi University (DU) marched through North Campus on Monday (September 28), demanding safer public and institutional spaces, a week after a 17-year-old girl was allegedly sexually assaulted by three men posing as policemen at Astha Kunj Park.

Students from Miranda House marched to the Faculty of Arts, where they from several colleges gathered before proceeding through North Campus.

This is the second such march organised by women students. Students of Lady Shri Ram College had staged a march on September 23, two days after the incident

All India Students’ Association’s (AISA) DU secretary, Anjali, said the Astha Kunj incident had affected the everyday lives of women on campus.

They also raised concerns over the functioning of Internal Complaints Committees (ICCs) in educational institutions. Ms. Anjali alleged that students had reported incidents of sexual harassment during university events, including the Diwali mela and annual fests, but that the complaints had not resulted in action.

“This march is a culmination of concerns over sexual harassment and the handling of complaints on campus over several years,” she said.

The students demanded functioning ICCs, better street lighting, improved public transport and greater accountability in handling complaints of sexual harassment. They also called for an end to survivor-blaming and moral policing.

They criticised the use of surveillance measures in place of basic safety infrastructure. “Pink booths are put up, but most of the time no one is sitting there,” Ms. Anjali said, alleging that such measures are being used more for surveillance and policing than for ensuring women’s safety.

The students also opposed proposals to restrict access to public spaces after dark, arguing that limiting women’s movement is not a solution to sexual violence.

Safety audits under way

Meanwhile, the Delhi police have begun safety audits of schools, colleges and other educational institutions across the Capital, focusing on physical security and compliance with child protection measures.

One round of the audits began on Friday and continued through the weekend, with the exercise still under way across the city. The audits are being conducted across 16 parameters, including security arrangements at main and other gates, boundary walls and fencing, verification of staff and workers, lighting and dark spots, CCTV coverage, abandoned buildings around institutions, unauthorised vendors selling liquor or tobacco, and safe transport facilities, an official familiar with the exercise told The Hindu.

The exercise is being conducted by gazetted officers, including Assistant Commissioners of Police and officers of higher ranks. Reports from individual institutions will be compiled for further action.

More than 5,000 schools and 30 universities across the Capital are expected to be covered.

As part of the exercise, 192 institutions in the north-west district, 245 in Rohini and 249 in outer north have been audited.

“Some deficiencies were found in the July audits. So, we are following up now on those gaps,” the official said.

A city-wide inspection drive launched in July as part of Child Protection Month had identified safety-related deficiencies in schools across Delhi.

The latest exercise is part of a wider series of safety audits being undertaken by the Delhi police following the Astha Kunj incident. The police are separately auditing parks, while a monthly assessment of dark spots is also being carried out across the city, officials said.

World.title: Trump unveils Essar’s new steel plant in Iowa
World.content:
U.S. President Donald Trump on Monday (September 28, 2026) unveiled Essar Group’s plans to build a massive steel plant in Iowa, at an investment of $15 billion.

Mr. Trump made the announcement in the Oval Office with Essar Group co-founder Ravi Ruia and his son Rewant by his side.

"Today, we're thrilled to announce that Mesabi Metallics will be building the largest steel plant in American history in the great state of Iowa," Mr. Trump said.

Essar Group's Mesabi Metallics chairman, Rewant Ruia, thanked Mr. Trump “for bringing back the importance of building things in America.”

Mesabi Metallics is building the plant with the aim of starting production by 2030, a White House official said.

The facility is expected to produce 10 million tonnes of steel a year and create as many as 1,750 permanent jobs in the state, the official said.

The plant will use iron ore from a new mine that the company invested $2.5 billion to build in Minnesota. The mine will produce about 7.5 million tonnes of iron per year and create about 350 jobs in the state, the White House official said, noting that it will be the first new iron mine in the U.S. in 50 years.

The mine is based in Minnesota’s Mesabi Iron Range, which stretches 80 to 100 miles and contributed about 60 per cent of total iron ore production in the U.S. during the 20th century.

Energy Secretary Chris Wright, Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick; John Jovanovic, chair of the Export-Import Bank; and David Copley, senior director for Global Supply Chain, were among the other people present at the announcement.

“This plant will use the latest technology and will compete head-to-head with any steel plant in the world on size, quality and on cost,” Rewant Ruia said.

World.title: SIR will unite Opposition, says Telangana CM Revanth
World.content:
Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy drew a parallel between the 1928 anti-Simon Commission agitation and the ongoing controversy over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, saying a similar nationwide movement could emerge against the exercise in the coming days.

Addressing a conclave in New Delhi on the theme ‘India’s Next Chapter’, Mr. Revanth said, “Just as the country united under the slogan ‘Simon Go Back’, it will unite under the slogan ‘Sir Go Back’ in the coming days,” adding that leaders, including Mamata Banerjee, Sharad Pawar, Uddhav Thackeray and M.K. Stalin could come together on the issue.

The Chief Minister alleged that decisions relating to electoral rolls were being centralised with the Election Commission and claimed that artificial intelligence was being used in the process.

Attack on Centre over Telangana projects

Mr. Revanth Reddy also accused the Union government of not extending the same cooperation to Telangana that, he said, Prime Minister Narendra Modi received from the then Prime Minister Manmohan Singh when Mr. Modi was Gujarat Chief Minister.

He alleged that files relating to the Regional Ring Road, metro rail expansion and other projects were pending with the Centre. He also alleged that investment opportunities, including a semiconductor project, were being shifted towards Gujarat.

“This is not a north-versus-south issue; it is becoming Gujarat versus the rest of the country,” he said.

On delimitation, Mr. Revanth argued that southern States could lose political representation if Lok Sabha seats were redistributed primarily on the basis of population. He also criticised what he described as the concentration of key Union Government portfolios in northern States and argued that southern States needed adequate political representation.

On welfare schemes, Mr. Revanth Reddy defended the Congress government’s guarantees in Telangana, saying political parties could not ignore welfare when competing with one another. At the same time, he said governments needed to balance welfare expenditure with funds required for development.

World.title: ‘This is not permission’: Delhi Police acknowledges October 2 Jantar Mantar protest intimation; Neha-led delegation says protest will go ahead
World.content:
Three days after the Delhi Police detained protesters attempting to reach Jantar Mantar, a delegation of the All India Students’ Association (AISA), led by its president Neha Bora, on Monday submitted an “intimation letter” at the Parliament Street police station about a proposed protest on October 2 demanding the resignation and arrest of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the electoral process.

The delegation included activist Yogendra Yadav, senior advocate Prashant Bhushan, Rashtriya Janata Dal MP Manoj Jha, social activist Nikhil Dey and educationist Nandita Narain.

“The right of citizens to peacefully assemble and express their views is an important constitutional freedom,” the letter stated, adding, “It is in exercise of this fundamental right that we are intimating you.”

‘Not a permission’

Delhi Police acknowledged receipt of the letter but clarified that this did not amount to permission for the protest. A stamp on the letter read, “This is not a permission. It is only an acknowledgement of your letter.”

The organisers, however, said the protest would go ahead at 11 a.m. on October 2.

“It is up to the Delhi police to facilitate us or to face us,” Ms. Bora said after submitting the letter.

Concerns over SIR

According to the letter, the protest will raise concerns over the “recent functioning and actions” of the Election Commission (EC) and “the actions and decisions of the Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar”.

The organisers have centred their concerns on the special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and its alleged impact on voters. The letter claims that “thirteen crore people have been excluded from the voter roll already” and raises concerns over the manner in which the revision is being undertaken and changes relating to Form 6.

The organisers said the protest intended to seek “accountability, transparency and protection of the electoral rights of citizens”.

The group called upon “all friends of the democratic movement and concerned citizens” to join the protest and asked the police to take necessary steps to facilitate the “peaceful and lawful exercise of our democratic and constitutional rights without unnecessary obstruction or hindrance”.

Bora questions police action

On September 25, more than 50 protesters, including Ms. Bora, Mr. Yadav and Mr. Bhushan, were detained near Jantar Mantar during an AISA-led protest against the SIR exercise and demanding Mr. Kumar’s resignation.

In a video message ahead of Monday’s submission, Ms. Bora questioned the police action against protesters seeking to demonstrate at what she described as a designated protest site.

“First, you steal our right to vote, then we go to protest against this at Jantar Mantar, a designated protest site, and you then steal our right to democratic dissent. This police is denying citizens the right to protest, on the basis of which law and on whose orders?” she said.

World.title: Asian Games 2026 LIVE: Team India faces packed schedule after bagging 8 medals yesterday
World.content:
Team India will be in action across several disciplines on September 29 at the ongoing Asian Games, with medal events in athletics, shooting, cycling, martial arts and other sports set to headline a packed day of competition.

World.title: Over 40 modules of Shahzad Bhatti network busted, 350 held across 15 States: Amit Shah
World.content:
More than 40 modules linked to the Shahzad Bhatti network, allegedly involved in cross-border smuggling of weapons, explosives and narcotics, have been busted and 350 people arrested across 15 States, Union Home Minister Amit Shah said on Monday (September 28, 2026).

Mr. Shah said more than 100 First Information Reports had been registered against members of the network and that the Union Government had declared the Shahzad Bhatti network a terrorist organisation under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA). Bhatti is a Pakistani social media influencer.

Extradition Portal

Mr. Shah launched a new Extradition Portal, which, according to the Home Ministry, is intended to coordinate and expedite efforts to bring fugitives back to India from abroad. He asked State police forces to form dedicated teams that could work with the Central agencies on extradition and other mechanisms for securing the return of fugitives.

He was speaking at the inauguration of a conference on ‘PRAHAAR – Counter Terrorsim Policy and Strategy’ in Delhi. The conference brought together senior officials from the Centre and the States to discuss the government’s counter-terrorism strategy. Union Home Secretary Govind Mohan; Director, Intelligence Bureau, Mahesh Dixit; Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri; heads of Central Armed Police Forces and Central Police Organisations; Directors General of Police of 15 States and Anti-Terrorism Squad chiefs of all States and Union Territories were present. Other State police chiefs and field-level police officers joined virtually.

Improved coordination

Mr. Shah attributed the action against the network to improved coordination between security and investigating agencies. He said the government had adopted a “zero-tolerance” policy against all forms and manifestations of terrorism and called for closer coordination among stakeholders to ensure there was no delay in counter-terrorism operations.

The Home Minister also said 288 fugitive criminals had been brought back to India from 36 countries between 2019 and 2026.

The PRAHAAR strategy rests on seven pillars: Prevention, Response, Aggregating Internal Capacities, Human Rights, Attenuating Conditions for Terrorism, Aligning International Efforts, and Recovery and Resilience.

Mr. Shah called for the strategy to be strengthened through continuous analysis of terror incidents and said a “strong and concrete” mechanism should be developed for the next 10 years.

He also stressed that the principles of PRAHAAR should percolate down to the police station level and asked police forces to take a proactive approach. Counter-terrorism responses should be institutionalised and automated at every level of the security framework.

World.title: BJP accuses Opposition leaders of conspiring to derail India’s progress
World.content:
Senior Bharatiya Janata Party leader and Union Minister J.P. Nadda on Monday (September 28, 2026) accused the Opposition of harbouring a “toolkit mentality” and attempting to derail the country’s progress.

At a press briefing, Mr. Nadda said Opposition leaders, specifically Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi, Aam Aadmi Party chief Arvind Kejriwal, Samajwadi Party’s Akhilesh Yadav, and Trinamool Congress chief Mamata Banerjee, had a “toolkit mentality”.

He accused them of attempting to defame constitutional institutions and derail India’s progress towards a Viksit Bharat. He said, “their political strategy relies on fabricating falsehoods and vitiating the national atmosphere to gain power for dynastic benefits rather than public service, national security, or dignity”.

Mr. Nadda said the BJP, on the other hand, was committed to the welfare of the poorest and the most marginalised persons in society and nation-building. Expressing confidence that the people would continue to see through the “disruptive conspiracies”, he said citizens would “decisively reject” such Opposition leaders.

The BJP leader said that when the country was fulfilling the resolve of a Viksit Bharat through the tireless efforts of 140 crore Indians and India’s achievements were being recognised across the globe, the Congress and its allies were “frustrated and disheartened”.

He said that “all the fabricated allegations made by the Opposition have repeatedly collapsed when tested against facts”.

“Lacking both policy and vision, they are now devising new conspiracies to spread confusion and disorder in the country. A few days ago, a completely fabricated story was used to create turmoil across the nation. Now, when all the members of the Election Commission have exposed each and every one of their false allegations, they have once again begun making fresh attempts to vitiate the atmosphere,” Mr. Nadda alleged.

World.title: Khamenei unbowed as Iran sees no direct talks with US
World.content:
• Supreme leader says US will be forced out of Mideast after ‘painful blows’

• Washington, Tehran set to hold separate talks with mediators

• US officials say Trump would ease sanctions for ‘concrete’ Iranian nuclear steps

• Iraqi Airways resumes flights between Najaf, Iranian airports

TEHRAN: Iran’s supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei vowed on Monday that the United States would be driven out from the region after suffering “painful blows”, as Tehran’s delegation at the UN General Assembly in New York said it had no plans for further talks with Washington.

Khamenei, who has not been seen in public since the start of the Middle East war in late February, made the remarks despite attempts to revive talks aimed at ending the fighting.

“Today, having suffered painful blows at the hands of valiant fighters and the guardians of the Strait of Hormuz, they do not venture beyond the Arabian Sea,” Khamenei said according to a statement carried by state television, without explicitly mentioning the United States.

“Whenever they have braved this risk, they have only brought harm upon themselves. It will not be long before the Arabian Sea, too, would rid itself of their presence.”

In a series of posts on X, Khamenei said that the country’s “enemy” had tried to “erode the social bedrock of the Islamic system”.

“But today, people from all walks of life stand resolutely in defending their righteous positions, including their determination to safeguard the Strait of Hormuz,” he said, adding that for the last seven months, Iranian compatriots had struck fear into the enemy while fighting for Islam.

Diplomacy

Meanwhile, Iran’s delegation in New York for the UN General Assembly is not planning further talks with the United States, the state news agency IRNA reported on Monday.

“Iran’s delegation in New York has no plans for negotiations with the United States,” IRNA quoted an unnamed source close to the delegation as saying. “Iran’s views and positions were conveyed clearly and explicitly to the US side via a Qatari mediator.”

The Iranian delegation will return to Tehran on Tuesday, the news agency added.

Despite the stall in direct engagement, US President Donald Trump is willing to give Iran sanctions relief and release frozen Iranian funds in return for “concrete Iranian steps” regarding its nuclear programme, US officials told the news outlet Axios.

Trump publicly rejected Iran’s latest proposal for ending the war on Saturday but told Axios on Sunday that he expected talks to resume in the coming days.

Trump told reporters in the Oval Office that US officials had talked with mediators trying to end the war, adding that Washington would win “very soon”.

“We’re going to win, as far as I’m concerned, it’s going to be one way or the other,” Trump said. “It’s going to go pretty quickly.” He also said gas prices would come down once the United States wins the war. Trump did not say which mediators US officials had spoken with.

Earlier, an official briefed on the negotiations told Reuters that Qatari mediators were likely to hold talks with Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi in New York and separately with the US side on Monday or Tuesday in a fresh push to end the war.

Iran’s semi-official ISNA news agency later confirmed that Araghchi would meet the Qatari mediators, who are acting as intermediaries between Iran and the United States, on Monday morning.

The two sides will “examine the latest proposals and views regarding the current situation”, ISNA reported. The meeting is expected to focus on messages exchanged with the United States regarding the conditions set by Iran for the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz.

However, the spokesperson for the Iranian foreign ministry, Esmaeil Baqaei, told IRNA that Araghchi’s stay in New York has not been extended for indirect negotiations between Tehran and Washington, noting the minister would proceed according to his previously planned schedule.

Last week’s indirect discussions were held by US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner with Araghchi. The talks are expected to focus on an amended version of a seven-day proposal that Iran presented last week.

As a precondition for ending its blockade on the Strait of Hormuz, Iran’s plan envisages a seven-day cease-fire across the Middle East, including in Lebanon, where its ally Hezbollah has been battling Israeli forces.

It is also demanding the unfreezing of billions of dollars worth of Iranian assets, the lifting of sanctions on its oil sector, and an end to the US naval blockade on Iranian ports. Tehran would then allow the reopening of the strait, and the two sides would resume talks on Iran’s nuclear programme.

Araghchi said on Sunday that mediators had not formally conveyed a US rejection to Tehran and that Iran was awaiting Washington’s definitive position before deciding its next steps.

“Our conditions are clear, and any move toward reopening the Strait of Hormuz is contingent on these conditions being met,” Araghchi said, adding that only a negotiated solution could resolve the impasse.

Najaf-Iran flights resume

In a separate development, Iran has lodged a complaint with the United Nations over US sanctions against its aviation sector that have forced the cancellation of flights, state media reported Monday.

The United States recently imposed restrictions on the entire aviation industry in Iran and vowed to take a hard line against companies that assist it.

“To defend the legitimate rights of the aviation industry and counter illegal restrictions imposed by America, Iran has drafted and submitted a formal protest to the International Civil Aviation Organisation,” civil aviation chief Abouzar Shiroudi told IRNA.

“In cooperation with the foreign ministry, we have also filed a complaint with the International Court of Justice at The Hague,” Shiroudi added.

Amid the aviation restrictions, Iraqi Airways resumed flights between Iraq’s holy city of Najaf and Iranian airports on Monday. Iraq had halted flights to and from Iran on Friday in line with US sanctions.

The resumption comes as the Trump administration was set to grant a limited waiver to its Iran sanctions programme on Monday to allow for flights carrying Shia Muslim religious pilgrims between Iran and Iraq, a person with direct knowledge of the matter said.

The source said the US Treasury Department waiver would allow Iraqi Airways to fly back and forth between Iran and Najaf for one month, with a more permanent waiver potentially following.

Published in Dawn, September 29th, 2026

World.title: India-held Kashmir’s assembly backs return to statehood
World.content:
SRINAGAR: India-held Kashmir’s asse­mbly endorsed the restoration of statehood on Monday, a non-binding resolution that politicians from Pri­me Minister Narendra Modi’s party condemned as “anti-national”.

It is the latest twist in the long-running contentious debate about rule ever since New Delhi revoked held Kashmir’s limited autonomy in 2019.

Omar Abdullah, who heads the occupied state’s government, introduced the resolution, saying that statehood was “our right”.

Members of the Bha­ratiya Janata Party staged a walkout before the vote, with many of them calling the resolution “unconstitutional” and “anti-nati­onal”.

It calls upon the government in New Delhi to ensure “the immediate and urgent restoration of full statehood to Jammu and Kashmir”.

The text also referred to resolutions demanding autonomy, passed in 2000 and 2024.

All three are not constitutionally binding.

Published in Dawn, September 29th, 2026

World.title: Govt notifies new procurement rules with IMF team in town
World.content:
• Changes retain certain exemptions for direct contracting with SOEs despite reservations

• IMF delegation meets finance, tax officials amid uncertainty on sovereign wealth fund law

ISLAMABAD: As question marks linger over the continuous breach of structural benchmarks regarding the sovereign wealth fund (SWF) law, the federal government on Monday notified new procurement rules two days ahead of the deadline, on the first day of talks with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) for disbursement of $1.2 billion.

Sources told Dawn that the IMF staff mission led by Iva Petrova held a series of discussions with officials from the finance ministry, the Federal Board of Revenue, the Establishment Division, and the finance secretaries of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Punjab.

The IMF team has been in Pakistan since September 23. It spent the initial days in Karachi for engagements with the State Bank of Pakistan and other stakeholders. The review talks usually begin with a customary call on the fina­nce minister, but he is currently abroad as part of the PM’s delegation to the UN General Assembly.

The Sovereign Wealth Fund law is part of the discussions with the visiting IMF team. Authorities are in breach of an end-March 2026 structural benchmark on amendments to the Sovereign Wealth Fund Act to adopt governance mechanisms and safeguards for seven state-owned enterprises, involving an asset portfolio of about $8 billion.

Most of them are blue-chip entities listed on the stock exchange but remain outside normal reporting requirements. They include OGDCL, PPL, Mari Petr­oleum, National Bank of Pakistan, Govt Holdings, Pakistan Development Fund, and the Neelum-Jhelum Hydropower project. The amendments are pending parliamentary approval.

New procurement rules

Against this backdrop, the government notified the Public Procurement Rules 2026 to promote greater transparency and competition in public procurement while keeping certain exemptions for direct contracting with SOEs and limiting the bidding to national firms. The IMF had certain reservations over the preferential treatment of SOEs for direct contracting.

Rule 32 of the new rules provide that a procuring agency may engage through EPADS (E-Pak Acquisition and Disposal System, a digital system developed and enforced by the Public Procurement Regulatory Authority) to manage and administer the process of procurement in direct contracting with state-owned entities for the procurement of such works and services, including consultancy ser­vices, which are time-sensitive, scattered, remotely located and in the public interest or in case of urgency and provided they do not sub-let those contracts.

The authorities would also have the powers in specific cases to limit bidding only to national bidders or certain categories of national bidders or prohibit participation of bidders of some nationalities or allow preference to domestic bidders for certain projects, and goods manufactured, mined, extracted and grown in the country.

The Public Proc­urement Regulatory Authority (PPRA) said the new Public Proc­urement Rules 2026 repealed the Public Procurement Rules 2004. Made under Section 26 of the PPRA Ordinance 2002, the new rules have come into immediate effect, with procurement cases initiated prior to the commencement of the new rules continuing under the 2004 framework.

The new rules make the use of EPADS mandatory for public procurement and disposal by federal procuring agencies, provide for the establishment of dedicated procurement cells, and introduce mechanisms to discourage conflicts of interest through third-party validation, evaluation, and pre-shipment inspection for large procurements.

The new rules further strengthen the enforcement mechanism through the provision of blacklisting and cross-debarment, independent grievance red­ressal committees with an appellate mechanism at PPRA to clearly identify material deviations and mis-procurement, including deliberate procurement outside EPADS, failure to constitute prescribed committees, tailor-made specifications, violation of  and response-time requirements, and failure to follow prescribed evaluation criteria.

The rules allow other efficient methods of procurement such as gallop tendering and alternative procurement methods, including shopping and negotiated tendering, subject to specified conditions. Efficiency measures have been embedded in the framework, reducing response times, shortening standstill periods, and streamlining tender processing cycles to enable faster contract awards.

The rules also emphasise sustainable procurement, encouraging inclusiveness of SMEs and marginalised groups, and aligning procurement practices with environmental policy.

PPRA Managing Director Hasnat Ahmed Qureshi said new rules introduce a range of measures to strengthen oversight throughout the procurement cycle, from procurement planning and bidding to contract management, performance evaluation and closure.
